ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Turbomachinery Aerodynamics Engineer, you will own the aerodynamics and design of compressor and turbine stages for Antares nuclear reactors. You will develop turbomachinery from early sizing and architecture trades through detailed aerodynamic design, structural and life analysis, and test validation. You will work closely with rotordynamics, mechanical design, manufacturing, test, and systems engineers throughout development.

The ideal candidate has strong experience designing compressors, turbines, pumps, or similar high-speed turbomachinery and can make sound engineering trade-offs between aerodynamic performance, structural integrity, life, manufacturability, and system requirements.



Roles & Responsibilities:

 - Own the aerodynamic and structural design of compressor and turbine stages.

 - Support architecture trades through meanline analysis, preliminary sizing, and performance modeling.

 - Design blades, vanes, diffusers, volutes, and related flow-path components.

 - Develop and maintain compressor and turbine performance maps and work closely with system engineers responsible for Brayton-cycle performance.

 - Perform stress and life analysis of rotating hardware, including static structural, modal, LCF, HCF, and creep analysis.

 - Evaluate aerodynamic forcing and vane-blade interaction for structural and life assessments.

 - Develop and improve analysis and test methods to correlate aerodynamic, structural, and life predictions with component and rig testing.

 - Investigate performance and structural issues identified during development testing and implement design improvements.

 - Contribute to turbomachinery design practices, analysis tools, and standards for aerodynamic performance, structural integrity, life, and reliability.

 - Support design reviews and technical decisions throughout the product lifecycle.

Basic Qualifications:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or a related engineering discipline.

 - 5+ years of professional experience designing compressors, pumps, and/or turbines.

 - Strong understanding of turbomachinery aerodynamics and aerodynamic design methods.

 - Experience with structural analysis of turbomachinery rotating components.

 - Knowledge of life-limiting mechanisms in high-speed rotating hardware including fatigue, creep, and modal resonance.

 - Experience making engineering tradeoffs involving performance, structural margin, life, manufacturability, cost, and schedule.

 - Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information clearly.

Preferred Skills & Experience:

 - Master’s degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or a related engineering discipline.

 - 7+ years of professional experience designing high-performance turbomachinery.

 - Proficiency with ANSYS Mechanical, CFX, BladeGen, TurboGrid.

 - Experience with meanline and preliminary design tools such as AxSTREAM, PUMPAL, or internally developed sizing and analysis tools.

 - Experience conducting forced-response analysis of vane-blade interactions.

 - Experience validating hardware through test and correlating analytical models with test data.

 - Proficiency with NX for 3D CAD design and drafting.

 - Strong organizational and communication skills.

Additional Requirements:

 - Flexibility to support hardware development milestones, including occasional weekend or long-hour pushes.

Salary Range:

 - Senior, Turbomachinery Engineer - $155,000 - $205,000

 - Staff, Turbomachinery Engineer - $195,000 - $245,000

Leveling is determined during the interviews and can change over time. 



Culture

At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful:

 - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system

 - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle

 - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done”

 - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together

 - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption

Radiation Protection and Radioactive Materials Program Lead

Antares is seeking a Radiation Protection and Radioactive Materials Program Lead to develop, shape, and oversee the programs necessary to protect workers, the public, and the environment during the development, deployment, and operation of advanced microreactors. This individual will also lead the acquisition and maintenance of NRC and state-specific radioactive source or material possession licenses needed to support Antares activities.

The role will establish scalable programs for Army deployments, NRC-licensed commercial deployments, state-regulated activities, and future fleet operations. The program lead will work closely with engineering, nuclear operations, licensing, quality, deployment, security, logistics, and site personnel to translate applicable requirements into practical design features, procedures, controls, records, and compliance evidence. This is primarily an individual-contributor role; line management and field execution will initially reside in supporting organizations.

Responsibilities and Duties

 - Develop, implement, and maintain scalable radiation protection, ALARA, dosimetry, radiological monitoring, contamination control, and radioactive materials programs.

 - Identify applicable federal, state, Army, NRC, DOE, and site-specific requirements and translate them into program, design, operational, training, and documentation requirements.

 - Establish and maintain processes for requirements traceability, compliance evidence, performance monitoring, regulatory reporting, and issue closure.

 - Lead applications, amendments, renewals, reporting, and regulator engagement for NRC and state radioactive source or material possession licenses.

 - Oversee radioactive material receipt, inventory, accountability, use, storage, transfer, transportation, and disposal processes.

 - Establish requirements for sealed source control, leak testing, radiological instrumentation, calibration, maintenance, and records.

 - Develop requirements and governance for radiation worker training, qualification, dosimetry, surveys, postings, access controls, respiratory protection, and radioactive waste management.

 - Integrate radiation protection considerations into reactor and facility design, shielding, maintenance, fuel and material handling, transportation, deployment, and operating strategies.

 - Provide programmatic direction and technical oversight to supporting line organizations, contractors, and site personnel.

 - Evaluate alternative compliance and control approaches and clearly communicate their safety, operational, cost, and schedule tradeoffs.

 - Support radiological emergency planning interfaces and response activities as a subject-matter expert without serving as the program owner.

 - Maintain awareness of regulatory developments, guidance, standards, and operating experience relevant to radiation protection and radioactive materials management.

Required Skills and Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in health physics, nuclear engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.

 - At least 10 years of relevant radiation protection, health physics, radiological control, or radioactive materials program experience.

 - Demonstrated ability to develop or administer radiation protection or radioactive materials programs in a regulated technical environment.

 - Ability to interpret regulations and standards and convert them into implementable, verifiable program and design requirements.

 - Experience establishing requirements tracking, compliance evidence, records, and reporting processes.

 - Strong technical writing, organization, communication, and cross-functional leadership skills.

 - Ability to exercise independent technical judgment and drive actions to closure without relying on direct line authority.

Desired Skills and Qualifications

 - Certified Health Physicist credential.

 - Experience obtaining, amending, or maintaining NRC or Agreement State radioactive materials licenses.

 - Experience in commercial nuclear power, DOE radiological control, national laboratories, advanced reactors, university reactors, Army or defense nuclear activities, or industrial radioactive materials programs.

 - Experience integrating radiation protection requirements into facility or reactor design, operations, maintenance, transportation, and deployment planning.

 - Familiarity with radioactive waste, source accountability, dosimetry, radiological instrumentation, respiratory protection, and material transportation requirements.

 - Experience developing programs intended to scale across multiple sites or operating organizations.

Culture

At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful:

 - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system

 - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle

 - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done”

 - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together

 - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption

About the Role:

At Crusoe, the Capacity Planning & Efficiency team works where all of Crusoe’s products, services and physical infrastructure meet. As the Staff Data Center Planner for Space, Power & Cooling, you will make sure the following requirements are set for every cluster we plan: data hall space, rack positions, power and cooling that are ready when the hardware arrives. You will work across Crusoe Cloud, our AI cloud platform, and Crusoe’s Digital Infrastructure Group (DIG), which develops, builds and powers our data centers, turning hardware demand into the physical capacity it needs.



The role sits between hardware planning and data center design and operations. You will take forecasted and committed deployments (GPU clusters, CPU and storage servers, network cores) and turn them into rack-level space, power and cooling requirements, check them against what each site can support, and flag gaps early enough to fix them. You will own the data and models that show how much usable capacity we have, where it is stranded, and how to get more out of the sites we already run. At the Staff level, you will set the direction for this work across the whole portfolio and be the technical authority leadership relies on for physical capacity decisions. This work directly supports Crusoe’s mission to align the future of computing with environmental sustainability.



What You'll Be Working On:

 - Space, Power & Cooling Fit Checks: Validate that each planned deployment fits its target site and data hall, covering rack positions, kW per rack, air and liquid cooling capacity, and power distribution from utility feed down to the rack. Give a clear go, no-go or at-risk call with the conditions attached.

 - Data Hall & Rack Design Inputs: Work with DIG engineering and design teams on data hall layouts, hot aisle containment and row designs, and network core placement. Confirm cabinet power and cooling assumptions for new platforms (for example, 70kW+ liquid-cooled GPU racks) before designs are locked.

 - Capacity Inventory & Modeling: Build and maintain one view of space, power and cooling capacity by site, data hall and row: designed, built, energized, allocated and in use. Replace manual analysis with models that combine all three.

 - Utilization & Efficiency Metrics: Own metrics such as the Capacity Health Index (actual vs. planned kW relative to actual vs. planned rack units), stranded power and stranded space. Recommend oversubscription, re-layout and consolidation strategies that recover usable capacity.

 - Hardware Refresh & Decommissioning: Assess the space, power and cooling impact of retiring older fleets (for example, A100, L40S and MI300X) and replacing them with new platforms, including timing, reuse of existing infrastructure and the sequence of moves.

 - Cross-Functional Coordination: Act as the main space, power and cooling contact for capacity planning, cloud deployments, networking, DIG operations and supply chain. Make sure the bills of materials passed to networking and deployment teams reflect the final physical plan.

 - Standards & Process: Define planning standards, including rack power classes, density assumptions, design margins and the hand-off between capacity planning and data center design.

 - Strategy & Roadmap: Set the multi-year space, power and cooling planning strategy across the portfolio, including density roadmaps for next-generation platforms. Shape site selection, data hall design standards and build sequencing with DIG leadership.

 - Team Building & Mentorship: Mentor planners and analysts, and help grow the space, power and cooling planning function as Crusoe scales.



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - Data Center Planning Experience: 8+ years in data center capacity planning, space and power planning, or mission-critical facilities engineering at a hyperscaler, colocation provider or large enterprise, including ownership of planning across multiple sites or regions.

 - Power & Cooling Fundamentals: Working knowledge of data center electrical distribution (medium voltage, UPS, PDUs, busway, rack power), cooling systems (air, rear-door heat exchangers, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, CDUs) and redundancy models (N, N+1, 2N).

 - High-Density Compute: Understanding of the physical requirements of AI/GPU infrastructure, including rack density, weight, liquid cooling and network cabling, and how they differ from traditional compute.

 - Analytical & Modeling Skills: Strong spreadsheet skills and comfort with SQL or a business intelligence tool. Able to build capacity models that others trust and reuse.

 - Design Literacy: Able to read data hall layouts, single-line diagrams and mechanical drawings, and turn them into usable capacity numbers.

 - Strong Cross-Functional Navigation: Able to explain physical constraints clearly to hardware, product, Finance and leadership, and to work through tradeoffs with engineering, construction and operations teams.

 - Technical Leadership: A track record of setting direction for a planning function, influencing senior engineering and operations leaders without direct authority, and mentoring other planners.

 - Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Mechanical or Industrial Engineering, or an equivalent technical field.

 - Familiarity with power oversubscription methods and capacity modeling at the cluster or campus level.

We are looking for an RF Engineer to design, build, and test board-level RF receiver circuits and subsystems for our autonomous turret and counter-drone systems, from schematic and layout through lab and field validation. You will focus on receiver topologies, demodulation techniques, and software defined radio (SDR), and develop RF hardware that integrates with our electromechanical and embedded systems and meets military-grade requirements. You will have support from senior engineers and ownership of well-scoped subsystems. This role fits an engineer with about 1–4 years of experience who is ready to take on more design responsibility.

What You’ll Do:

•       Create RF schematics and block diagrams for receiver chains, and select parts.

•       Evaluate and implement receiver topologies (superheterodyne, direct-conversion/zero-IF, low-IF) and trade off sensitivity, selectivity, dynamic range, and image rejection.

•       Develop and test demodulation techniques for analog and digital modulation schemes, including synchronization, carrier and timing recovery, and filtering.

•       Work with software defined radio platforms to prototype, characterize, and validate receive signal chains from RF front-end through ADC to baseband processing.

•       Support RF PCB layout in Altium or similar, covering impedance control, grounding, shielding, and isolation.

•       Run circuit and EM simulations (ADS, SPICE, ANSYS Electronics, or similar) and perform gain, noise figure, linearity, and receiver cascade analysis.

•       Bring up, characterize, and debug boards using VNAs, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and oscilloscopes, in the lab and in the field.

•       Integrate RF hardware with mechanical, embedded, and software teams, ensuring reliability in harsh environments.

•       Document designs, simulations, and test procedures.

•       Support EMI/EMC and environmental testing against military standards.

What You’ll Need:

•       Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field.

•       About 1–4 years of industry, internship, or co-op experience in RF design, test, and troubleshooting.

•       Solid RF fundamentals: transmission lines, impedance matching, S-parameters, noise, linearity, filters.

•       Understanding of receiver topologies and architectures, and of demodulation techniques for common analog and digital modulation schemes.

•       Familiarity with software defined radio concepts, including sampling, ADC/DAC considerations, and digital downconversion.

•       Hands-on use of VNAs, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and oscilloscopes.

•       Working proficiency with schematic and PCB tools (Altium Designer, OrCAD, or similar) and simulation tools (ADS, SPICE, or ANSYS Electronics).

•       Clear written and verbal communication.

You’ll Stand Out:

•       Hands-on SDR experience (USRP, GNU Radio, or similar) or FPGA/DSP implementation of demodulators and receive chains.

•       MATLAB or Python for signal processing, analysis, and test automation.

•       Knowledge of EMI/EMC design and mitigation.

•       Experience testing to military standards.

•       Thermal management knowledge for high-power systems.

•       Familiarity with communication protocols used in robotics systems (CAN, UART, I2C, SPI).

The team supports customers and merchants in their day-to-day use of Alma, handles complex operational situations, and shares frontline feedback to help improve our products and processes. Customer Operations also works closely with teams involved in merchant onboarding, payment operations, risk and fraud management, and debt collection.

As Customer Operations Team Lead, you will manage and develop a team of Customer Operations Specialists in a fast-growing and international environment. You will work closely with Operations Managers and Specialists across countries, as well as with Product, Tech, Risk and other central teams.

You will report to the Customer Operations management team and contribute to the evolution of our organization, processes and ways of working.


💼 ABOUT THE JOB

As Customer Operations Team Lead, you will be at the heart of Alma’s operational engine. You will combine people management, operational expertise and continuous improvement to help your team deliver an excellent experience to our customers and merchants.

Lead and organize the team

 - Organize the team’s activity, prioritize daily workloads and coordinate resources according to business needs and operational priorities.

 - Set clear objectives aligned with the wider Operations OKRs, while helping the team adapt its organization and areas of specialization as Alma grows.

Coach and develop your team

 - Hold regular one-to-ones, provide actionable feedback and create an environment where team members can grow in confidence, autonomy and skills.

 - Support recruitment, onboarding and training, while ensuring that the team has the right tools, knowledge and resources to succeed.

Stay close to customers and operations

 - Remain hands-on by contributing to email and chat support, typically between 10% and 25% of your time depending on the team’s size and business context.

 - Handle complex cases and escalations, support your team with difficult situations, and take ownership of relevant Customer Operations processes.

Drive collaboration and continuous improvement

 - Work with country Operations teams and key stakeholders to communicate new products, features and operational changes.

 - Collect feedback from the frontline, identify improvement opportunities, keep our knowledge base up to date and contribute to better processes, tools and customer experiences.


🧰 YOU WILL WORK WITH

Customer support and chat channels • Internal knowledge base • Operational processes and reporting tools • Collaboration and communication tools • Alma products and payment solutions


🧩 ABOUT YOU

To succeed in this job

 - You have previous experience in Customer Operations, Customer Support or a similar operational environment, ideally with an initial experience in people management or team coordination.

 - You are fluent in both French and English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills.

 - You are empathetic, approachable and able to create a positive, caring and motivating team environment.

 - You are organized, autonomous and resourceful, with the ability to prioritize effectively and find practical solutions in a fast-changing environment.

And it will be nice if you also

 - You have experience in fintech, payments, e-commerce or another technology-driven environment.

 - You have worked in an international or multilingual organization, collaborating with teams across different countries.

 - You have experience improving operational processes, maintaining a knowledge base or using customer support quality metrics.

 - You enjoy combining hands-on operational work with coaching, organization and problem-solving.

Job Description:

We are looking for a strategic operator and exceptional communicator who can design the connective tissue of a complex, matrixed organization. You will own the operational rhythm of the Product leadership team using strategic communication levers, lead high-priority surge projects, and ensure senior leaders are focused on the most critical strategic trade-offs. If you believe a well-designed meeting, a tightly crafted narrative, and a thoughtful offsite agenda can be the difference between organizational drift and organizational momentum, this is the role for you.





Responsibilities:



1. Communications Architecture & Organizational Rhythm

 - Design and own the communications architecture across the Product team (~400 people) — from CPO leadership touchpoints to multi-day offsites, Product Town Halls, Product QBRs, and planned moments of cross-functional alignment. You think about how Slack communication flows through the Product team and other key channels, and how to improve day-to-day communication practices that elevate work and clarify both decisions and progress. You are not simply scheduling meetings; you are engineering the information flow of the organization.

 - Shape the leadership cadence: Ensure the CPO’s leadership team is spending its time on the thorniest, highest-leverage problems. Design leadership team agendas that drive strategic debate and real decision-making, not status reporting.

 - Reimagine how we convene: Rethink Product town halls, Product all-hands, and QBRs to be authentic, engaging, and aligned to the narratives that matter. Establish planned moments of communication — both internal and with partner functions like Sales, Marketing & Public Affairs, and Customer Experience — that build transparency and confidence in the product planning and execution model.

 - Facilitate quarterly ceremonies and cross-functional touchpoints that surface dependencies, progress, and trade-offs across suites and shared services.

 - Manage and develop a junior team member who supports deck development, research, and communications execution. You set clear priorities, coach in real time on the work itself, and create stretch opportunities that grow their capabilities and extend the reach of the function.
   
   

2. Strategic Leverage & Executive Voice

 - Executive communications: Draft internal memos, leadership-facing decks, and department-wide communications that ensure a consistent, motivating narrative from Product leadership.

 - Narrative synthesis: Translate complex product, operational, and pedagogical updates into clear, high-level executive summaries for company leadership and cross-functional partners. Establish and communicate the narratives that align product development with broader company objectives, with a focus on operational excellence in delivery.

 - Information cascading: Ensure strategic decisions from leadership flow to teams without losing context, and that ground-level insights flow up to inform strategy. You act as the connective tissue between the top of the house and the people doing the work.



3. Special Projects & Surge Capacity

 - Lead cross-cutting initiatives that are complex, high-priority, and don’t have another natural home — the projects that fall between functional lines and would otherwise stall. You drive them to completion.



4. Culture Carrier & Organizational Health

 - Serve as a “temperature taker” for the Product function: You have a finger on the pulse of team morale, energy, and engagement across the Product organization. You proactively surface what people are feeling — not just what they’re delivering — and translate those signals into actionable recommendations for leadership.

 - Take action on employee engagement: You analyze quarterly pulse check employee engagement data and EOY engagement data, identifying with product leadership the highest-priority improvement areas and building recommendations for how to improve and how you’ll measure improvement function-wide.

 - Be a culture carrier: Model and reinforce the behaviors and norms that define how Product works at its best. Whether through the tone of a town hall, the design of an offsite, or a one-on-one conversation with a frustrated team lead, you shape the lived experience of the organization.

 - Build trust across the org: Serve as a trusted, neutral point of contact for other departments and for teams across Product who need a place to raise concerns, flag friction, or simply be heard. You create the conditions where people feel seen and where cross-functional decision-making moves faster because relationships are strong.



Who You Are…

 - A Nimble Thinker: You can digest a 50-page research paper and turn it into a 5-slide strategy deck by morning. You move fluidly between the strategic and the tactical.

 - A “Low Ego” Leader: You are equally comfortable presenting to the ELT as you are rolling up your sleeves to fix a spreadsheet or coordinate logistics for a 200-person offsite.

 - An Expert Navigator: You know how to build influence across a matrixed organization to get things done without formal authority. You are the person people turn to when something is stuck.

 - An Operational Strategist: You find deep satisfaction in a perfectly run meeting and a clear, actionable project plan. You see operational design as a form of leadership, not overhead.

 - A Champion and Unifier: You are an internal force that straddles multiple product lines, grade levels, and functions — representing the broader Product organization in cross-functional forums and ensuring alignment across product development initiatives.

 - A Gifted Communicator: You write with precision, present with clarity, and design communications experiences that leave people better informed and more aligned than they were before.
   
   

Basic Qualifications:

 - 8–10+ years of experience in a high-growth environment plus 5 years of increasing managerial experience (Strategy, Operations, Chief of Staff, Program Management, or Management Consulting), ideally in technology, education, media, or another content-driven business.

 - Proven experience designing organizational operating rhythms — you have built the meeting cadences, planning cycles, and communication architectures that keep complex organizations aligned.

 - Exceptional deck and narrative skills: You are the person leaders turn to when the story needs to land. You can build a board deck, an all-hands presentation, or a strategic memo with equal fluency.

 - Experience operating in a matrixed, cross-functional environment where influence without authority is the primary leadership currency.

 - People management experience: demonstrated ability to directly manage and develop a team member, with a track record of coaching early-career talent and accelerating their growth.

 - K–12 or education context preferred — familiarity with curriculum development, the school adoption cycle, or the general complexity of the American education system is a meaningful advantage.

 - Educational foundation: Undergraduate degree required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

Job Description:

We are looking for a process design leader who can architect a lightweight, collaboratively-built operating playbook for a complex Product organization. The bar is high in two directions at once: enough rigor to stop the patterns that erode delivery today, and enough restraint to avoid smothering the people doing the work with overhead. You will own and standardize the core processes that govern how Product plans, builds, and ships — but you will design them with business unit partners, not for them. You will also continuously scan the organization to spot where new process infrastructure is needed (and equally, where existing process should be retired or simplified).



The right person for this role has spent a career proving that great process is a force multiplier — not bureaucracy — and has the instinct to feel the line between too much process and too little, and to stay on the right side of it.



Responsibilities:



1. Planning & Roadmapping

Co-design and steward the cross-functional planning calendar for the Product organization — coordinating annual planning cycles, aligned artifacts, delivery expectations, and planned moments of alignment with Sales and GTM. The calendar that actually gets used is the one the people running it helped shape; you build it with Suite Leads, the Resource Allocation team, and GTM partners — not in a vacuum.

 - Resolve the misalignment that exists today — inconsistent work planning methodologies across suites, mismatched planning timeframes (platform, digital product, and suites all on different cadences), lack of backward planning for cross-team dependencies, and rolling release cycles out of sync with the school year — by introducing the lightest framework that genuinely solves the problem.

 - Maintain dynamic business unit and cross-product roadmaps and ensure alignment across all other planning functions, building shared visibility into where the portfolio is headed and how dependencies fit together.



2. End-to-End Launch Planning & Related Processes

 - Design the standardized end-to-end launch process across business units — including launch readiness checklists, health checks, cross-stakeholder touchpoints, release documentation, and clean flow of data from product to supply chain.

 - Co-develop the launch playbook with Go-To-Market, Sales, Customer Experience, Marketing, and Supply Chain — building it with the functions executing against it, not imposing it on them. The teams who run launches today have hard-won knowledge; your job is to surface and codify it, not overwrite it.

 - Codify ready-to-launch protocols that ensure pricing is finalized, manufacturing and distribution are confirmed, market collateral is approved, and Sales and CX teams are fully enabled — every time, regardless of which suite is launching, and without adding meaningful overhead to the teams doing the work.



3. Stage Gates & Decision Frameworks

 - Steward and continuously evolve the five-gate stage gate process that the organization is currently rolling out — including the differentiated tracks (e.g., new programs, new markets, in-market management) so that gating is right-sized to the investment and not a one-size-fits-all forcing function.

 - Co-develop refinements with suite leaders and stage gate sponsors as pilots (Science V2, CA K-8 Literacy, and others) generate real-world learnings. The gate process should feel like it belongs to the people running it, not like compliance imposed from outside the suite.

 - Manage gate review orchestration — scheduling, materials, decision documentation, and tracking — so decisions made in stage gate meetings actually stick. You stop the “decisions get unmade” pattern that has dogged the org, without turning gate prep into a second job for the teams.

 - Own scope change management — the process for evaluating and approving changes after a gate has been passed — so the organization can respond to legitimate new information without descending into the “culture of yes” that erodes delivery.

 - Partner with Finance & Analytics to link funding and resourcing decisions to gate readiness, helping deliver against the 2026 KPI that 60% of 2027 R&D spend is vetted through stage gates or an independent strategic framework.



4. Spot Gaps and Build Lightweight, Co-Developed Process

 - Identify new areas where process infrastructure is needed: you scan the organization continuously — listening to Suite Leads, project managers, and shared services about where work is breaking down — and you triage where new process is genuinely the answer (versus better tools, clearer ownership, or simply leaving things alone).

 - Build process that earns its keep: your default is the lightest possible framework that solves the problem at hand. You instinctively distinguish between rigor that protects delivery and overhead that drains it, and you reach for the former without slipping into the latter.

 - Retire and simplify as actively as you create. When a process isn’t working, you change it; when a process isn’t needed, you retire it. You see the absence of a framework as a hypothesis to test, not a mandate to fill.

 - Build and lead the central team that designs, iterates on, and supports critical processes and associated tools and templates — while making sure business units have what they need to execute consistently.

 - Establish a continuous improvement loop — instrumenting the processes you own, learning from pilots, and iterating quickly based on what you (and the people doing the work) observe in the field.



Who You Are…

 - A Lightweight-First Process Designer: Your instinct is always toward the lightest framework that solves the problem. You see overhead as a tax on delivery, and you have the judgment to know when more process is the answer and when it isn’t. You can feel the line between too much and too little process — and you stay on the right side of it.

 - A Co-Creator, Not an Imposer: You build process with the people who will live with it. You start every engagement with deep listening — to suite leaders, PMs, designers, content leads — and you ship frameworks that feel like extensions of how teams already work, not corrections imposed from above.

 - A Gap-Spotter: You actively scan the organization for places where process infrastructure could unlock impact — and equally for places where existing process should be simplified or retired. You triage thoughtfully: not every gap needs a framework, and not every framework is worth keeping.

 - An Operator’s Operator: You have run real launches, real planning cycles, and real stage gates — and you bring that experiential credibility to every conversation with suite leaders. You know what overhead feels like from the receiving end, which is why you’re so careful not to create more of it.

 - A Continuous Improver: You see every pilot as a learning opportunity, every miss as a signal, and every win as a stepping stone. You instrument your work and let the data — and the people doing the work — guide refinement.

 - An Expert Navigator: You know how to build influence across a matrixed organization to get things done without formal authority. You are the person leaders trust to make a fair call when process and urgency are in tension.



Basic Qualifications:

 - 8+ years of progressive experience in business operations, program management, process design, or product operations leadership — ideally in technology, education, media, publishing, or another product- and content-driven business.

 - Demonstrated track record of building lightweight, well-adopted process: frameworks that teams actually use rather than binders that gather dust. Bonus points if you can point to a process you deliberately simplified or retired.

 - Proven experience designing and rolling out core operating processes at scale — stage gates, planning cadences, launch readiness frameworks, scope change governance, or analogous frameworks in complex, multi-product organizations.

 - Strong bias toward partnership and co-creation: you have designed and rolled out processes by listening first, prototyping with operators, and iterating publicly. You don’t ship V1 from a corner office.

 - Track record of leading cross-functional product launches end-to-end — including the GTM, Sales, CX, Marketing, and Supply Chain coordination that turn a “ready to ship” product into a successful one in market.

 - People management experience — you have built and led teams of process designers, program managers, or business operators, and you’ve grown talent in those roles.

 - Comfort with both strategy and execution — you can articulate the “why” of a new process to senior leadership and the “how” to the program manager building the template.

 - K–12 or education context preferred — familiarity with curriculum development, the school adoption cycle, or the general complexity of the American education system is a meaningful advantage.

 - Execute continuous monitoring: ACAS and Nessus vulnerability scanning, SCAP and STIG compliance checking, audit log review, and remediation tracking against CAT I, II, and III findings

We're hiring a Senior Technical Account Manager who has already done this job at a SaaS company: someone who has led complex implementations and owned enterprise relationships for the long haul, and who builds with AI rather than just using it.

 

TAMs at ClickUp are the long-term technical and strategic partner for a portfolio of enterprise customers. This isn't a relationship-only CSM role, and it's not an implementation role where you get buried in requests and lose the account strategy. You'll discover the business problem, build and implement the right solution, drive adoption, and prove the business impact, staying with your customers from first rollout through renewal and expansion, turning delivered value into a credible growth story.

 

What you'll do

 

Own your customers for the long term

 - Be the strategic and technical owner of a portfolio of enterprise accounts, from first rollout through renewal and expansion.

 - Build and grow champions across admins, operators, and executive stakeholders.

 - Monitor adoption, account health, and stakeholder engagement; spot risk early and build recovery or acceleration plans.

 - Run executive business reviews with a clear point of view on delivered business value, progress, opportunities, and priorities.

 - Drive renewal strategy with your account team and bring the commercial instincts to spot expansion signals and turn outcomes into strong value stories.

 

Design and deliver the solution

 - Lead discovery that maps current-state vs. future-state workflows (Intake → Execution → Reporting).

 - Lead complex implementations end to end: governance, architecture, process design, and rollout across multiple teams or business units.

 - Recover momentum when projects stall, priorities shift, or stakeholder alignment breaks down.

 - Know when to standardize, when to keep flexibility, and how to balance technical ambition with customer readiness.

 

Build with AI

 - Design, build, and scale ClickUp AI agents, automations, and workflows tied to real customer KPIs.

 - Advise customers on prompt design, agent architecture, and scaling AI use cases across teams.

 - Track AI usage and consumption against plan, and turn usage insight into new opportunities.

 

Drive adoption and change

 - Make adoption your mandate, not a milestone. Pair every solution with a structured enablement and change management plan so new ways of working actually take hold across teams rather than stopping with the project sponsor.

 - Define success measures and adoption milestones with your stakeholders before go-live, track them relentlessly, and course-correct early when usage signals turn negative.

 - Build a culture of adoption inside your accounts: champion networks, internal advocates, and team-level habits that keep ClickUp and AI central to how they work, not a tool they drift away from.

 - Treat low adoption as a commercial signal: a customer who isn't using the product is a customer who won't renew. Intervene before it becomes a renewal conversation.

 

Partner across ClickUp

 - Be the voice of the customer for Product, Engineering, Sales, and Support.

 - Keep ownership even when multiple teams are involved.

 

What we're looking for

 

Required

 - 5+ years in a customer-facing, post-sale SaaS role (Technical Account Management, Professional Services, Implementation, Solutions Consulting, or similar).

 - Direct experience leading enterprise SaaS implementations end to end, with multiple stakeholders.

 - A track record of owning long-term enterprise customer relationships and building champions.

 - Demonstrated experience building and deploying AI-powered workflows, agents, or automations in a business context.

 - Executive presence: confident with both hands-on operators and C-level stakeholders.

 - Strong judgment in ambiguity; you simplify complexity and keep momentum through change.

 

Preferred

 - Hands-on experience with ClickUp, Asana, Monday.com http://Monday.com, Smartsheet, Wrike, Jira, or a comparable work-management platform.

 - Hands-on experience with agentic tools such as Claude, n8n, Make, Zapier, or LangChain.

 - Technical aptitude with integrations, APIs, automation logic, and data modeling.

 - Experience carrying a renewal or expansion number (GRR, NRR).

 

What sets you apart

 - You've built something with AI that a team actually runs on, and you can walk us through how it works.

 - You think in workflows and systems, not just relationships.

 - You've run enterprise implementations and know change management firsthand.

 - You stay with customers long after go-live, and they want you there.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Docker Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) embed directly with our most strategic customers to solve important, complex technical problems and turn ambitious ideas into production outcomes. FDEs take on the most challenging technical problems using existing Docker products and patterns when possible, and work across customer, Docker Product and Engineering teams to realize new approaches when required.



The Sr. Principal FDE is a rare, deeply specialized role at the frontier of the practice, whose expertise shapes Docker's long-term direction. You are accountable for outcomes that are strategic, cross-functional, and often company-defining: the customer relationships, technical patterns, and product capabilities that determine how the world's largest organizations adopt agentic AI on Docker. You work as a trusted advisor and partner to executive leadership, both at Docker and at our most strategic customers, and you are recognized internally and externally as a leader in the field.



You take on the most consequential customer challenges, often with no established playbook, and own the technical journey from discovery and architecture through production rollout. More importantly, you turn what you learn into an advantage: reference architectures, engagement standards, product direction, and the next generation of FDE leaders. You work with broad latitude and the work you do shapes Docker products and services.

_______________________________________________________________________




RESPONSIBILITIES


LEAD DOCKER'S MOST STRATEGIC CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENTS

 - Serve as the technical lead on Docker's most strategic and highest-stakes customer engagements, from first prototype through stable production rollout, often across multiple customers and workstreams at once. Use existing Docker products and patterns when possible; invent, prototype and validate new approaches when necessary.

 - Deliver working technical artifacts that set the bar for the practice: custom MCP servers with tightly integrated Docker Sandbox environments for coding agents and containerized agents; Docker Compose definitions for multi-agent harnesses and model-backed applications; Hardened Image standardization and migration at enterprise scale; and new tools that unblock customer progress.

 - Integrate Docker's AI platform with the customer's existing stack, including identity providers (OIDC/SAML/SSO), secrets management, private and air-gapped registries, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, and observability tooling.

 - Own technical delivery on your engagements and set the delivery standard for others: scope the work, sequence it, make trade-offs between speed and quality, remove blockers early, and contribute directly to code whenever progress depends on it.

 - Act as a trusted technical advisor to customer CTOs, CISOs, and senior engineering leaders, aligning them on architecture, risk, and adoption strategy.


MAKE AI ADOPTION SAFE AND GOVERNABLE

 - Translate customer security, compliance, and platform requirements into concrete plans and see them through from ideation to production.

 - Define the reference frameworks and controls that let customers adopt agentic AI to solve their unique business problems without compromising security, compliance, data sovereignty, or end-user experience.

 - Set the standard for when AI-generated outputs and agent actions require scrutiny, validation, or human override, building rigor and accountability into how customers and Docker approach agentic workloads.

 - Partner with customer security and platform leadership to get agentic workloads through architecture review, threat modeling, and change control.

 - Establish quality and performance standards with customers, and work with Docker Product and Engineering to resolve issues that fall outside established thresholds.


PARTNER WITH SOLUTIONS ARCHITECTURE AND THE FIELD

 - Work with Solutions Architects to enable off-the-shelf solutions when possible, and provide technical leadership when a bespoke solution is necessary.

 - Turn implementation learnings into reference architectures, SOW templates, and success patterns, so that FDE innovations become standard features and repeatable implementation patterns across the field.

 - Support the field with technical depth during proofs of concept, escalations, and expansion conversations, and help shape strategic account plans when a working build is the fastest path to adoption.


SHAPE PRODUCT DIRECTION WITH PRODUCT AND ENGINEERING

 - Work as part of Docker Engineering to fold FDE innovations, learnings, and design patterns into existing and new products and services.

 - Be the voice of the customer at the executive level. Deliver data-driven, actionable evidence on what works, what does not, what customers are asking for, and what blocks their adoption, and use it to influence roadmap priorities and Docker's investment decisions.

 - Advise Docker leadership on market direction, competitive dynamics, and where agentic AI adoption is heading, based on what you see in the field.


SHAPE THE PRACTICE

 - Define the FDE engagement model, delivery standards, and quality bar, and codify them so engagements are consistent across customers, regions, and delivery partners.

 - Develop Principal and Senior FDEs into the next generation of FDE leaders, and shape hiring bar, leveling, and onboarding for the practice.

 - Act as the senior-most technical escalation point for the hardest customer problems. Treat every incident as an opportunity to improve Docker products and services.

 - Establish frameworks and approaches that other teams adopt, and build organizational capability to take on new and evolving challenges.

 - Operate at the frontier of the agentic AI stack: LLMs, APIs, MCP, coding agents, model and harness evaluation, performance and quality thresholds, and deployment patterns. Shape how Docker, and where relevant the broader industry, understands and responds to AI-driven shifts.

 - Represent Docker externally as a recognized expert, through customer executive forums, conferences, open source, and published work.

 - Participate in the team's paid on-call rotation

_______________________________________________________________________




QUALIFICATIONS


REQUIRED

 - 12+ years of software engineering experience, including 6+ years in a customer-facing technical role such as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Professional Services Engineer, or Software Engineer with consulting or technical founder experience.

 - A track record of strategic technical leadership across multiple engagements, teams, and domains, including setting delivery standards, defining repeatable patterns that others adopt, and influencing product direction and company investment through field evidence.

 - Recognized as a leading practitioner in forward deployed engineering, developer platforms, or enterprise AI adoption, internally and, where relevant, externally.

 - Expert production coding skills in Go, Python, or TypeScript, with a track record of shipping and operating software that other people depend on and of leading technical design reviews.

 - Deep, hands-on Docker expertise: Dockerfiles and multi-stage builds, Docker Compose, image and registry operations, container networking and storage, and container security.

 - Hands-on experience building with LLMs and agents in production, including tool use and function calling, the Model Context Protocol (MCP server and client implementation), prompt and context engineering, and evaluation of agent behavior, plus a current, informed view of how AI is reshaping software development.

 - Deep knowledge of software supply chain security: SBOMs, image signing and attestation, vulnerability management, minimal and hardened base images, and secure CI/CD.

 - Experience designing and integrating with enterprise systems at scale: identity providers (Okta, Entra ID, LDAP/Active Directory), federated identity protocols (OIDC, SAML), secrets managers, Kubernetes, and at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, GCP).

 - Proven ability to scope and deliver company-defining work in highly ambiguous, fast-moving environments, with sound judgment on trade-offs, risk, and the limits of AI-generated output.

 - Credibility with executives: communicates with precision in senior forums, aligns stakeholders on high-stakes topics, and leads through influence rather than authority, with a low-ego, collaborative approach.

 - Proven record of developing leaders, not only contributors: engineers you mentored have gone on to lead teams or practices of their own.

 - High agency and comfort operating with the highest degree of autonomy in a distributed, remote-first company.

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Travel to customer sites to build in person with customer teams, estimated at up to 50%.


BONUS QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with Docker Hardened Images, Docker Scout, MCP Gateway, MCP Toolkit, Docker Sandboxes, or Docker Model Runner.

 - Experience deploying and operating coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or similar) in team or enterprise settings.

 - Experience with air-gapped, regulated, or compliance-driven environments in financial services, healthcare, government, or similar sectors.

 - Contributions to open source projects in the container, Kubernetes, or MCP ecosystems.

 - Experience founding or scaling a Forward Deployed Engineering or Professional Services practice.

 - External visibility in the field: conference talks, published writing, or standards and community leadership.

SUMMARY



You'll be the deepest technical voice in our sales cycle — the person who can sit with an engineering team, read their stack, and build a working Dust integration before the meeting is over. This role goes well beyond demos: you'll write code, design integration architectures, navigate enterprise security and compliance reviews, and own technically complex POCs with large enterprise and engineering-led accounts. You'll also help shape the SE function itself — building internal tooling and playbooks, mentoring more junior SEs, and feeding direct technical insight into our product roadmap.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO




LEAD ENGINEERING-LEVEL TECHNICAL EVALUATIONS

 - Partner with Account Executives as the primary technical voice for enterprise and engineering-led accounts — the person who earns trust in a room full of engineers and DSIs

 - Run architecture deep-dives, API walkthroughs, and live integration builds with customer engineering teams — not just polished slides

 - Own the technical evaluation end-to-end: scoping, custom environment setup, POC design, success criteria definition, security review support, and close




BUILD — ACTUALLY BUILD

 - Build pragmatic API integrations to customer systems, independently or in collaboration with customer engineering teams, and unblock evaluations without needing to escalate to Dust engineering

 - Build and maintain Dust4Dust internal tooling — agents, workflows, and automations that make the SE team operate at a higher level




NAVIGATE ENTERPRISE COMPLEXITY

 - Lead security reviews, IT governance discussions, and compliance conversations (GDPR, data sovereignty, SOC2) with CIOs and IT teams — the things that stall deals if no one owns them

 - Articulate Dust’s differentiation in relation to other agentic platforms as well as in contrast to deterministic automation tools (such as Make, Zapier, n8n).

 - Help define the enterprise pilot playbook: repeatable evaluation frameworks, security approval templates, and integration patterns that scale




RAISE THE BAR ACROSS THE TEAM

 - Act as the primary feedback loop to Product and Engineering — translate technical friction from customer conversations into structured, actionable roadmap input

 - Mentor and onboard more junior SEs; help establish the craft bar the function will be measured against

 - Contribute to the SE knowledge base: technical documentation, reusable demo assets, and integration playbooks

 


REQUIREMENTS

Every candidate and employee's success is measured against the same 3 dimensions. Aptitude, Attitude and Agency.




APTITUDE

 - Strong hands-on coding ability: you write Python, TypeScript, or Bash, call APIs directly, and have shipped real integrations — with concrete projects to show, not side projects

 - Deep understanding of integration architecture: APIs, webhooks, data connectors, authentication patterns — you can design and explain this to an engineering team independently

 - Fluency in LLM/AI architecture: RAG pipelines, prompt engineering, agent orchestration, data connectors — you can go deep with ML engineers and data teams without needing backup

 - Experience navigating enterprise security reviews: GDPR, data sovereignty, SOC2, IT governance — you understand the questions and know how to answer them

 - Ability to adapt technical depth for any audience — from C-level to DevOps lead — without dumbing down or losing the engineering teams




ATTITUDE

 - Builder mindset: you don't wait for a playbook — you write it, then make sure others can use it

 - Low ego, high standards: you give direct feedback, receive it without defensiveness, and make the engineers and AEs around you sharper

 - Customer-centric at depth: genuine curiosity about how engineering teams are built and operated, not just the business problem on the surface

 - GenAI-native: you use AI tools as a force multiplier in your own workflow — not as a novelty, but as how you work

 - Mentorship instinct: as an L4+, you actively invest in the growth of more junior SEs — through code reviews, deal coaching, and knowledge sharing




AGENCY

 - Technical self-sufficiency: when you hit a wall, you debug it yourself first — then bring back what you learned to improve how the team operates

 - Proactive infrastructure builder: you see gaps in how the SE team operates and build tools or systems to fix them without being asked

 - End-to-end deal ownership: from the first technical call to security approval and POC close, you own the outcome — not just your stage

 - Roadmap influence: you don't just flag product gaps — you validate them across customers, assess priority, and bring structured proposals to Product and Engineering

 - Scope expansion mindset: you define your role by outcomes, not job description — and consistently find problems to solve that no one assigned you

 


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

 - Engineer the systems behind one of the world's largest compute buildouts. Everything runs as code, version-controlled and reproducible, so a new hire, team, or site spins up in minutes instead of days.  - Solve multi-tenancy problems most IT engineers never touch. Fluidstack runs teams, sites, and customers in parallel, and the internal systems have to keep them cleanly separated and secure at speed. You'll own architecture problems usually reserved for product infrastructure, on the inside.

 - Give every employee the speed it takes to reach 10s of GW. The faster the company's people move, the faster we get to 10s of GW. You'll own the internal systems and support that keep a 10x workforce unblocked.


ROLE SCOPE

 - Own corporate IT end to end: identity, endpoint fleet, SaaS estate, and employee support for a workforce that grew 10x in the last year.

 - Stand up IT at each new data center site as it comes online, and keep a growing multi-state fleet of live sites supported while construction continues around them.

 - Build and lead the IT organization: hire engineers ahead of demand, direct contractors, and own delivery on a scope that outpaces headcount.

 - Run internal systems as code: version-controlled, reproducible, and automated so provisioning a new hire, a new team, or a new site takes hours, not weeks.

 - Partner with Security on the identity, access, and endpoint controls that hold up to audits from the most demanding customers in AI.

ABOUT GENESIS

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.




THE ROLE

You will own Robot safety end to end - from hardware and controls to the learned models that drive mobile manipulation around people. You will define what our robots are allowed to do, build the evidence that lets us prove it, lead certification with international regulators, and build the team that keeps the safety bar as the fleet scales.

This is a key leadership role on the safety side of Genesis. You will work directly with our co-founders, with the hardware, AI research and deployment teams, and with external certification bodies and customers. You will set the precedent for how general-purpose robots driven by learned autonomy are brought to market safely - at Genesis, and for the industry.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the robot safety case. Define where, how, and around whom our robots can operate. Decide what evidence we need to ship, and lead the construction of the technical documentation that supports it across jurisdictions.

 - Design the safety architecture with hardware, controls and AI teams. Define the envelope the model is allowed to command motion within, and the independent, deterministic layer that limits motion or stops the robot when the model steps outside it. Make sure model updates cannot change safety parameters.

 - Validate the safety of learned behavior in simulation and on real robots. Design and lead safety evaluations across Genesis World and physical testing. Probe failure modes, recovery behaviors, and unfamiliar conditions that could lead to safety hazards. Define safety acceptance metrics independently of task performance and set revalidation criteria for model updates.

 - Lead certification with test labs and notified bodies. Own the regulations approaches across different markets (EU, US, etc). Build and maintain the relationships with the Notified Bodies that will assess us.

 - Lead safety acceptance at customer sites. Work with customer EHS teams to validate Eno against site-specific safety criteria. Translate safety-related incidents, near misses, and safety limit violations into regression tests, risk mitigation measures, and updated operating limits.

 - Build and lead the safety team. Hire system safety, software safety and compliance engineers. Lead go/no-go reviews for releases and deployments. Set the standard that the rest of the company builds against.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Led system safety or functional safety for a physical product from hazard analysis through release, certification, and field deployment. Robotics, autonomous vehicles, aerospace, or industrial machinery backgrounds are all strong fits.

 - Hands-on experience specifying and verifying safety functions in hardware and controls, grounded in the most relevant certifications and standards.

 - Experience evaluating learned or probabilistic behavior in physical systems, and translating results into operating limits, release criteria, and safety arguments that regulators and customers can accept.

 - A track record of building and leading teams, and making hard safety calls across engineering, product, and operations without slowing the mission.

 - Strong written and verbal communication. You can explain a safety architecture to a Notified Body, a plant manager, a journalist, and a founder with equal clarity.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Direct experience with end-to-end robot policies or vision-language-action models for mobile manipulation.

 - Experience leading a certification programme under a regulated market.

 - Experience bringing a safety-critical product to market at a startup pace, with the discipline of an incumbent.

 - Familiarity with assurance cases, structured safety arguments (e.g. Goal Structuring Notation), and modern approaches to safety for learned systems.

We believe conversations will become the #1 way to shop.

At Gorgias, we’re building the platform that makes this real: a unified AI agent that sells, supports, and re-engages customers across the entire journey. Conversational Commerce is the future of ecommerce, and we’re leading that shift.

Our mission is to turn every interaction between a brand and its customers into a relationship: personal, seamless, and intelligent. By combining deep product expertise with the latest in AI, we’re making shopping feel more natural, human, and connected than ever before.

To win, we focus relentlessly on:

 - Quality: conversations that feel authentic and on-brand.

 - Experience: effortless shopping from chat to checkout.

 - Re-engagement: personal, 1-1 dialogue instead of noisy marketing.

The opportunity is massive. As AI reshapes how people buy, Gorgias is building the foundation for the next decade of ecommerce, where every brand has its own intelligent agent and every customer feels understood.

Join us to make Conversational Commerce real.




ABOUT THE TEAM

Demand Generation builds Gorgias's pipeline engine across SMB, Commercial, and Enterprise. Growth & Demand Generation owns acquisition strategy, creative experimentation, and pipeline; GTM Engineering builds the AI agents, data pipelines, and automations that turn winning experiments into systems that scale. Together we're building an AI-native demand generation engine where a good idea quickly becomes an automated, measurable, repeatable play.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll own demand generation across paid advertising, outbound, and ABM, with one goal: qualified pipeline across SMB, Commercial, and Enterprise. You'll design acquisition strategies, prototype campaigns with AI tools, and work with GTM Engineers to turn what works into automated growth systems. A strong fit finds unconventional ways to grow, experiments with AI by default, and measures success by pipeline generated and systems built, not campaigns launched.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Targeting and scoring: Define ICPs, account segmentation, and account scoring models that combine fit, estimated opportunity value, buying signals, and engagement.

 - Account intelligence: Choose the first- and third-party data sources, enrichment, and account-mapping approach to find decision-makers, champions, and buying committees.

 - Signal-based plays: Build GTM plays triggered by events such as executive hires, company growth, technology adoption, or changes in customer behavior.

 - Paid advertising: Run creative strategy on LinkedIn, Google, and other channels; test audiences, positioning, messaging, and formats; use AI to generate ad variations and spot optimizations; and optimize spend on qualified pipeline, not clicks or lead volume.

 - Outbound: Design personalized outbound from account intelligence and intent signals, set the business logic and quality bar for AI agents that research prospects and write outreach, and test targeting, messaging, and timing to lift replies, meetings, and pipeline.

 - ABM: Build account- and industry-specific programs for high-value Commercial and Enterprise accounts that combine ads, outbound, and events, with messaging for each persona in the buying committee. Partner with Sales on target accounts and coordinated outreach.

 - Experimentation: Generate hypotheses, prototype campaigns and workflows with AI and no-code tools, run structured experiments, and analyze results all the way to pipeline outcomes.

 - AI-native workflows: Find repetitive work to automate, define the requirements, decision rules, and success criteria for AI growth plays, and decide where agents act on their own and where a human reviews.

 - Scale with GTM Engineering: Hand winning experiments to GTM Engineers and build reusable workflows together for enrichment, scoring, activation, personalization, and optimization, with feedback loops from campaign and sales outcomes.

 - Pipeline ownership: Own demand generation results across segments. Track the funnel from account identification to qualified opportunity, channel efficiency, conversion rates, and pipeline quality, and align priorities with Sales, Marketing, and RevOps.

 - Example projects: an AI-powered account prioritization engine, an AI-native advertising engine where agents optimize within guardrails, signal-based outbound campaigns, a repeatable Enterprise ABM playbook, and a demand generation engine that improves from its own pipeline data.




WHO YOU ARE

 - 3–5 years in demand generation, growth marketing, performance marketing, or ABM, ideally at a fast-growing B2B SaaS company.

 - AI-native: you already use AI tools in your work and want to use AI agents to change how campaigns are designed, run, and optimized.

 - Commercially driven: you think in qualified pipeline, conversion rates, and revenue, not vanity metrics.

 - Creative and resourceful: you find unconventional ways to reach customers and challenge standard marketing playbooks.

 - Hands-on builder: you prototype, launch, and prove something works before scaling it.

 - Strong analytical skills: comfortable with data, experiment design, and turning metrics into decisions.

 - Solid grasp of paid advertising, outbound, and ABM, and how they work together to create pipeline.

 - You know how to define ICPs, segment audiences, read buying signals, and write messaging for specific personas.

 - Systems thinker: you turn successful experiments into repeatable processes.

 - Technically curious: you translate business problems into clear requirements for engineers. Deep software engineering expertise is not required.

 - Excellent communicator and copywriter, with both business and technical stakeholders.

 - High ownership and bias for action, comfortable in ambiguity.

 - Nice to have: prototyping marketing workflows with ChatGPT, Claude, or Clay; HubSpot or similar marketing automation, CRM, and enrichment tools; running ABM or personalized outbound at scale; SQL, no-code automation, or basic scripting; working with GTM Engineering, Marketing Ops, or RevOps.

The Role

The Casting Team delivers castings to Hadrian's downstream manufacturing processes. As a Casting Product Engineer, you will develop and define sand casting processes, tooling, and fixturing that meet customer metallurgical and dimensional requirements. You will work on the production floor with the Operations team and own casting quality, yield, and cost results from development through production.

What You'll Do

 - Develop and deliver castings that meet metallurgical and dimensional requirements for Hadrian's downstream processes.

 - Coordinate the design, purchase, and validation of custom sand casting tooling, fixtures, and gauges.

 - Define dimensional inspection plans and first article layouts using CMM and structured light scanning to meet AS9100 requirements.

 - Lead continuous improvement projects that lower scrap rates, improve yield, and reduce production costs.

 - Work with Hadrian teams to document unwritten casting process knowledge in Hadrian's operating system.

Basic Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials, or Metallurgical Engineering, or Materials Science, or 10 years of equivalent casting engineering experience.

 - 5+ years of experience producing sand, investment, or die castings in a production environment.

 - Experience leading at least one tooling or casting process development project from start to completion.

 - Experience working within an AS9100 or ISO 9001 Quality Management System, including first article inspection.

 - Experience applying statistical analysis and at least one structured problem-solving method (e.g., 8D, RCCA, DMAIC) in a casting environment.

 - Experience applying GD&T to castings and using CMM or structured light metrology.

 - [Must be a U.S. person as defined by ITAR (22 CFR §120.62), or eligible to obtain the required export authorization. See note below.]

Preferred Qualifications

 - Casting experience for maritime, aerospace, defense, or space applications.

 - Master's degree in a technical field.

 - Six Sigma Green/Black Belt or AFS coursework/certification.

 - Experience with NAVSEA quality requirements and processes.

 - Experience with government contracts and MIL standard requirements.

 - Experience with Teamcenter, NX, Oracle/NetSuite, Jira, and [foundry manufacturing data systems / specific software name].

 - Experience with Zeiss Inspect and/or PolyWorks.

The Role

The Casting Team delivers sand castings to Hadrian's downstream processes that meet metallurgical and dimensional requirements. As a Casting Engineer – Process Control, you will own the Key Process Variables (KPVs) that keep the sand, molding, and pouring operations in statistical control.

This role needs sand casting knowledge, a data-driven approach, and hands-on work with Operations on the foundry floor. Casting Engineers work closely with the Product Engineering focus area and may rotate between focus areas as the team grows.

What You'll Do

 - Apply sand casting process knowledge to develop and deliver castings to Hadrian's downstream processes that meet metallurgical and dimensional requirements.

 - Lead continuous improvement work that lowers scrap rates, improves yield, and reduces production costs, using root-cause analysis of casting defects.

 - Partner with Operations, Metallurgy, Quality, and Machining to trace casting defects to their root causes and close the loop.

 - Document tacit process knowledge in Hadrian's operating system.

 - Define, monitor, and control KPVs for the sand system, molding, and casting operations, and set the control limits and reaction plans that keep them in statistical control.

 - Own the sand system and molding process. Track and adjust sand properties (compactability, moisture, green/compression and shear strength, permeability, AFS grain fineness, LOI, active/MB clay, friability) and bond additions to keep the system in spec.

 - Build and maintain SPC, capability studies (Cp/Cpk), and process dashboards that catch drift early and drive data-based corrective action.

 - Plan and run DOEs to optimize sand, molding, and pouring parameters.

 - Tie casting defects (gas, sand inclusions, penetration, scabs, shrink, dimensional variation) back to upstream sand and molding KPVs.

Basic Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Materials Science, Metallurgy, or a related technical field, or 10 years of equivalent foundry engineering experience.

 - 5+ years of engineering experience in a production sand foundry (green sand or chemically bonded/no-bake).

 - Experience interpreting sand lab data and making process adjustments based on it.

 - Experience applying SPC and at least one structured problem-solving method (e.g., 8D, 5-Why, DMAIC).

 - Experience with process data collection, capability analysis (Cp/Cpk), and DOE.

 - Experience working within an AS9100 or ISO 9001 Quality Management System.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience producing castings for maritime, aerospace, defense, or space applications.

 - Master's degree in a technical field.

 - AFS coursework or certification, or Six Sigma Green/Black Belt.

 - Experience with NAVSEA quality requirements, government contracts, and MIL standards.

 - Experience with solidification simulation software (e.g., MAGMA, ProCAST, FLOW-3D CAST).

 - Experience with Minitab or JMP.

 - Experience with Oracle/NetSuite, Jira, and foundry manufacturing data systems.

 - A track record of carrying improvement projects from start to completion.

YOU HAVE

 - Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, including with senior customers

 - High ownership mindset with pride in end-to-end accountability
