ABOUT THE ROLE

Every major step in crypto has unlocked something new. Bitcoin made it possible to send money. Ethereum made money programmable. Solana made programmable money scale. But all of it is still public, and a financial system can't run on a ledger where every balance and transaction is visible to everyone. Privacy is the last big unsolved problem.



Helius' Privacy team is building programmable privacy that scales, natively on Solana. Others have tried to solve this by building entirely new blockchains and bootstrapping developer ecosystems from scratch. We're building where developers already are, on infrastructure that scales with Solana.



At the core is a permissionless default privacy ring. Alongside it are custom rings for partners who need their own deployments. Custom rings hold large amounts of encrypted user data, so the infrastructure behind them has to be secure by design. Our security bar here is higher than anywhere else at Helius.



As a Sr. Backend Engineer, you'll build and own that infrastructure: Rust and Go services, Kubernetes, AWS with Nitro Enclaves and trusted execution environments, and infrastructure-as-code. Part of the job is DevOps. If something can be automated, it should be. Some details of how custom rings will work are still taking shape, so you'll help define the system as much as build it.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and run the backend services behind our privacy infrastructure, mostly in Rust and Go

 - Stand up the infrastructure for custom rings, including how we store and protect encrypted user data

 - Design systems on AWS Nitro Enclaves and handle the hard parts: attestation, key management, and keeping workloads isolated

 - Manage our infrastructure as code and make provisioning and deploys predictable

 - Run services on Kubernetes and keep them reliable as usage grows

 - Automate CI/CD, provisioning, and anything else the team keeps doing by hand

 - Think about security from the start, from threat models to access controls to what an auditor would ask

 - Work with our cryptography and protocol engineers to get zero-knowledge proofs running in production

 - Write design docs and help decide what custom rings should look like

 - Review code, mentor engineers, and set the standard for how the team builds
   




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 8+ years of backend engineering experience, with staff-level scope: you've owned the design and operation of critical systems end to end

 - Strong production Rust experience, plus working proficiency in Go

 - Experience running services on Kubernetes in production

 - Deep AWS experience and hands-on infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform)

 - Security depth: you've built systems that handle sensitive data, and you understand encryption, key management, and access control in practice

 - A DevOps mindset: you'd rather automate a process than document it

 - Solid distributed systems fundamentals and experience building for scale

 - High ownership and comfort operating with autonomy while the problem space is still being defined

 - Clear written communication. We're remote and async-heavy, and your design docs need to stand on their own.



NICE TO HAVE

 - Zero-knowledge proof experience, whether that's proving systems, circuits, or shipping ZK in production

 - Experience with trusted execution environments (Nitro Enclaves, Intel SGX/TDX, or similar)

 - Other privacy tech like MPC or FHE

 - Crypto experience, especially on Solana

 - Based in or able to work Pacific hours




WHY HELIUS?

 - High-impact work: Help build programmable privacy on Solana from the ground up, with the distribution of a company that thousands of teams already build on, including Coinbase, Jupiter, and Phantom

 - Serious engineering: Work on hard problems in security, trusted execution, and zero-knowledge proofs, in systems that have to scale with Solana

 - Ownership & growth: Lead critical initiatives, influence architecture and product direction, and take on more responsibility as the company scales

 - Remote-first flexibility: Work where you're most effective with a flexible, fully distributed team

 - Mission-driven team: Join ambitious builders who move fast, take ownership, and are working on the piece crypto still needs before the financial system can move on-chain: privacy

Helius runs its global edge network and high-performance services directly on bare metal. This role joins our Platform team to make that fleet faster to provision, safer to access, cheaper to run, and boring to deploy to.

 

You'll work across the foundation everything else at Helius depends on: automating how servers get spun up and configured, standardizing how software gets built and shipped to machines, and executing on our engineering security roadmap. This is an intermediate role with a lot of room to grow. We care more about ownership, intensity, and learning speed than about a perfect match on today's stack.

 

No crypto background is needed. If you've run serious infrastructure anywhere, we'll teach you the blockchain parts.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Automate the server lifecycle end to end: provisioning, OS installs, configuration, hardware validation, and decommissioning

 - Write clear runbooks and docs so the rest of a remote team can operate what you build

 - Hands-on bare metal experience, such as provisioning and managing physical servers (PXE, IPMI/BMC, RAID, NICs), working with colo or dedicated-server providers, and debugging hardware versus software issues

 - Deep Linux fundamentals, including systemd, networking, storage, and performance tuning

 - Experience with configuration management and infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Ansible, Terraform, Salt, Nix)

 - Solid scripting or programming ability in Python, Go, Bash, or similar

 - A security mindset: you think about access, blast radius, and secrets by default, not as an afterthought



NICE TO HAVE

Hinge Health’s events bring these leaders together around evidence, practical insights, and new ideas to help them improve health outcomes, expand access to care, and reduce costs. As Event Content Lead, you will shape what these audiences learn and take away, turning our expertise and the experiences of customers, partners, and industry leaders into ideas they can act on.



You will work closely with executives, customers, partners, and subject-matter experts to turn complex healthcare topics into clear, engaging, audience-relevant presentations. AI is part of the operating model for this role. You will use AI-powered tools to synthesize research, structure and draft content, pressure-test messaging, revise materials, and accelerate iteration while applying human judgment and maintaining accuracy and confidentiality.



For assigned events, you will own the event narrative strategy, including audience framing, objectives, themes, story arc, key messages, and content recommendations. You will own content development from research and narrative through slide-level content, wireframes, scripts, speaker coaching, rehearsals, run-of-show content, and day-of content coordination, then partner with Commercial Creative on final visual design. As the content show runner for Hinge Health-owned events, you will be accountable for content flow, speaker readiness, transitions, cues, and last-mile content changes. IN YOUR FIRST 6 MONTHS

Hi 👋 I’m Nitesh, Engineering Manager at hyperexponential. I'm one of the career mentors in the Product Foundations stream. We tackle the fundamental problems every product team at hx runs into, so the vertical streams can focus on building features for customers. Right now that means deployments, observability, security, AI observability tooling and a permission service that other value streams will build on.

I’m hiring a Senior Security Engineer to join us as our second security hire. The foundations are already in place. We’ve chosen and implemented our tooling, and our repositories and cloud environments are onboarded. The next step is shaping how security actually works here. This won’t be a traditional, hierarchical security function. Our engineers go straight to the person who owns an issue and ask them to fix it, and you’ll help define what security looks like in that model.

There’s no established playbook for this yet, which is what makes it exciting. If that sounds like your kind of challenge, I’d love to hear from you.




ABOUT HYPEREXPONENTIAL (HX)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.




ABOUT THE SECURITY FUNCTION

The Security function's mission is to safeguard the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of our customers' data and hx's systems. By fostering a culture of vigilance, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement, we maintain the highest standards of security excellence.

Security at hx underpins every product and every customer interaction. As we scale our multi-product platform globally and adopt AI across the business, the team ensures that innovation and growth are matched with rigorous security practices. We design controls, shape culture, and guide decisions that protect our business, our customers, and the wider industry.

As a Senior Security Engineer, you’ll be the second engineer in our security team, working directly alongside our Staff Security Engineer. The foundations are in place, with our core tooling chosen, rolled out and onboarded across our repositories and cloud environments. Much of how security works at hx is still to be built, though, so you’ll have real autonomy to shape it, with a direct line to the teams who own the issues you find. You’ll strengthen hx’s security posture by driving continuous improvement across our technical teams: owning security reviews, running and extending our security tooling, and turning findings into fixes, often by writing the code or making the infrastructure change yourself. You’ll champion security initiatives across the organisation, help teams adopt AI securely, and use AI to multiply your own impact. This role combines hands-on technical depth, ownership and influence to make security a practical part of how our teams work every day.

Check out our Engineering Candidate Hub https://www.hyperexponential.com/careers/hubs/engineering for a behind the scenes look at the team you would be joining!




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Modify, maintain, and extend our security tooling across engineering and IT environments, including CSPM, SAST, SCA, and secret scanning, ensuring it's reliable, well tuned, and genuinely useful to the teams who depend on it.

 - Use our tooling and your own judgement to proactively identify gaps across cloud security, dependencies, secrets, and code. Work with the owning teams (starting with 2 to 3 where the gaps are greatest) to secure their commitment to prioritise remediation, and see it through.

 - Write code and make infrastructure changes yourself to fix security issues and improve our tooling, rather than just recommending improvements.

 - Own security reviews end to end, partnering with engineering teams on new designs, significant changes, and new tools, and working through follow-up questions and challenges until each review is resolved.

 - Take ownership of and complete a medium-sized security project within your first three months.

 - Partner with our IT team on security best practice, helping implement practical improvements in authentication, authorisation, and security hygiene across our corporate environment.

 - Guide teams across the business on adopting AI securely, from assessing new AI tools and use cases to mitigating risks like data leakage and prompt injection, while using AI yourself to increase your impact.

 - Support our compliance programmes, such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2, by helping teams implement and evidence technical controls.

 - Act as a trusted voice for our technical teams, owning security issues raised with them through to resolution and handling the related correspondence.




WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO HAVE DONE

 - Secured AWS cloud environments hands-on: using Cloud Security tooling to find common weaknesses, and fixing them yourself through infrastructure and code changes. Cloud Security experience is required.

 - Secured containerised workloads and infrastructure-as-code, catching issues before they reach production.

 - Experience working with SAST, SCA, and secret scanning tools, including triaging findings, filtering out false positives, and partnering with engineering teams to get real fixes shipped

 - Supported compliance efforts such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, or GDPR by implementing and evidencing technical controls.

 - Used AI to improve your own security work and helped others adopt it safely, with a practical understanding of AI-specific risks such as data leakage, prompt injection, and agents and integrations with excessive permissions.

 - Spotted and addressed non-technical risks, such as weak processes, risky behaviours, and gaps between teams, that can undermine technical security.

 - Discussed security in depth with engineering teams, explaining complex concepts clearly and concisely and influencing teams through to implementation.

 - Taken ownership of security projects and initiatives and driven them to completion independently.




HOW WE BUILD IN AN AI-FORWARD COMPANY

hx is a maximally AI-forward company because we believe AI should amplify what exceptional people can achieve. Everyone here is a builder. That means staying close to what’s changing, continuing to learn, and using AI to raise the quality, pace and ambition of your work.

We expect everyone to actively experiment with AI and agentic systems, whether at work or in their personal lives. This means going beyond prompting, exploring what agents can do autonomously, and learning by doing. You don't need to be an engineer, but you do need to be curious, hands-on and willing to push what's possible.

Your current environment is context, not the answer. We’re interested in how you think about what should be possible now, not simply how things are done where you work today. We care about judgement, creativity and ownership, not simply using more tools.

The bar is simple: your work should be meaningfully better because of how you operate in this new world.

If reading our Culture Document https://hx.wiki leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

About the Institute of Foundation Models The Institute of Foundation Models is a research lab at Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) dedicated to building, understanding, and responsibly deploying foundation models. Our researchers and engineers work across model training, evaluation, and systems. We share our work through publications, technical reports, and open-source releases, and help train the next generation of AI researchers and builders.

The Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) team studies how foundation models can contribute to training and evaluating their successors. A model might construct a coding task, write a verifier, or use execution feedback to revise a solution. The research question is whether those contributions improve the next model’s ability to solve unfamiliar problems, and whether that model can, in turn, produce better training tasks and feedback.

As a Research Scientist, you will shape this research agenda and lead projects from an initial hypothesis through large-scale experiments. You will design learning algorithms, build environments that provide meaningful feedback, and study how gains and errors accumulate over successive training rounds. The role combines independent research with hands-on engineering across data generation, post-training, and evaluation.

  • Develop algorithms for recursive self-improvement. Design and test methods for models to propose tasks, attempt solutions, learn from feedback, and select experiences for subsequent training rounds.

  • Build tasks and environments with verifiable outcomes. Develop agentic tasks in domains such as coding, program analysis, and tool use. Design execution-based verifiers and investigate what happens when a verifier accepts an incorrect solution or rejects a valid one.

  • Study how to select training data as models improve. Investigate which tasks produce the greatest learning gains at each stage of training and how to maintain coverage as earlier tasks become easier.

  • Measure improvement across generations. Design held-out evaluations, ablations, and compute-matched baselines that isolate the contribution of model-generated tasks and feedback. Diagnose failure modes such as reward hacking, declining task diversity, and errors that compound across rounds.

  • Scale promising methods. Work with research engineers to integrate generation, verification, and training into distributed post-training systems. Quantify the trade-offs among model capability, feedback quality, and computational cost.

  • Communicate and share research. Publish findings, contribute reproducible code and evaluations for public release, and build collaborations within MBZUAI and across the research community.

    • MSc, MEng, or PhD in machine learning, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent research experience.

ABOUT KASTLE

Kastle is building the AI employee for banks. We help financial institutions scale their contact center and compliance operations with autonomous AI agents that process payments, originate loans, and guide customers through some of the biggest financial decisions of their lives.

We’ve processed over $2 billion in transactions, raised a $24M Series A, and are backed by Insight Partners and Y Combinator.

We’re building AI for environments where precision, reliability, and performance matter. Our mission is to redefine how the critical industries powering America operate.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As Kastle’s Founding Enterprise Sales Engineer, you’ll own how we demonstrate, architect, and prove the value of our platform to financial institutions.

You’ll work directly with the founders and Account Executives to win our most strategic customers. From the first discovery call through technical evaluation and close, you’ll understand how a prospect operates, identify where AI can make the biggest difference, and build demonstrations that make that opportunity tangible.

Our customers need to understand how an agent will connect to their systems, follow their policies, handle exceptions, and serve their borrowers. You’ll turn those questions into a clear solution and a credible path to production.

As our founding hire in this function, you’ll also build the foundation for sales engineering at Kastle: our demo environments, technical discovery process, and standards for bringing engineering into a deal. What you learn in customer conversations will directly influence what we build next.

This role is for someone who loves building, understands how to win enterprise deals, and wants to help create a function from the ground up.



RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the technical sale. Partner with founders and Account Executives from discovery through close, identifying technical requirements, addressing objections, and helping prospects make confident buying decisions.

 - Go deep into customer workflows. Understand borrower journeys, operational bottlenecks, existing systems, and compliance requirements. Identify the strongest initial use cases and define measurable success criteria.

 - Build demos that win deals. Configure AI agents and create tailored demonstrations around a prospect’s workflows, policies, and customer experience.

 - Lead technical evaluations. Scope and run proofs of concept, coordinate resources, troubleshoot issues, and demonstrate results against agreed success criteria.

 - Architect the solution. Map integrations with loan servicing systems, APIs, data sources, and telephony platforms. Identify dependencies and constraints early.

 - Build trust across the buying team. Work directly with executives and engineering, security, compliance, and operations teams to address their questions and requirements.

 - Set deployments up for success. Partner with Forward Deployed Engineers and Product Managers to transfer customer context, agreed scope, architecture, and commitments into implementation.

 - Build the sales engineering foundation. Create reusable demo environments, integration prototypes, technical collateral, and evaluation playbooks. Help define how the function grows.

 - Shape the product. Bring customer needs and competitive insights directly to the engineering team, helping distinguish immediate deal requirements from broader product opportunities.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years of relevant experience in sales engineering, solutions engineering, or a technical role working directly with enterprise customers.

 - Experience owning technical discovery, custom demonstrations, and evaluations within complex enterprise sales cycles.

 - Strong technical fundamentals. You can work with APIs, understand authentication and data flows, and write Python, JavaScript, or similar code to build prototypes and integrations.

 - Clear communication across audiences, from engineers reviewing an architecture to executives evaluating a business case.

 - Commercial judgment. You know which technical questions matter to a buying decision and how to focus your effort on resolving them.

 - High agency and attention to detail. You can take an ambiguous customer problem, structure an approach, and drive it forward with limited guidance.

 - A builder’s mindset. You’re excited to create the tools, processes, and standards that future hires will use.

 - Curiosity about how businesses operate and a willingness to learn banking and lending workflows in depth.


ESPECIALLY RELEVANT EXPERIENCE

 - Building or selling conversational AI, voice agents, contact center software, or workflow automation.

 - Navigating enterprise security reviews and integration requirements.

 - Joining an early sales engineering team or building a customer-facing technical function.


WHY JOIN KASTLE

 - Build a foundational function. Define how Kastle demonstrates its product, runs technical evaluations, and wins enterprise customers.

 - Work directly with the founders. Have a short path from customer insight to product and company decisions.

 - Own consequential work. Help financial institutions adopt AI in workflows that affect millions of customers.

 - Grow with the company. Help shape the team, hiring standards, and operating approach as sales engineering scales.

 - Great team: work side by side with a world-class team product and GTM teams that will reshape the trajectory of your career

 - Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.

Camper Support Director, Early High School Camp

The role consists of two appointments: a part-time Camper Support Planning Director position during the academic year and a seasonal Camper Support Director position during the summer. Together, these responsibilities cover preparation, staff development, camper well-being, family communication, and on-site health coordination.

Planning Director responsibilities (January through camp start):

  • Review and provide feedback on policies and procedures concerning camper wellness, behavioral expectations, and family communication.

  • Evaluate counselor training materials related to student well-being, social dynamics, and challenging behaviors.

  • Participate in pre-camp leadership meetings to establish incident-response protocols, communication channels, escalation procedures, and staff training plans.

  • Interview candidates for Associate Camper Support Director and camp nurse positions and contribute to hiring decisions.

  • Review relevant student records, prepare confidential notes for residential and academic staff, and follow up with families when additional information is needed.

  • Participate in the camp leadership retreat, if possible, scheduled for a weekend in February or March 2027.

    • Seasonal Camper Support Director responsibilities:

    Staff Support and Training

  • Supervise, train, and provide day-to-day direction and performance feedback to the Associate Camper Support Director and camp nurse.

  • Train and guide counselors and faculty on supporting gifted and twice-exceptional students, including their emotional, social, and behavioral needs.

  • Prepare staff to address issues specific to high school students, such as relationships and physical boundaries, identity, mental health, disordered eating, academic pressure, perfectionism, and phone and social media use.

  • Observe classes and provide in-person classroom support when needed.

  • Advise staff managing challenging behavioral situations and serve as an escalation point when issues exceed their experience or responsibilities.

  • Train staff on behavioral management procedures and lead incident follow-up, response, and documentation.

    • Camper Support and Advocacy

  • Collaborate with the Camp Director and counselors to foster an inclusive environment that encourages friendships, engagement, and positive interactions in academic and recreational settings.

  • Provide individualized support to campers experiencing homesickness, anxiety, social difficulties, or other emotional and behavioral challenges.

  • Help high school students adapt to greater independence while maintaining appropriate camp rules and boundaries.

  • Recognize signs of serious mental health concerns, including depression, self-harm, and disordered eating, and respond according to established protocols.

  • Coordinate with camp leadership, nursing staff, families, and external professionals when additional support or intervention is required.

  • Mediate conflicts and bullying situations, helping students and staff resolve issues constructively.

  • Participate in the on-call rotation during designated hours and coordinate with the Camp Director to ensure continuous coverage while campers are on site.

    • Parent Communication

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for parents throughout the camp session.

  • Proactively communicate updates about campers' experiences, progress, and any challenges that arise.

  • Respond to parent inquiries and coordinate with relevant staff to address concerns and resolve issues.

  • Manage the biweekly camp blog to keep families informed about activities and daily camp life.

  • Print and distribute parent emails as needed.

    • Proactive Engagement and Health Management

  • Regularly visit classrooms, activities, and residential areas to build relationships with campers and monitor their well-being.

  • Act as the on-site point of contact for camp nurses, ensuring effective communication between healthcare staff and the leadership team.

  • Coordinate with Camp Medical Services on health concerns and potential escalations, ensuring staff understand when and how to involve the service.

  • Oversee camper medication administration as directed by licensed nursing staff when the nurse is unavailable and support basic first aid within the scope of camp protocols.

  • Coordinate further medical assistance when necessary, including arranging transportation to urgent care.

  • Monitor general camper and staff health and escalate potential public health concerns appropriately.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate will bring relevant experience in education, psychology, social work, or a related discipline, alongside a strong understanding of adolescent development and the needs of academically advanced students. They should be compassionate, proactive, and confident handling sensitive situations while building trusting relationships with students, families, and colleagues.

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in education, psychology, social work, or a related field; a focus on social-emotional learning is strongly preferred.

  • Experience working with gifted and twice-exceptional (2e) students.

  • Strong understanding of the social and emotional needs of early high school students, particularly those who are academically advanced or have unique learning profiles.

  • Experience supervising groups of students in residential or overnight environments, such as summer camps, boarding schools, or multi-day school trips.

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build rapport and trust with students, staff, and families.

  • Ability to remain calm and effective in high-pressure situations, supported by strong problem-solving, conflict-resolution, and decision-making skills.

  • A compassionate, flexible, and proactive approach to student support and advocacy.

  • Current CPR and First Aid certification, or willingness to complete the required certification before arriving at camp.

  • Authorization to work in the United States.

  • Willingness to commit to at least two summers, covering 2027 and 2028.

    • Benefits:

  • Summer 2027 seasonal appointment: $9,744 stipend for approximately five weeks on site, including four weeks of camp.

  • Future summer appointments: The anticipated stipend will be $8,500 for Summer 2028 and beyond.

  • Academic-year planning appointment: $40 per hour, with approximately 100–125 hours of work during the academic year.

  • Accommodation and meals: Room and board provided during the summer appointment.

  • Travel: Travel expenses provided for the seasonal on-site commitment.

  • Retirement plan: Camp leadership team members are eligible for a 401(k) plan with a 4% employer match.

  • Dependent tuition discount: Children and dependents of camp staff receive a 20% discount on tuition at camp programs.

  • Long-term opportunity: The position offers the possibility of continued involvement in the camp community beyond the initial two-summer commitment.

As Care Center HR Operations Director, you will oversee the HR function supporting owned and operated healthcare practices while ensuring alignment with broader organizational priorities. You will establish scalable processes, support acquisitions, strengthen compliance, and provide strategic guidance to HR leaders and clinic management teams. Your responsibilities will include:

  • HR Operations Leadership: Lead the development, implementation, and ongoing management of the Care Center HR function, establishing effective business processes, policies, and employee support mechanisms while leveraging national HR centers of excellence.

  • Acquisition Due Diligence: Serve as the primary HR contact for Business Development during practice acquisitions, evaluating workforce-related financial models, including labor expenses, employee training requirements, and compliance costs.

  • HR Integration and Onboarding: Manage HR onboarding and integration processes for newly acquired practices and large-scale clinical acquisitions, ensuring smooth transitions and consistent employee experiences.

  • Process Optimization: Guide HR leaders in identifying and addressing best-practice gaps, improving operational efficiency, standardizing policies, and harmonizing vendors and HR processes across locations.

  • HR Audits and Compliance: Oversee HR-related audits for incoming practices and ensure consistent adherence to applicable employment regulations and organizational policies.

  • HR Team Leadership: Provide functional leadership and guidance to HR professionals supporting independent practices, including direct supervision and matrix-based management where appropriate.

  • Service Delivery Management: Regularly assess HR service delivery, ensuring high levels of internal customer satisfaction, operational effectiveness, and regulatory compliance.

  • Clinic Workforce Management: Oversee Office Managers within owned and operated practices, supporting the execution of day-to-day HR responsibilities and acting as a strategic partner for workforce planning and organizational change management.

  • Compensation and Benefits: Collaborate on compensation strategies to maintain competitive and equitable pay structures, provide guidance on incentive programs, and oversee benefits administration for employed clinical groups.

  • Healthcare Compliance: Ensure compliance with healthcare-related HR requirements, including HIPAA, OSHA, FLSA, and FMLA, across all locations employing clinical professionals. Maintain accurate employee records and documentation to minimize organizational risk.

  • Performance and People Management: Coach clinic leaders on effective employee management and lead teams through Career Committee activities, performance reviews, and related talent management processes.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Sales and Recruiting teams to develop and expand HR service offerings for existing and prospective healthcare practices.

  • Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to strengthen HR programs, improve the employee experience, and support the organization's continued expansion.

  • Additional Responsibilities: Perform other duties and projects as assigned by leadership.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate is an experienced HR leader with a strong background in multi-site healthcare operations and the ability to build scalable people strategies across geographically distributed clinical teams. You should combine strategic thinking with practical HR expertise, strong leadership capabilities, and a thorough understanding of healthcare workforce requirements. The following qualifications and skills are expected:

  • At least 10 years of professional Human Resources experience, including a minimum of 5 years in progressively senior HR leadership positions.

  • At least 3 years of experience working in a multi-site healthcare environment.

  • Strong understanding of clinical operations, healthcare workforce management, and clinical staffing models.

  • Proven experience developing and implementing HR processes, policies, and operational frameworks across multiple locations.

  • Previous experience supporting practice acquisitions, HR due diligence, employee onboarding, and organizational integration is highly valuable.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead HR teams, influence senior stakeholders, and provide strategic guidance to managers and operational leaders.

  • Experience managing employee relations, performance management, compensation strategies, benefits administration, and workforce planning.

  • Strong knowledge of healthcare-related employment regulations and compliance requirements, including HIPAA, OSHA, FLSA, and FMLA.

  • Experience using Human Resources Information Systems (HRIS), with Workday experience strongly preferred.

  • Strong project management, organizational, and process improvement skills, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives and competing priorities.

  • Proficiency with Google Enterprise applications and related workplace productivity tools is preferred.

  • Professional HR certification, such as PHR or SHRM-CP, is strongly preferred.

  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, coaching, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively with HR professionals, clinic managers, and executive leadership.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with sound judgment and attention to detail.

  • Ability to navigate organizational change, establish consistent practices, and build effective relationships across geographically distributed teams.

  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly to various locations across the United States, approximately 15% of the time.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Accounting Operations and Financial Reporting: Own the monthly close calendar and process, delivering accurate and timely financial statements, including profit and loss statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements. Establish clear deadlines, checklists, and accountability measures while continuously improving close efficiency and accuracy.

  • Financial Review and Analysis: Conduct comprehensive reviews of financial results, billing, and key reports to identify discrepancies, unusual fluctuations, and potential risks before they affect reporting. Investigate anomalies and proactively implement corrective actions.

  • GAAP Compliance and Consolidation: Prepare consolidated financial statements in accordance with US GAAP, including intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation, and multi-entity reporting. Coordinate with international accounting providers and review subsidiary financial statements for accuracy and compliance.

  • General Ledger Management: Maintain and improve the chart of accounts and general ledger structure, ensuring accurate transaction coding, classification, and period reporting. Review and approve journal entries and account reconciliations.

  • Billing and Accounts Receivable: Oversee accurate and timely client billing, accounts receivable, aging reports, and collections. Review customer agreements for revenue recognition implications and escalate overdue or at-risk balances to leadership.

  • Accounts Payable and Vendor Management: Supervise accounts payable processes, payment runs, approval workflows, vendor master data, purchase orders, and resale certificate compliance.

  • Payroll Oversight: Oversee domestic and international payroll processing, related accruals, and compliance requirements in partnership with the organization's Professional Employer Organization (PEO).

  • Inventory Accounting: Establish and maintain appropriate inventory accounting practices for reseller and drop-ship operations, including inventory reporting, aging, reserves, reconciliation procedures, third-party inventory tracking, and inventory turnover analysis.

  • International Financial Management: Manage monthly consolidation across domestic and international entities, coordinating with accounting providers in Ireland, India, and Singapore to ensure accurate reporting and appropriate consolidation adjustments.

  • Internal Controls and Risk Management: Strengthen financial controls, establish segregation of duties, maintain approval matrices, and configure and enforce NetSuite approval workflows.

  • Audit and Tax Compliance: Coordinate annual audits, financial reviews, and tax filings. Work with external providers on sales and indirect taxes, state tax nexus, and exemption certificate compliance while maintaining audit-ready financial records.

  • Cash Flow and Financial Planning: Maintain and update a rolling 13-week cash flow forecast and consolidated cash visibility across domestic and international entities. Partner with the Fractional CFO on forecasting, financial strategy, pricing, capital allocation, and contract decisions.

  • Management Reporting: Provide leadership with clear financial insights, including revenue performance, gross margins by client, customer concentration, and other key performance indicators to support pricing and diversification strategies.

  • Budgeting and Cost Analysis: Support budget development, budget-versus-actual reporting, and variance analysis. Develop job costing and client/project profitability reporting suited to a services-based business.

  • ERP Optimization and Automation: Improve the use of NetSuite's reporting, dashboards, workflows, and automation capabilities to establish a reliable financial data foundation for operational reporting.

  • Accounting Team Leadership: Direct and review the work of internal accounting staff, establish priorities, develop team capabilities, and ensure accountability for deliverables. Manage relationships with outsourced accounting and tax providers and serve as the primary point of contact for the external CPA firm.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Build effective relationships with operations, sales, HR, clients, vendors, and external partners to resolve financial matters efficiently and support informed business decisions.

  • Technical Accounting: Research complex accounting matters and prepare technical accounting memoranda when necessary to support conclusions under US GAAP.

  • Strategic Development: Identify financial risks and opportunities, communicate recommendations proactively, and progressively take on broader finance leadership responsibilities in partnership with the Fractional CFO.

  • Confidentiality and Professional Standards: Maintain discretion when handling sensitive financial, employee, and business information, ensuring records meet applicable regulatory and audit requirements.

  • Continuous Improvement: Drive process improvements through automation, stronger workflows, enhanced ERP utilization, and consistent financial accountability.

    • During the first 12 months, you will focus on taking full ownership of the monthly close process, establishing consistent reporting across all entities, strengthening internal controls and NetSuite workflows, improving inventory accounting, and developing reliable cash flow reporting with the Fractional CFO. You will also build strong relationships with international accounting providers and reduce executive involvement in day-to-day accounting decisions by establishing clear ownership and accountability.

As Director of Finance & Business Operations, you will lead the financial and operational activities of the business unit, ensuring accurate financial visibility, effective resource management, and alignment with corporate finance standards. You will work closely with executive leadership, Sales, Operations, and corporate Finance to support sustainable growth, operational discipline, and informed decision-making.

  • Lead financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and analysis for the business unit, serving as a strategic finance partner to executive and functional leaders.

  • Manage and develop the Business Operations Analyst and Finance Operations Analyst, establishing priorities, reviewing deliverables, and ensuring effective coverage across monthly and quarterly activities.

  • Own monthly and quarterly forecasting processes and the annual budget, including headcount, spending, margins, and investment planning.

  • Connect Sales pipeline activity with bookings, billings, and recognized revenue, providing clear explanations of financial performance and variances.

  • Coordinate month-end and quarter-end close activities, ensuring timely and accurate deliverables that meet corporate Finance and Accounting requirements.

  • Oversee end-to-end quote-to-cash operations, including contract setup, customer onboarding, invoicing, usage-based billing, collections, and cash application.

  • Manage billing processes involving resellers, government contract vehicles, and public-sector payment portals, ensuring accurate reconciliation with the general ledger and appropriate revenue recognition.

  • Lead revenue operations and pricing governance, maintaining price lists, discount controls, and quote structures while supporting Sales with financial analysis for commercial decisions.

  • Support pricing and packaging initiatives established by business unit leadership, evaluating financial implications and implementing approved changes.

  • Oversee procurement and spending across cloud and model consumption, software and data subscriptions, contractors, and events, ensuring purchases remain within approved budgets.

  • Manage vendor selection, onboarding, purchase requests, renewals, and spending approvals in accordance with corporate procurement and accounts-payable processes.

  • Partner with Operations to improve cloud-cost visibility and FinOps reporting.

  • Establish and maintain documented financial and operational controls, including approval workflows, segregation of duties, and audit-ready evidence.

  • Support sales tax compliance, ensure billing data is tax-ready, and handle customer and billing records in accordance with FedRAMP and Department of Defense impact-level requirements.

  • Analyze the economics of GSA and other government contract vehicles, reseller arrangements, funding structures, periods of performance, and applicable FAR/DFARS cost principles.

  • Collaborate with Sales and Contracts teams on financial modeling, pricing decisions, and proposal responses.

  • Integrate business unit financial activities with corporate Finance, supporting consolidation, external audits, accruals, deferred revenue, intercompany transactions, and subscription and usage-based revenue recognition.

  • Support SOX 404(b) control owners, including change-control boards and release leads, by providing evidence related to financial processes.

  • Oversee finance systems and data integrity across billing, CRM, and accounting platforms, ensuring consistent and reconciled financial information.

  • Define and maintain reliable SaaS and revenue metrics, including ARR, bookings, retention, and consumption, and develop dashboards for leadership reporting.

  • Apply AI-assisted tools to financial analysis, reconciliation, and process automation while maintaining appropriate human review of information used in accounting records and executive reporting.

  • Present financial results, forecasts, assumptions, and risks to business unit and corporate leadership in a clear, decision-ready format.

  • Identify process weaknesses and lead improvements that strengthen reporting accuracy, operational efficiency, and cash management.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate will have extensive experience managing finance and business operations within a federal contractor, defense contractor, or technology organization serving government customers. You should combine strong financial and analytical capabilities with practical knowledge of government contracting, revenue operations, and public-company reporting requirements.

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field.

  • At least 10 years of progressive finance experience, including leadership of finance or business operations for a business unit, program portfolio, or product line within a federal or defense contractor or federal-facing technology company.

  • At least 3 years of direct experience managing and developing financial or business operations analysts.

  • Demonstrated ownership of P&L forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis, including the ability to connect Sales pipeline activity to revenue projections.

  • Experience overseeing order-to-cash and billing operations, including invoicing, collections, cash application, and general ledger reconciliation.

  • Working knowledge of U.S. federal contracting, including government contract vehicles, reseller arrangements, government invoicing and payment cycles, and FAR/DFARS cost principles.

  • Experience managing procurement, vendor relationships, and spending controls.

  • Familiarity with monthly financial close, consolidation, and audit support within a public-company environment.

  • Advanced financial modeling skills in Microsoft Excel and the ability to work directly with data from billing, CRM, and accounting systems.

  • Strong understanding of financial controls, revenue recognition, and financial reporting processes.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain financial performance, uncertainty, and risks to executive, technical, and nontechnical stakeholders.

  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

    • Preferred Qualifications:

  • CPA, CMA, or MBA.

  • Experience leading finance operations for an acquired company or business unit within a larger public organization, including post-acquisition integration of financial processes and systems.

  • Experience with subscription-based or consumption-priced products, including ARR, retention, and usage-based revenue models.

  • Knowledge of ASC 606 revenue recognition for subscription and usage-based arrangements.

  • Experience with Unanet or comparable project-based ERP systems, and Stripe or similar subscription-billing platforms.

  • Familiarity with government invoicing systems and billing in FedRAMP or Department of Defense impact-level environments.

  • Experience managing cloud costs and FinOps processes across Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud Platform.

  • Knowledge of SQL or business intelligence tools such as Power BI or Tableau for reporting and reconciliation.

  • Experience applying generative AI tools to financial analysis, reconciliation, or process automation.

  • Ability to obtain a Department of Defense Secret security clearance; an active clearance is a plus.

    • Benefits:

  • Annual target compensation range of $173,601–$260,401.

  • Fully remote work arrangement for candidates currently residing in the United States.

  • National Capital Region location preferred.

  • Opportunity to lead finance and business operations within an innovative AI and defense-technology environment.

  • Strategic exposure to executive leadership and cross-functional business operations.

  • Compensation determined based on relevant experience, education, skills, certifications, location, and organizational requirements.

  • Additional employee benefits are offered; specific details are not provided in the job description.

Director of Human Resources - (Healthcare, clinical research, or pharma background preferred)

As Director of Human Resources, you will serve as a strategic advisor to executive leadership while overseeing the delivery and continuous improvement of HR programs across the organization. You will lead a high-performing HR team, align workforce initiatives with business priorities, and ensure consistent people practices across multiple locations. Your responsibilities will include:

  • Strategic HR Leadership: Partner with senior leadership to develop and execute HR strategies aligned with business objectives, supporting organizational growth, expansion into new markets, workforce planning, succession planning, and organizational design.

  • Team Leadership: Lead, develop, and manage the HR team by establishing strategic priorities, setting performance expectations, providing coaching, and supporting professional development.

  • Workforce Planning and Analytics: Use HR metrics, including employee turnover, time-to-fill, and engagement data, to identify trends, anticipate workforce needs, and recommend data-driven improvements.

  • Talent Acquisition and Onboarding: Oversee recruitment strategies, employer branding, requisition management, and hiring processes for clinical, operational, and corporate positions. Ensure consistent onboarding experiences, timely completion of required training, and accurate job descriptions and position titles.

  • Employee Relations and Compliance: Advise managers and employees on HR policies, performance management, corrective actions, and employee separations. Oversee workplace investigations when necessary, maintaining fairness, confidentiality, and compliance with applicable employment regulations.

  • Employment Policies and Risk Management: Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local employment laws, including ADA, FMLA, FLSA, EEO, and wage and hour requirements. Maintain and regularly update employee handbooks, HR policies, and procedures.

  • Compensation and Benefits: Develop and administer compensation strategies, job leveling frameworks, and annual review cycles to promote internal equity and market competitiveness. Oversee employee benefits programs, open enrollment, and vendor relationships.

  • HR Systems and Payroll: Oversee HRIS and payroll platforms, such as ADP, ensuring accurate employee records, data integrity, payroll processes, and HR reporting.

  • Learning and Development: Manage leadership development, employee training, and professional learning initiatives, including mandatory compliance training programs.

  • Employee Engagement and Culture: Lead engagement, recognition, and retention initiatives, using employee feedback and performance data to measure effectiveness and drive continuous improvement. Champion diversity, equity, and inclusion across organizational practices.

  • Operational Management: Oversee team administration, including recruitment, performance reviews, employee counseling, career coaching, timecards, payroll coordination, absence tracking, new hire orientation, and training.

  • Performance and Operational Excellence: Monitor team activities, proactively identify and resolve operational challenges, and ensure compliance with internal policies and applicable regulations.

  • Stakeholder Collaboration: Build strong working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, understand their needs, and ensure HR services support organizational priorities.

  • Organizational Representation: Represent the organization at relevant conferences and industry events, promoting its mission and strengthening its reputation within the clinical research community.

  • Communication and Collaboration: Participate in and lead departmental, management, and organizational meetings, fostering a positive, results-oriented environment and encouraging collaboration across teams.

  • Additional Responsibilities: Perform other duties and projects as assigned to support the organization's evolving business and operational needs.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate is an experienced HR leader with strong strategic, operational, and people-management capabilities. You should bring a solid understanding of employment legislation and HR best practices, along with the ability to manage complex workforce needs across multiple locations. Experience in healthcare, clinical research, or pharmaceuticals is strongly preferred. The following qualifications and skills are required:

  • A bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Psychology, Business Administration, or a related field, combined with at least 10 years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience.

  • At least 8 years of experience in Human Resources management, with advanced knowledge of HR principles, employment legislation, and industry best practices.

  • Previous experience in healthcare, clinical research, or pharmaceutical environments is highly preferred.

  • Experience supporting multi-site, multi-state organizations and managing HR operations across geographically distributed teams is strongly preferred.

  • Proven expertise in employee relations, workplace investigations, organizational change management, and conflict resolution.

  • Senior-level HR certification, such as SPHR, SHRM-SCP, or an equivalent qualification, is highly preferred.

  • Strong leadership and people-management skills, with experience developing teams, coaching managers, and influencing senior stakeholders.

  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across all organizational levels.

  • Strong organizational, time-management, problem-solving, and project-management abilities, with excellent attention to detail and the capacity to meet strict deadlines.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft applications, HRIS platforms, payroll systems, and web-based applications. Ability to type at least 40 words per minute.

  • Basic mathematical proficiency and the ability to interpret HR data, workforce metrics, and operational reports.

• Lead the Payments tribe across three cross-functional squads comprising backend, frontend, mobile, and QA engineers, with responsibility for delivery outcomes, engineering quality, team health, and professional development.

  • Coordinate priorities, execution, and dependencies across squads and other engineering teams to ensure predictable delivery and alignment with business objectives.

  • Own people management activities, including performance reviews, career development, compensation and promotion recommendations, hiring, and performance improvement when required.

  • Oversee payment provider and payment method integrations, enabling expansion into new markets and acting as the senior engineering contact for providers during technical escalations.

  • Safeguard the reliability of payment and payout flows by leading incident response, conducting root cause analyses, and driving improvements in payment approval rates, payout processing times, and reconciliation accuracy.

  • Ensure payment systems meet demanding security and compliance standards by minimizing exposure of sensitive data, strengthening security controls, preventing API abuse, and collaborating with Security, Fraud, and Compliance teams on audits and risk mitigation.

  • Maintain robust engineering practices for financial transactions, including idempotency, safe retries, reliable transaction state management, auditability, and consistency across distributed systems.

  • Work closely with Team Leads and Product Managers to clarify requirements, identify technical risks, align priorities, and remove execution obstacles.

  • Improve planning, coordination, development, and release processes as the platform and its portfolio of brands expand.

  • Communicate roadmap progress, delivery commitments, payment performance metrics, technical constraints, and risks to Product, Operations, Finance, and senior leadership.

  • Build a strong understanding of the payment architecture, providers, and engineering workflows during onboarding, and participate in the incident on-call rotation.

  • Drive the continuous improvement of the Payments tribe, with measurable progress in reliability, security, operational performance, and team effectiveness.

    • Requirements:

  • At least 10 years of software development experience, with deep backend engineering expertise in the Java ecosystem and a strong understanding of concurrency, distributed systems, and scalable service architectures.

  • Proven experience building, operating, or leading teams responsible for systems where financial accuracy is essential, such as payment processing, payouts, digital wallets, billing, ledgers, or banking platforms.

  • Hands-on experience delivering integrations with payment service providers, acquirers, payment orchestration platforms, or payout providers, including an understanding of their operational challenges and failure scenarios.

  • Demonstrated engineering leadership experience managing teams of approximately 15–25 engineers, ideally across multiple squads through Team Leads.

  • A track record of delivering complex production systems while balancing technical direction, execution management, and people leadership.

  • Experience leading production incident response and driving meaningful post-incident improvements for revenue-critical systems.

  • Strong understanding of payment security and the protection of sensitive financial and personal information, including measures to prevent payment API abuse.

  • Strong product and business judgment, with the ability to identify gaps, anticipate risks, assess technical implications, and challenge requirements constructively.

  • Excellent delivery ownership, including realistic estimation, stakeholder alignment, clear communication of timelines, and the ability to explain scope options, trade-offs, and risks.

  • Strong English communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively in technical discussions, cross-functional meetings, and external vendor interactions.

  • Nice to have: Experience with payment orchestration platforms, multiple payment providers, and payment routing and fallback strategies.

  • Nice to have: Knowledge of 3DS2, Strong Customer Authentication, chargebacks, and fraud and risk management tools.

  • Nice to have: Experience managing payouts through ACH, push-to-debit, or e-wallet providers.

  • Nice to have: Familiarity with multicurrency processing, settlement, and financial reconciliation.

  • Nice to have: Knowledge of PCI DSS and KYC/AML requirements in regulated markets.

  • Nice to have: Experience in fintech or another regulated industry, iGaming, or high-load real-time platforms.

  • Nice to have: Previous experience as a Staff Engineer, Principal Engineer, or Solution Architect.

  • Nice to have: Experience working in product-led companies or high-growth scale-ups.

  • Fully remote work: Work remotely from the location where you are most productive.

  • Paid time off: 30 days of paid leave covering vacation and sick leave, in addition to public holidays.

• Lead and manage strategic relationships with assessment, accreditation, and regulatory partners, acting as the senior point of contact and making decisions within agreed organisational parameters.

You will lead the marketing function end to end, developing the strategy, processes, and team needed to increase brand awareness, support revenue growth, and strengthen relationships with customers and partners. Your responsibilities will include:

  • Brand Awareness and Storytelling: Define the brand narrative, positioning, and messaging across all channels. Develop a distinctive market story and oversee brand assets, including guidelines, website content, presentations, visual identity, and templates.

  • Demand Generation: Design and execute integrated inbound and outbound campaigns to generate qualified pipeline. Manage the marketing funnel, budget, attribution, and performance targets in alignment with the Revenue team.

  • Events and Trade Shows: Lead participation in industry events and trade shows, establish performance KPIs, and coordinate lead generation, conversion accountability, and post-event follow-up campaigns.

  • Communications and PR: Build relationships with media outlets and industry analysts, secure relevant coverage, and manage press releases, company announcements, executive thought leadership, and social media. Ensure consistent internal and external communications.

  • Product Marketing: Translate product capabilities into compelling customer value propositions in collaboration with Product. Develop product updates, launch plans, release communications, competitive intelligence, and sales battlecards. Organize customer and prospect webinars and deliver product training for internal teams.

  • Sales Enablement and Partner Marketing: Equip Sales with effective content, playbooks, and tools. Develop and deliver Managed Intelligent Partner (MIP) workshops, create co-marketing programs, and manage partner marketing development funds (MDF). Oversee partner newsletters, subscription growth, and customer success stories through testimonials, use cases, one-pagers, and videos.

  • Team Development: Evaluate existing marketing capabilities and identify organizational gaps, including opportunities for agency and freelance support. Design a scalable team structure and phased hiring plan, recruit and develop talent, establish clear goals and KPIs, and foster a collaborative, accountable culture.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate is an experienced B2B marketing leader with a strong understanding of technology-driven businesses and the ability to balance strategic direction with practical execution.   • 10+ years of B2B marketing experience, ideally within technology, SaaS, or agency environments.

  • Demonstrated success across brand strategy, demand generation, and product marketing.

  • Experience in channel or partner marketing, including co-marketing initiatives and MDF programs.

  • Strong storytelling, writing, and presentation skills, with confidence engaging with the media and speaking at industry events.

• Take end-to-end ownership of payment platforms and infrastructure across multiple DTC brands, overseeing quality assurance, reporting, documentation, and continuous performance analysis.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for all payment-related matters, supporting internal brand and operations teams as well as external payment service providers (PSPs).
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation covering payment flows, platform configurations, integrations, and provider setups for each brand.
  • Lead payment infrastructure setup for new brands, including PSP integrations, merchant account verification, business onboarding, and payment configuration.
  • Ensure all payment systems and integrations are properly configured, tested, and fully operational before new brand launches.
  • Research, evaluate, and test new payment providers, developing strategies for integrating additional PSPs into the existing payment ecosystem.
  • Analyze and compare payment provider performance based on transaction fees, authorization rates, reliability, and customer support quality.
  • Continuously monitor payment performance across all brands and identify opportunities to improve transaction acceptance and authorization rates.
  • Optimize payment routing, retry logic, checkout configurations, and other payment processes to maximize successful transactions.
  • Monitor fraud trends and configure fraud prevention rules and filters to balance transaction approval rates with financial risk exposure.
  • Manage the complete dispute, claim, and chargeback process across all payment providers, including Stripe, PayPal, and other platforms.
  • Gather supporting documentation, prepare compelling representment cases, and submit evidence within payment provider deadlines.
  • Analyze dispute reason codes and identify recurring patterns, translating insights into recommendations for checkout improvements, customer policies, and Customer Support processes.
  • Monitor payment provider account health, including dispute ratios, reserve requirements, risk status, and relevant monitoring programs such as VAMP and SAFE.
  • Identify potential account risks early and implement corrective actions to maintain healthy payment processing relationships.
  • Develop and maintain daily, weekly, and monthly reports covering key payment performance indicators.
  • Present payment performance, account health, emerging risks, and optimization opportunities to senior leadership and relevant stakeholders.

    • Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

  • Payment acceptance and authorization rates.
  • Fraud rates and associated financial losses.
  • Payment processing fees and effective transaction costs across providers.
  • Payment service provider account health, including account standing, reserves, and risk status.
  • Dispute and chargeback rates.

    • Requirements:

  • At least 2 years of professional experience in payments, fraud prevention, or financial risk management, preferably within e-commerce or direct-to-consumer (DTC) businesses.
  • Hands-on experience managing payment service providers such as Stripe, PayPal, or similar platforms.
  • Practical experience handling payment disputes, chargebacks, and representment processes.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to build and maintain KPI dashboards, analyze transaction data, and identify actionable performance insights.
  • Familiarity with fraud prevention tools, 3D Secure (3DS), and payment provider risk management programs, including dispute ratio thresholds and monitoring requirements.
  • Experience onboarding new merchant accounts, configuring payment systems, and managing payment integrations.
  • Understanding of payment authorization processes, transaction routing, processing fees, and fraud prevention strategies.
  • Excellent written communication skills, particularly for preparing dispute evidence, maintaining technical documentation, and collaborating with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Strong organizational and problem-solving abilities, with the capacity to manage multiple payment platforms and operational priorities simultaneously.
  • Ability to work independently and take full ownership of responsibilities, balancing reactive activities such as dispute management with proactive payment optimization.
  • A proactive, detail-oriented, and results-driven mindset, with a strong focus on operational efficiency and financial performance.
  • Experience managing payment operations across multiple brands, merchant accounts, or international markets is a strong advantage.

  • Complimentary fresh fruit, healthy snacks, and quality coffee at the office.

  • Document modelling assumptions, methodologies, calculations, and assessment criteria.

As a senior MDM advisor, you will oversee key design decisions, assess implementation deliverables, and guide teams toward scalable, transparent, and sustainable master data solutions.

  • Auditability and Explainability: Promote transparent and reversible mastering practices, ensuring matching and survivorship decisions can be traced to source records and supported by comprehensive audit histories.

Medical Director, Utilization Management and Case Management

Provide strategic medical oversight across utilization management and complex case management activities, ensuring clinically appropriate decisions, effective resource utilization, and high-quality member experiences. You will serve as a trusted physician advisor to clinical teams and external providers while contributing to clinical governance, quality improvement, and healthcare cost optimization initiatives.

  • Conduct prospective, concurrent, and retrospective utilization reviews using evidence-based guidelines, including InterQual criteria, nationally recognized clinical standards, and client-specific medical policies.

  • Review prior authorization requests and make independent medical necessity determinations for services that do not meet established clinical criteria.

  • Issue timely, accurate, and well-documented approval, modification, or denial decisions in accordance with applicable regulatory, accreditation, and organizational requirements.

  • Conduct peer-to-peer discussions with treating physicians and other healthcare providers to explain medical necessity decisions and explore appropriate alternative treatment options.

  • Review inpatient admissions, continued hospital stays, transitions of care, post-acute services, and specialty treatment requests to promote appropriate healthcare resource utilization.

  • Provide physician-level guidance to nurses and clinical team members handling escalated utilization management questions and complex medical situations.

  • Review appeals and grievance cases when not involved in the original determination, communicating clinical reasoning and decisions clearly and professionally.

  • Ensure utilization management activities comply with NCQA, URAC, ERISA, state regulatory requirements, and client-specific standards.

  • Collaborate with clinical operations leadership to improve review consistency, decision turnaround times, healthcare affordability, and member outcomes.

  • Serve as the physician advisor for complex, catastrophic, chronic, and high-risk cases requiring multidisciplinary care coordination.

  • Provide clinical oversight for high-cost and medically complex cases, including oncology, organ transplants, specialty pharmacy, neonatal and pediatric intensive care, behavioral health, and other significant healthcare needs.

  • Participate in multidisciplinary case conferences, safety reviews, escalation meetings, and complex case discussions to support optimal clinical decisions.

  • Review complex case management recommendations and individualized care plans for medically fragile and high-utilizing members.

  • Collaborate with case managers, care coordinators, behavioral health clinicians, pharmacists, and specialty vendors to address treatment barriers, care gaps, and opportunities for improved outcomes.

  • Evaluate quality-of-care concerns, member safety incidents, potential adverse outcomes, and clinical escalations, recommending appropriate corrective actions and improvements.

  • Analyze high-cost cases and emerging utilization patterns to identify opportunities for early intervention, more effective care management, and reduced avoidable healthcare expenditures.

  • Contribute to the development and implementation of clinical programs focused on chronic disease management, population health, specialty condition management, and care optimization.

  • Review utilization, quality, safety, and clinical outcome data to identify trends and recommend improvements for members and clients.

  • Maintain strong clinical relationships with providers, hospitals, centers of excellence, specialty vendors, and payer partners to facilitate coordinated, high-quality care.

  • Participate in Medical Director meetings, utilization management and quality committees, and broader clinical initiatives.

  • Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of medical policies, clinical guidelines, and operational workflows.

  • Support physician and clinical staff education on utilization management, care management practices, and evidence-based medicine.

  • Act as a subject matter expert on healthcare delivery, clinical quality, cost containment, and member advocacy.

  • Protect confidential company and member information by following applicable privacy, security, compliance, and organizational policies.
