ABOUT THE ROLE:

Machina Labs is looking for a Director of Infrastructure & Security to build the secure, scalable technology foundation for our next stage of growth. 

You’ll lead enterprise IT, cloud and DevOps infrastructure, cybersecurity, compliance, and physical security systems across Machina Labs’ commercial operations and Machina Bellator, our defense-focused subsidiary. 

This is a build role. You’ll inherit capable teams and an existing technology foundation, but there is significant work ahead as Machina scales. You will define the infrastructure and security roadmap, strengthen our defense-compliant environment, build our Security Engineering capability, and ensure our systems can scale without slowing down the engineers and operators who rely on them. 

You’ll report to the VP of Engineering – Software & IT and partner closely with leaders across Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, EHS, Legal, and the broader business. 

This is a player-coach role for someone who can set strategy and build organizations while staying close enough to the technology to dive in when it matters. 

What You’ll Do:

 - 

 - Set the infrastructure and security strategy. Define and execute the strategy for IT, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and security systems across Machina Labs and Machina Bellator as our teams, facilities, and defense programs scale. 

 - Lead and grow the organization. Lead the IT and DevOps teams, define the organization needed for the next stage of growth, develop existing leaders, and build the Security Engineering function from the ground up. 

 - Scale cloud and DevOps infrastructure. Guide the architecture, reliability, security, and cost management of our AWS environment in partnership with DevOps and Software Engineering. Establish scalable approaches to infrastructure as code, CI/CD, observability, and production operations. 

 - Build our cybersecurity capability. Establish and mature security operations across endpoint protection, SIEM and logging, threat detection and response, vulnerability management, incident response, and security architecture. 

 - Lead technical defense compliance. Own the technology strategy, controls, documentation, and audit readiness required to support CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, DFARS, ITAR/EAR, and other requirements associated with our defense and aerospace programs. 

 - Own physical security technology. Partner with EHS, which owns the broader physical security program, to architect and operate the technology behind facility security — including access control, surveillance, identity integration, monitoring, and related security systems. 

 - Establish policy and governance. Partner with Legal, EHS, Compliance, Engineering, and Operations to create pragmatic security and IT policies that protect the company and satisfy customer and regulatory requirements without creating unnecessary friction. 

What We’re Looking For:

 - 

 - 10+ years of experience across infrastructure, enterprise IT, cybersecurity, DevOps, or related technical functions, including significant experience leading technical teams and senior leaders. 

 - Experience owning infrastructure and/or security in a complex engineering, manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or similarly regulated environment. 

 - Demonstrated ability to build and scale technology functions, operating models, and teams — not simply operate established systems. 

 - Strong working knowledge of modern enterprise IT, cloud infrastructure, networking, identity and access management, and cybersecurity architecture. 

 - Experience with AWS or comparable cloud environments and modern DevOps practices. 

 - Experience building or operating cybersecurity programs spanning areas such as endpoint security, logging/SIEM, vulnerability management, incident response, and detection and response. 

 - Experience working with security and compliance frameworks such as CMMC or comparable regulated environments. 

 - A builder mindset. You’re comfortable moving between long-term strategy, organizational design, and the technical details required to get something working. 

Nice to Have:

 - 

 - Experience in defense, aerospace, or another environment handling CUI, export-controlled information, or classified programs. 

 - Experience taking an organization through CMMC certification or a comparable cybersecurity compliance program. 

 - Experience working in ITAR/EAR-controlled environments. 

 - Experience designing technology infrastructure for manufacturing facilities, engineering labs, or other complex physical environments. 

 - Experience with physical security technologies such as access control, video surveillance, visitor management, and integrated identity systems. 

 - Experience scaling infrastructure and security through a period of rapid company and facility growth.

ABOUT MAINCODE

Maincode is an AI research and engineering company. We build Matilda, a large language model trained and served on our own infrastructure, and the products around it: Matilda Chat on web and mobile, and Matilda Code in the terminal, on the desktop and through the API. Our Seattle team works on the layer above the model, focusing on product and user experience.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Matilda has launched out of beta and into the hands of users. You will be the person at Maincode who knows those people best: who they are, what they are trying to get done, where Matilda helps them and where it gets in their way.

You will run the research yourself. You will talk to users every week, watch them work, and bring what you learn directly to our product lead and the engineers who build the product. We are a small, high-agency team, so nothing sits between your findings and the people who can act on them. When the research says something should change, you make the case to the people who will change it, and you will often see the result in the product that same week.

This is a role with real influence over what we build. We expect you to have a view and to argue for it.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Run user interviews and usability tests across the Matilda products, focusing on Matilda Code, from people opening it for the first time to users who rely on it every day.

 - Decide what we most need to learn next, in collaboration with teammates, and choose the method that will answer it, qualitative or quantitative.

 - Work day to day with our product lead and core engineers, and turn what you find into changes we ship.

 - Go back to users once a change is out and find out whether it worked.

 - Build the way Maincode does user research: the participant pool, the interview guides, and a record of findings the whole team can use.




YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF

 - You have a master's or PhD in human-computer interaction or a related field such as cognitive science, psychology, design research or information science, or equivalent experience.

 - You are a mixed methods researcher. You have run interviews and usability tests with real participants, and you are just as comfortable with quantitative analysis and interpretation.

 - You are warm and curious. You will be talking to our users from your first week, and we need to be comfortable putting you in front of them.

 - You balance research depth with practicality.

 - You are hungry to do this work and are opinionated about the future of AI products.

ABOUT MARIANA MINERALS

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company on a mission to supply the critical minerals powering modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. We’re reimagining the minerals supply chain by combining deep industry expertise with advanced software, automation, and data-driven decision-making.

As a Lab Technician in our San Francisco Bay Area lab, you'll focus on high-quality sample preparation and routine analytical testing on instruments like our ICP-OES and TOC analyzer. This entry-level role is a great fit for a detail-oriented, disciplined technician who puts lab safety first, enjoys hands-on analytical work, and has a foundational understanding of spectroscopic instruments and other chemical analysis equipment. Your results feed our process engineering team. The role is built around a consistent daily routine, so if you take pride in doing the same work well, day after day, you'll fit right in. We'll train the right person on our instruments.

Responsibilities

 - Prepare samples using established procedures, including dilution and sample transfer.

 - Enter sample IDs and results accurately into our system.

 - Load and run samples on the ICP-OES and TOC analyzer.

 - Keep clear, accurate records and flag anything that looks off.

 - Keep your work area and equipment clean and organized.

Qualifications

 - A science background from a degree, coursework, or hands-on lab experience. Recent grads and experienced techs are encouraged to apply.

 - Comfortable with sample prep and chemical handling, with a solid understanding of lab safety.

 - Accurate and detail-oriented when recording sample IDs and results; minimal calculation required.

 - Able to read, understand, and follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), including safety and quality procedures.

 - Experience in a chemistry or testing lab, or with ICP-OES, TOC, or similar instruments, is a strong plus.

Schedule

 - 12:00pm–8:30pm, Monday–Friday

Working Environment & Physical Requirements

 - Work with acids and reagents; full PPE provided and required.

 - Standing, repetitive bench work and occasional lifting up to 50 lbs

ABOUT US


Medical data exchange is one of the biggest unsolved problems in US healthcare. If you've spent any real time in the healthcare system, you've felt it, and it only gets worse the sicker and older you get. Metriport exists to fix that. We connect to the data sources the healthcare providers of tomorrow need, take raw data that's unusable in its source form, and turn it into a single clean format that care teams, and their agents, actually use to improve outcomes. Record retrieval across thousands of legacy systems and antiquated data pipes that used to take weeks now takes seconds. Clinicians walk into appointments with the full patient picture already in hand, and that speed can mean spotting a condition early enough to actually treat it.

We're not a healthcare company. We're a technology company that happens to operate in healthcare, and we build every layer ourselves: connect, transform, and insight. Legacy EHRs were built to get providers paid, not to serve the clinical experience. We're building what should have existed instead: the system of record for all of US healthcare. We started in data exchange. Today we compete with the largest data platforms in the space. Tomorrow we will be the infrastructure layer healthcare runs on.

We’ve raised $28.4 million from top tier VCs (including Matrix, ARTIS and Y Combinator), found product market fit (multi million dollar ARR, 100+ customers including Amazon One Medical, Circle Medical, Color Health, and Strive Health), and have years of runway ahead of us. If you’ve had a good healthcare experience in the past few years, there’s a good chance Metriport was behind it. That’s the version of healthcare we want people to not just expect, but demand. Join us and build the future.

We're a small, high output team, mostly former founders including YC alumni, and we operate with real autonomy and almost no bureaucracy. We hire on competence, not pedigree. Leaders are in the office six days a week, not because we count hours, but because there's always more wood to chop when revolutionizing how tomorrow’s healthcare providers deliver care to their patients today. We trust our team to take the time off they need and we've never said no to a time off request.

You have an entrepreneurial mindset and a strong sense of ownership. You don't wait to be told what's broken. The Role 

As a Founding Designer at Metriport, you'll spend your time understanding customer workflows, defining the right solution to those problems, and making sure everything we ship product, marketing, brand, looks and feels right. The upside is real autonomy: you set the design standard, you own the output, and you're not waiting on anyone else's approval. The tradeoff is that the scope is wide and the bar is high. If that sounds like too much, it probably is. If it sounds like exactly enough, keep reading.

At Metriport we think of design like a rough hewn yet elegant table: does its job, looks right in the room, built to last, and finished. You'll bring that sensibility to everything, knowing when a decision needs more thought and when it needs to ship.

We strongly believe in the 80/20 rule, and rely on everyone joining our team to use it so that we can ship fast and continue to delight our users.

 - Technical literacy: You know enough about how software gets built to write specs engineers can use and have real tradeoff conversations.

 - The "Metriport" Mindset: Low ego, high ownership. You ask "Why can't this be done in 3 days?" instead of 3 weeks.

On the frontend, we use React on the backend, we rely on Node.js and TypeScript for writing core business logic. THE ROLE

As the Strategic Projects Lead, you will be tasked with owning multiple, long term healthcare projects that drive the business forward and will directly impact the experience of our customers. These projects will primarily focus on Metriport’s role in the broader healthcare interoperability landscape. You will navigate the legal, technical, and compliance frameworks that define the present and future of US health data exchange and ensure Metriport is positioned to support our customers’ needs.

You will be a highly collaborative individual contributor who identifies internal needs that can be solved via partnerships efforts. This team member will ruthlessly execute on strategic efforts at hand – ensuring high level alignment, coordination, and owning tactical steps. You'll be held accountable for achieving measurable results that enable our organization and customers to provide better care to their patients.




YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR:

 - Project Leadership: Leading end to end execution of internal and external projects that require attention to detail and consideration of both national and state requirements.

 - Ruthless Prioritization: You can identify the most important item to focus resources on. You constantly ensure the most important task at hand is on track and that your priorities are aligned with the company’s needs.

 - Consensus Building: You can play up to the leadership level, identifying different stakeholders, their incentives, and how to ensure Metriport can accomplish its goals within existing constraints.

 - Forward Thinking: You think and see five steps ahead, identifying future blockers and ensuring they don’t exist when they would become problematic.

 - Problem Solving: Ability to work through hard problems with many constraints, using sound judgment to assess risks and lay out arguments in well structured, data informed narratives.

 - Applying Product Knowledge to Projects: Translating an understanding of our product (technical and non technical components) into requirements and considerations within our strategic projects.




REQUIREMENTS

 - Project Ownership: 3+ years of project management, business operations, or MBB consulting experience.

 - Partnership Experience: 3+ years of building partnerships with external parties from scratch

 - Healthcare Domain: 3+ years of experience within healthcare interoperability.

 - Organization: You turn chaos into concise clarity through incredible organization that keeps you, internal stakeholders, and external stakeholders on schedule. Missed deadlines keep you up at night.

 - Regulatory & Governance Fluency: Familiar with working in regulated industries and on projects that have significant governance requirements.

 - Autonomy: Comfortable taking an ambiguous objective, breaking it down to ensure alignment, identifying the most efficient way to accomplish it, and executing.

 - Peripheral Skills: You know enough about topics such as finance, data, compliance, and engineering to ask thoughtful questions and loop in the appropriate stakeholders when relevant.

 - Location: Based in San Francisco (or willing to relocate) to work from our South Beach office.

 - The "Metriport" Mindset: Low ego, high ownership. You are someone who asks "Why can't this be done in 3 days?" instead of 3 weeks.

ABOUT US


Medical data exchange is one of the biggest unsolved problems in US healthcare. If you've spent any real time in the healthcare system, you've felt it, and it only gets worse the sicker and older you get. Metriport exists to fix that. We connect to the data sources the healthcare providers of tomorrow need, take raw data that's unusable in its source form, and turn it into a single clean format that care teams, and their agents, actually use to improve outcomes. Record retrieval across thousands of legacy systems and antiquated data pipes that used to take weeks now takes seconds. Clinicians walk into appointments with the full patient picture already in hand, and that speed can mean spotting a condition early enough to actually treat it.

We're not a healthcare company. We're a technology company that happens to operate in healthcare, and we build every layer ourselves: connect, transform, and insight. Legacy EHRs were built to get providers paid, not to serve the clinical experience. We're building what should have existed instead: the system of record for all of US healthcare. We started in data exchange. Today we compete with the largest data platforms in the space. Tomorrow we will be the infrastructure layer healthcare runs on.

We’ve raised $28.4 million from top tier VCs (including Matrix, ARTIS and Y Combinator), found product market fit (multi million dollar ARR, 100+ customers including Amazon One Medical, Circle Medical, Color Health, and Strive Health), and have years of runway ahead of us. If you’ve had a good healthcare experience in the past few years, there’s a good chance Metriport was behind it. That’s the version of healthcare we want people to not just expect, but demand. Join us and build the future.

The role

We're looking for "generalist" engineers who can operate at a Senior level:

 - You're confident in building scalable, distributed systems across the full stack with particular depth on the back end and people usually come to you for technical guidance.

 - You fully own your work technical decisions, delivery, results and you level up the engineers around you through code reviews, pairing, and guidance. Multiplying the team's output energizes you as much as shipping your own.

 - You're entrepreneurial minded with an olympian level work ethic (about half our engineering team are former founders).

 - You understand reliability, security, and networking end to end designing for uptime, thinking like an attacker to harden your systems, and diving into the network layer yourself rather than treating it as someone else's domain.

 - You care about delivering value to customers, not about what frilly new tech is under the hood.

 - When someone scopes a project for 3 weeks, you ask "why can't it be done in 3 days?" and you help others develop that same instinct.

 - You're a hacker at heart, with a good sense of which rules should, and shouldn't, be broken.

We ingest clinical data for millions of patients from external healthcare sources, with continuous updates for a growing subset of those patients. You'll be a catalyst to scale the platform that powers our product and ship it to customers fast.

Day to day, that looks like:

 - Raising the technical bar: applying and improving our patterns for low latency, highly scalable, event based systems integrations; championing observability into every part of the platform you touch; writing maintainable code that sets the example for others; and making effective use of AI in our product (evals, harnesses, observability).

 - Working across our back end heavy platform: our public API (the core product our customers build on), integrations with health information networks (Carequality, CommonWell, eHealth Exchange) and third parties (EHRs, data vendors, partner platforms), and the platform work that lets the rest of the team ship faster.

 - Driving projects end to end, from ideation to production rollout: writing Design Documents, shipping v0's quickly, and iterating to v1 and beyond.

 - Multiplying the team: mentoring engineers, reviewing designs and PRs, judging when to invest in quality vs. ship fast, and improving our dev processes and tooling so quality and security are enforced by default.

 - Participating in bi weekly sprint planning and retros, joining our daily 30 min remote stand up at 7:30am PST (our only mandatory meeting), and taking part in the on call rotation.

Example projects you could own:

 - Refactoring our core data pipeline to process data 10x faster than originally designed.

 - Using AI/ML to turn freeform doctors' notes into structured data we can add to patients' medical records.

 - Identifying the biggest infra cost opportunities and shipping the changes saving money while increasing scalability.

 - Transforming incoming TCP messages from hospitals using a 90s era protocol into modern HTTP webhooks routed to our customers.

 - Leveling up developer experience: making systems easier to test, tightening CI/CD, and cutting the time from PR to production.


REQUIREMENTS

 - 6+ years as a full stack engineer, with a heavy lean towards back end public APIs, distributed systems, and complex integrations with external systems.

 - Experience developing, maintaining, and scaling cloud based platforms to many millions or billions of transactions a day including optimizing architecture and code for scalability and cost.

 - Experience mentoring or guiding other engineers through code reviews, pairing, design feedback, or onboarding.

 - You've made engineering teams faster better developer experience, more testability, shorter release cycles and you can talk about the before/after.

 - You’re located in San Francisco or the Bay Area (or willing to relocate).

 - Bonus:
   
   - Experience processing large amounts of data, including moving it across different services, transforming/consolidating, and building services to query it.
   
   - Healthcare standards/technologies: FHIR, HIE, IHE, EHR/EMR, NPI, TEFCA, ADT, HL7, HEDIS, RAF, SNOMED, LOINC, ICD 10, etc.

 - Competitive equity + compensation package 🚀

 - Full family Platinum health insurance, dental, and vision coverage 🦷

 - 401(k) retirement plan + matching 💰

 - Flexible work from home or in office 🏢

 - Healthy lunches are complimentary when working in office (and breakfast + dinners as needed) 🍏

 - MacBook provided by us 💻

 - Unlimited PTO (we work hard, but trust you to take time you need to be at your best) 🧘‍♂️


OUR TECH

Core business logic in Node.js and TypeScript, with Python in data and ML workflows. AWS across the board (ECS, Lambda, SQS, SNS, Batch, etc.), infrastructure as code with CDK. Data lives in S3, PostgreSQL/Aurora, DynamoDB, Snowflake, and our FHIR server with Athena for querying S3 and SageMaker for ML. The ideal person for this role is a generalist who picks the best tool for the job.

THE ROLE

This is the first Machine Learning Engineer role at Metriport. We have access to the richest clinical datasets in the country longitudinal medical records for hundreds of millions of individuals and we've barely scratched the surface of what can be learned from it. You'll own machine learning at Metriport end to end: from framing the problem with customers, to training the models, to serving them in production and keeping them honest.

This is applied ML on messy, high dimensional, real world healthcare data, not a research role, and not an LLM wrapper role.

 - You have deep ML fundamentals, from classical methods through deep learning. You can take a prediction problem from a linear baseline to gradient boosted trees to a neural network and you know when each one is the right answer.

 - You've shipped models to production and lived with them: you have opinions about evaluation, monitoring, retraining, and what can break after launch.

 - You're deeply experienced with ML, but still have strong eng chops: you can stand up a service, write the IaC, instrument it, and own it end to end. Python is home; TypeScript, AWS, and SQL aren't going to scare you.

 - You're pragmatic about LLMs. You've used them where they win and you know where a smaller, cheaper, more reliable model wins instead.

 - You're comfortable with messy, real world data: sparse, inconsistent, high dimensional, and full of surprises. Healthcare data is all of these at once.

 - You're entrepreneurial minded with an olympian level work ethic (about half our engineering team are former founders).

 - When someone scopes a project for 3 weeks, you ask "why can't it be done in 3 days?"  and you help others develop that same instinct.

 - You're a hacker at heart, with a good sense of which rules should, and shouldn't, be broken.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

You'll build the models, and the ML platform underneath them, that turn raw clinical data into intelligence our customers act on.

Day to day, that looks like:

 - Building predictive models on clinical data at scale: risk stratification, expected utilization / prediction, care gap detection.

 - Owning the full ML lifecycle: problem framing, feature engineering over sparse and high dimensional clinical data, training, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring for drift and degradation in production.

 - Turning unstructured clinical data into structured, usable records: parsing PDFs, images, doctor notes, etc.

 - Standing up our ML infrastructure: training and inference pipelines, experiment tracking, model versioning, and evals so that every model we ship is measurable, debuggable, reliable.

 - Working directly with founders, engineers, and customers to figure out which ML problems are highest leverage to solve next.

Example projects you could own:

 - Building a model that predicts expected hospitalizations for new patients from their medical history.

 - Turn freeform doctors' notes and scanned documents into structured data we can add to patients' medical records.

 - Build classifiers to categorize billions of clinical documents with incomplete metadata.
   
   


REQUIREMENTS

 - 7+ years building ML systems that run against real data at scale.

Clinicians walk into appointments with the full patient picture already in hand, and that speed can mean spotting a condition early enough to actually treat it.

ABOUT NOVO

Small businesses are the backbone of the US economy, comprising almost half of the GDP and the private workforce. Yet, big banks don’t provide the access, assistance and modern tools that owners need to successfully grow their business.

We started Novo to challenge the status quo. We’re on a mission to increase the GDP of the modern entrepreneur by creating the go-to banking platform for small businesses (SMBs). Our modern bank accounts and tools help owners save time, increase cash flow and manage their business in one place.


WHY NOVO?

 - 250,000+ business customers using the platform

 - $30B+ in transactions processed

 - Profitable, with $170M raised to date

 - Backed by firms including Valar Ventures, Crosslink Capital, Stripes, BoxGroup, RRE Ventures, and Notable Capital

 - Global workforce with offices in New York, LatAm, and India


THE ROLE

Until now, businesses have found Novo on their own. We haven’t had a sales function, and you’ll be the one who builds it.

We’re starting now for two reasons. We want to bring on larger businesses, and a business that size switches after a real conversation with someone who knows the product. We’ve also built a lot more than a checking account, so there’s far more to sell than there used to be.

This is a player-coach role, and it starts with the player part. In your first few months you’re the one prospecting, calling and closing, so you learn firsthand which businesses to go after and what gets them to switch. Then you hire and lead a team built around what you learned.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Sell

 - Develop the sales strategy to target and reach Novo’s ideal customer.

 - Prospect, call and close businesses that keep their money somewhere else today.

 - Show owners in plain terms why Novo is the better choice, and lay out the easiest way to move over.

 - Get hands-on with the switch when a customer needs it, so moving payments, payroll and everything tied to their old account doesn’t stall the deal.

 - Learn which businesses, offers and messages convert, and keep a clear record of it.

Work with AI

 - Use AI as your main tool for prospect research, list building, outreach and pipeline tracking.

 - Build your own workflows with it, and keep improving them as you learn what works.

 - Set how the sales team uses AI as it grows.

Build the team

 - Turn what worked into a playbook other sellers can follow.

 - Hire, train and coach the first sales team, using what you learned selling yourself.

 - Keep carrying your own deals while you lead.

 - Tell product and engineering what customers need in order to buy, backed by what you hear on calls.


WHY THIS ROLE

 - You build it your way. There’s no inherited process or structure. You design the sales function the way you think it should run.

 - You report to the Co-CEO. You have a direct say in the decisions that affect what you sell.

 - Product and engineering respond. When you can show that something will help you sell, it gets built.

 - The upside is uncapped. Commission has no ceiling, and with very strong results this can be the best-paid role at Novo.

 - The team is yours to build. As sales grows, you hire and lead the people who scale it.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


MUST HAVE

 - A record of beating quota on deals you found and closed yourself, cold outreach included.

 - Experience moving customers off a complicated financial product (banking, payments, payroll, lending or similar) and onto a competing one.

 - You can explain in plain words why one product beats another, to a business owner who is short on time.

 - AI is already part of how you work every day, and you can show us something you built with it for research, outreach or tracking.

 - You do well without structure: no playbook and no sales ops team to start.

 - Some experience coaching or leading other sellers, and the drive to build a team of your own.

 - You’re ready for a bigger job than the one you have now, and willing to bet on yourself to get it.

 - Able to work in person from our New York office.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Time on the sales team at a sales-led fintech.

 - Experience selling to business owners or finance leads.

 - You were an early sales hire somewhere, or built a new channel from scratch.

 - A network of business owners you can call in your first week.

 - You’ve moved fully into management and no longer sell yourself.

 - Your numbers have mostly come from inbound leads or cross-selling to existing customers.

 - You need an established process, tooling and a support team around you to do your best work.

ABOUT ONEBRIEF


Onebrief builds collaboration and AI-powered workflow software for military planning and operational coordination.

Military planning is complex by nature, requiring teams to coordinate information, people, and decisions across systems and locations. Onebrief brings planning, collaboration, simulation, and AI into one connected environment, helping teams test strategies, adapt to changing conditions, and make decisions with greater clarity when the stakes are real.

We are a distributed team of builders from military, operational, and technology backgrounds who care deeply about improving how important work gets done. Some team members work remotely, while others work directly alongside customers in operational environments around the world.

Founded in 2019, Onebrief is backed by leading investors including General Catalyst, Battery Ventures, Insight Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Human Capital. Valued at more than $2 billion, we continue to invest in product innovation, AI capabilities, and team growth.

Required: Top Secret clearance with eligibility for SCI

Remote with up to 50% travel




WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Department of War headquarters and operational formations need advanced capabilities to plan, visualize, analyze, and execute operations across echelons and joint environments. Atom Engine helps address these needs by enabling more dynamic, integrated, and technically sophisticated operational planning environments.

As a member of the AtomEngine Delivery Team at Onebrief, you will serve as a technical and operational partner to DoW customers, helping translate complex operational requirements into practical Atom Engine implementations. You will work directly with military planners, operational leaders, and technical stakeholders across the Department of War to integrate AtomEngine into existing planning environments, support exercises and high-priority operational events, and demonstrate its value across military formations.

This role combines operational expertise with technical aptitude and customer-facing delivery. You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Growth, and Mission Success to ensure successful customer implementations, identify opportunities to expand AtomEngine adoption, and translate field experience into repeatable delivery practices.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Lead Customer Implementations: Own the delivery and implementation of AtomEngine capabilities across assigned DoW customers. Translate operational requirements into implementation plans, coordinate technical resources, establish success criteria, and drive engagements from initial discovery through successful operational employment.

 - Translate Operational Requirements: Work directly with military headquarters, operational planners, and technical stakeholders to understand planning processes, modeling and simulation requirements, and operational challenges. Configure and tailor AtomEngine capabilities to support customer-specific workflows and mission requirements.

 - Support Exercises and Operational Events: Provide hands-on delivery support during command-post exercises, warfighter exercises, joint exercises, wargames, and other high-priority operational events. Ensure AtomEngine capabilities are properly integrated, configured, and employed to support customer objectives.

 - Drive Technical Integration: Partner with Product and Engineering to support customer integrations, troubleshoot technical challenges, and translate operational requirements into actionable technical solutions. Develop proficiency in AtomEngine architecture, capabilities, and technical implementation.

 - Partner Across Onebrief: Collaborate with Growth, Mission Success, Product, and Engineering to support demonstrations, pilots, new customer implementations, and expansion opportunities. Provide operational and technical expertise throughout the customer lifecycle.




MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience supporting operational planning, modeling and simulation, wargaming, or mission execution within a military headquarters, operational formation, or joint environment.

 - Working knowledge of military staff structures, operational planning processes, and coordination across headquarters and subordinate echelons.

 - Experience supporting the implementation, integration, or employment of complex technical systems within operational environments.

 - Ability to translate operational requirements into technical solutions and communicate effectively with both operational users and technical teams.

 - Demonstrated ability to independently manage complex customer engagements, technical implementations, exercises, or operational events involving multiple stakeholders.

 - Strong technical aptitude with the ability to learn complex software platforms, troubleshoot issues, and coordinate technical resolution.

 - Experience working across classified and unclassified environments and familiarity with DoW network environments.

 - Current Secret clearance with eligibility for TS, ability to access DoW facilities, and readiness to travel more than 50% of the time, both within the continental United States and internationally.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with military modeling and simulation (M&S), constructive simulation, wargaming, or operational analysis.

 - Experience supporting command-post exercises, Warfighter Exercises (WFX), joint exercises, or other large-scale operational events.

 - Experience integrating software platforms, data environments, simulation systems, or operational planning tools.

 - Familiarity with military mission command systems, operational architecture, and digital planning environments.

 - Experience delivering technical demonstrations, pilots, or solutions to senior military leaders and operational stakeholders.




INDICATORS OF SUCCESS

Customer requirements, technical environments, and operational priorities will evolve. Success in this role requires technical curiosity, operational credibility, adaptability, and the ability to deliver in dynamic customer environments.

The outcomes below illustrate what success typically looks like approximately six months into the role:

 - Successful Implementations: Assigned DoW customers have successfully implemented and begun employing AtomEngine capabilities against defined operational requirements and customer objectives.

 - Operational Integration: AtomEngine is effectively incorporated into customer planning environments, exercises, or operational workflows, with technical and operational challenges identified and addressed.

 - Customer Confidence: Military planners, technical stakeholders, and operational leaders understand AtomEngine’s capabilities and demonstrate confidence in its application to their mission requirements.

About the team

OpenAI’s Compute Strategy & Partnerships team develops the partnerships and transactions that support our long-term ambitions. Our work across industrial compute spans cloud infrastructure, semiconductors, datacenters, energy, and financing—bringing together the technology, capital, and commercial relationships needed to build and deploy AI at scale.

About the role

We’re looking for a Business Development professional to help originate, structure, negotiate, and execute complex strategic partnerships. You’ll work at the intersection of business strategy, finance, technology, and law, turning ambitious objectives into executable agreements and durable relationships.

This role offers direct commercial responsibility across the transaction lifecycle: identifying opportunities, developing a business case, shaping deal terms, aligning internal stakeholders, negotiating with counterparties, and supporting implementation. Many of these transactions involve novel structures, competing priorities, and decisions with significant long-term consequences.

We welcome candidates with backgrounds in business development, transactional law, finance, or investing. An experienced attorney interested in applying their deal skills to commercial strategy and execution could be an excellent fit.

Key Responsibilities

 - Develop strategic opportunities. Identify and evaluate partnerships across the compute and infrastructure ecosystem, informed by OpenAI’s priorities and an understanding of counterparties’ capabilities and incentives.

 - Structure and negotiate transactions. Develop commercial proposals and negotiate arrangements involving capacity, hardware supply, infrastructure development, financing, strategic investments, and joint ventures.

 - Evaluate economics and risk. Work with finance and technical partners to assess pricing, capital requirements, financing alternatives, delivery commitments, and downside scenarios.

 - Connect strategy to contract terms. Translate business objectives and technical requirements into practical terms that balance economics, flexibility, accountability, and execution certainty.

 - Drive decisions and execution. Coordinate engineering, infrastructure, finance, legal, and other stakeholders; resolve open issues; and maintain momentum through diligence, approvals, negotiation, and closing.

 - Build lasting partner relationships. Understand counterparties’ objectives, navigate difficult negotiations constructively, and develop solutions that support successful execution.

 - Communicate clearly with leadership. Distill complex issues into concise recommendations that explain the opportunity, key tradeoffs, and decisions required.

 - Support partnerships after signing. Help manage commercial commitments, address changing circumstances, and translate lessons from individual transactions into better structures and processes.

Qualifications

 - Eight or more years of relevant experience in business development, corporate development, transactional law, investment banking, investing, or a related field.

 - Meaningful experience structuring and negotiating complex transactions. Relevant backgrounds include M&A, structured finance, project finance, restructuring, commercial real estate, and strategic commercial agreements.

 - Strong commercial and financial judgment, including the ability to connect contractual provisions to economics, incentives, and practical business outcomes.

 - A record of taking ownership of demanding workstreams and advancing transactions involving multiple parties and competing priorities.

 - Excellent writing and communication skills, with the ability to explain complex matters clearly to executives, technical colleagues, and external partners.

 - Sound judgment about which issues matter most, when to escalate, and how to propose a workable path forward.

 - Intellectual curiosity, attention to detail, and the ability to learn unfamiliar technologies and industries quickly.

Preferred Skills

 - Juris Doctor (JD).

 - Experience with capital-intensive businesses, infrastructure, technology, energy, or semiconductor supply chains.

 - Experience developing novel transaction structures or negotiating agreements involving multiple interdependent parties.

 - Familiarity with financial models and evaluating investment or financing alternatives.

 - Prior AI or semiconductor experience is helpful, but strong transaction skills, commercial judgment, and a willingness to learn are central to success in this role.

ABOUT OPSMILL

OpsMill’s mission is to simplify infrastructure and network automation. We’re developing the building blocks that network, infrastructure and automation teams need to automate with confidence, starting with Infrahub, our foundation. Infrahub gives teams one place to define what their infrastructure and network design should be, generate the changes from it, and review and approve every change before it reaches the network. We also steward Nornir, one of the most widely used open source automation frameworks, and more building blocks are on the way.



THE ROLE

OpsMill's experts and community create more valuable content than any one writer could. As Technical Content Lead, you decide how that expertise becomes content that reaches the right people. You find the value in what engineers, product managers, leaders and community members create, edit it to a high standard, and turn it into content for every channel.

You work AI-first, as described below. You report to the Head of Marketing, work with our campaign manager on campaign strategy and on the content each campaign needs, and work closely with the Product team and our Developer Advocate.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the editorial strategy. Decide which stories OpsMill tells, within campaign priorities, and commission them from experts in OpsMill and the community.

 - Originate flagship content. Develop and own major pieces that only OpsMill could publish, such as research on the state of network automation or an interactive tool that helps engineers assess their automation stack.

 - Find the value in contributions. Run intake and a weekly review of content from across OpsMill and the community, and decide where each piece goes: a campaign, a programme, standard publishing, or back to the author with a suggestion.

 - Keep the quality high. Edit to our style guide and core messaging, own our voice and vocabulary, and help contributors improve without rewriting their work. Build and maintain OpsMill's writing skills for Claude, and help everyone who writes use them.

 - Partner on campaigns. With the campaign manager, shape campaign themes, briefs and the content calendar, then deliver the content each campaign, launch and event needs. Review results together and apply what you learn to the next campaign.

 - Get our content to the right people. Run our newsletters, The Current and Ottermatic, and OpsMill's social channels. Turn the most valuable pieces into posts, clips, newsletter items and Sales material. With our Developer Advocate, distribute content across LinkedIn, engineering communities such as Slack, Discord, Reddit and the Network Automation Forum, YouTube, our website, earned media, and search and AI assistants.

 - Build our people's external voices. Coach leaders and engineers on building their own presence, especially on LinkedIn, and build relationships with credible outside voices for joint posts, podcasts and community work.

 - Develop website content and SEO, working in a Git-based workflow with AI tools to publish and update webpages quickly.


HOW AI FITS INTO THIS ROLE

AI is a core way of working here. You build and use AI skills so that quality does not depend on you reviewing everything. AI drafts, repurposes and checks; you decide what matters, what it means and what gets published.

Most releases and contributions should move through simple, repeatable publishing routines that you design and largely automate. This keeps routine work fast and leaves your time for deciding where each piece goes, keeping quality high, setting the editorial strategy and building campaigns with the campaign manager.

In practice, you will run AI checks before anyone reviews a draft, ask AI about our code and documentation before asking a person, and keep improving the tools as they change.



HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED

 - Content drives results. Campaign content contributes to pipeline and adoption, measured with the campaign manager.

 - The right people see our work. Target audiences grow and engage with us across newsletters, social channels, search and AI assistants.

 - More voices, at a high standard. More people from across OpsMill and the community contribute, and what we publish meets our quality bar.

 - A consistent story. What we publish reflects our core messaging and covers the value pillars that matter most.

 - Routine publishing is automated. Most routine publishing runs through automated routines.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Fluency in the network automation and infrastructure world: you know the audiences, the conversations and what credibility looks like. You do not need to have been an engineer; our experts provide the technical depth.

 - Senior-level experience writing and editing for technical audiences, from network engineers and architects to the leaders who buy.

 - Strong editorial judgement: you can see what is valuable in a technical draft and improve it without losing the author's voice.

 - Hands-on AI experience: you have built prompts, agents or Claude skills, or you are eager to.

 - Comfort with Markdown, Git and pull requests, or the confidence to learn them quickly.

 - Experience running newsletters and social channels, and measuring their reach.

 - Working knowledge of SEO, and interest in how people now find companies through AI assistants.

 - Self-direction and clear written communication in a remote team, including working asynchronously across time zones, and the ability to earn the trust of experts and community members.

A note on background: there is no single path to this role. Backgrounds in content marketing at an infrastructure or developer tools company, technical writing, developer relations or community management are all relevant. We care more about ecosystem fluency, editorial judgement and an AI-first way of working than about a particular title or number of years.



NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with developer or open source communities

 - Experience with Git-based website tools

 - Video editing


WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT

 - Not a solo writer role. You will write, but much of your impact comes from what others create.

 - Not documentation. The Product team owns our docs.

 - Not campaign management. The campaign manager owns campaign plans, channels and reporting; you partner on the strategy and own the content.

 - Not design. Design support comes from our design partners and AI tools.

 - Not people management, to start. This is an individual contributor role.


LOCATION AND LOGISTICS

 - Location: remote, in Europe or the US. You must have the right to work in the country where you live.

 - Time zone: At least part of your working day overlaps with CET.

 - Travel: twice-yearly company offsites, potential to occasionally support marketing events.

 - Reports to: Head of Marketing.

ABOUT OPTERY

Optery is a privacy and data removal company. We find and remove our customers' personal information from data brokers and people-search sites, helping individuals and businesses reduce their exposure to scams, phishing, identity theft, harassment, and social engineering attacks. We serve both consumers (B2C subscriptions) and businesses (Optery for Business), protecting employees, executives, and their families.






ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll own Optery's affiliate program as a true performance channel, with real targets for partner-driven signups, revenue, and cost per acquisition. That means recruiting, activating, and growing the publishers, review sites, creators, and complementary products that introduce Optery to new audiences, then making sure every partner promotes us accurately and profitably.

This is a hands-on IC role. You'll run the program day to day, from outreach and commission design to tracking, payouts, and reporting, and work closely with our paid, lifecycle, and analytics teams so affiliate traffic converts and is measured correctly.






WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the affiliate program end to end: recruitment, onboarding, activation, optimization, and long-term relationship management

About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!





About the Team

The Guest Lifecycle & Loyalty (LILO) team is building what amounts to a world-class marketing agency for every restaurant on Owner — running automatically, at scale, with data-driven optimization that even a great agency could never match. We own the messaging, loyalty, and discounting systems that turn first-time visits into repeat guests and long-term regulars across email, SMS, and push — so restaurants can reliably grow repeat orders and lifetime value.



Our work sits at the intersection of product, data, personalization, and deliverability/reliability: we're scaling high-volume communications safely, improving attribution and experimentation rigor, and raising the quality and timeliness of the customer data that drives personalized outreach.



And we're at an inflection point. The foundations — reliable delivery, trustworthy attribution, modern campaign infrastructure — are established. That unlocks the exciting part: making marketing radically more personalized at both the restaurant and the guest level. Picture campaigns that generate themselves from real-world signals relevant to each location and its guests, creative that adapts to each restaurant's brand voice, and channel, item, and offer decisions optimized for each individual guest.


What you’ll work on

 - Own high-impact lifecycle and loyalty initiatives end-to-end from ambiguous goal → design → build → launch → iteration.

 - Build the next-generation segmentation and targeting platform allowing restaurants to reach their guests at the right time, with the right content and offers to drive engagement.

 - Build reliable messaging and data pipelines that power campaign execution (segmentation, scheduling, send-time optimization) across email/SMS/push at scale.

 - Ship AI-assisted capabilities that make lifecycle marketing more autonomous (e.g., smarter targeting, creative generation, and adaptive campaign optimization), with a bias toward production-ready systems.

Role Overview

The Voice AI team builds the AI that answers a restaurant's phone. When a guest calls, our agent picks up, takes a pickup order validated against the live menu, answers questions about hours and the restaurant, and sends the order straight to the kitchen, or hands the call to staff when a person is the better answer. We also build the tooling that lets restaurants go live without an engineer in every launch. If a restaurant joins Owner, our team is how its phone turns into orders and revenue instead of missed calls, and how guests get what they need while staff stay focused on service.

This is not a typical backend or ML role. Real-time voice is unforgiving: a guest on the line notices every extra half-second, every interruption handled badly, and every wrong modifier. The team works across streaming speech and LLM pipelines, telephony, turn-taking, and recovery when speech, model, or network services fail mid-call, and we measure quality on real calls, not demos. We're scaling well beyond our first live restaurants, and we automate everything we can, including with AI.

As the Engineering Manager, you'll lead this team and own its delivery and technical direction. You'll build a team that ships quickly with a high bar for quality, and you'll own hiring, coaching, career development, and performance management. Your scope spans the real-time voice experience, the systems that connect conversations to restaurant menus and ordering, and the tooling and engineering support that help restaurants launch and run reliably.

This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the United States or Canada. For San Francisco-based candidates: we have a new HQ in the Presidio for optional in-person collaboration.



Why we’re looking for you

Owner helps independent restaurants grow their business. The phone is still how a huge share of restaurant orders start, and too many of those calls go unanswered or get passed to a busy host. Our voice agents answer those calls, take orders, and help guests get what they need while restaurant staff focus on service. Real restaurants are already using it, and the product has proven the idea.

The next challenge is scale. Improving call quality, making onboarding self-serve, and keeping the agent reliable across more restaurants takes dedicated engineering leadership. Today, voice delivery, technical direction, and engineering support are spread across existing leads. We're hiring an Engineering Manager to own them, grow the team, and set the bar for how we build real-time voice AI at Owner.



Our Tech Stack

 - Voice & Real-time: LiveKit, Gemini, streaming STT/LLM/TTS pipelines, full call lifecycle persisted

 - Agents & AI: Vercel AI SDK, tool calling, agent loops, conversation state

 - Backend: Node.js, TypeScript, MongoDB, PostgreSQL

 - Frontend & Tooling: React, TypeScript, restaurant onboarding and launch tooling

 - Observability & Evals: Datadog, Braintrust, LangSmith, call replay and regression testing



The impact you'll have

 - Lead, hire, and grow the Voice AI team. Give direct feedback, support career growth, manage performance, and help engineers take ownership of systems and outcomes.

 - Set technical direction and turn product goals into focused plans. Partner with Product, Design, and Customer Success to prioritize work around restaurant needs and follow through from development to rollout.

 - Improve how we work. Spot repetitive tasks or recurring ticket causes and help test small, manager-approved improvements or automations, keeping validation and human approval in place.

ABOUT POINTFIVE

PointFive finds the cost buried inside enterprise infrastructure, from the cloud to coding agents. We pioneered DeepWaste across cloud and data platforms, and we are now doing the same for AI token spend with TokenShift. 
Fanatics, H&M, Hertz, Nubank, Citizens Bank and other Fortune 500 companies use PointFive to see and cut what their infrastructure and AI actually cost.

We have raised $96 million, most recently a $60 million Series B led by Accel https://www.pointfive.co/press/pointfive-raises-60m-series-b. Engineering sits in Tel Aviv and our go-to-market team is focused on North America. PointFive Labs, our research arm, publishes original work on how infrastructure and AI actually get paid for.

CRN named us one of the 10 hottest cloud computing startups of 2026 https://www.crn.com/news/cloud/2026/the-10-hottest-cloud-computing-startups-of-2026-so-far?page=9, Forbes Israel put us on its Next Billion Dollar Startups list https://forbes.co.il/rankings/2025nextbilliondollarstartups/, and Redpoint selected us for its InfraRed 100 https://www.pointfive.co/press/pointfive-infrared-100, its ranking of the private companies shaping the future of cloud infrastructure.


ABOUT THE ROLE

TokenShift is PointFive's newest product — an endpoint runtime for AI coding agents that gives organizations control, visibility, and efficiency across how agents execute commands and consume models.

As AI agents move from chat interfaces into developer machines, they increasingly need access to shells, filesystems, credentials, developer tools, and local compute. At the same time, enterprises are beginning to run models locally — on laptops, workstations, developer VMs, and managed endpoint fleets — across a wide variety of operating systems and hardware architectures.

This role exists to push that frontier forward.

You'll research how AI coding agents execute and isolate workloads, design secure sandboxing mechanisms, and build the infrastructure required to deploy and operate local models across heterogeneous endpoint environments. You'll work across macOS, Windows, Linux, WSL, developer containers, and other runtime environments, figuring out how to provide agents with powerful capabilities without giving them unrestricted access to the machine.

It's a rare opportunity to work at the intersection of operating systems, endpoint security, AI infrastructure, local inference, and developer tooling — in a product already running inside enterprise engineering environments.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Research AI coding agent runtimes — reverse-engineer how tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Codex, and emerging agents execute commands, access files, spawn processes, and interact with the operating system.

 - Design agent sandboxing architectures that safely constrain filesystem access, networking, process execution, credentials, and other sensitive endpoint capabilities.

 - Explore and implement OS-native isolation mechanisms across macOS, Windows, and Linux, including containers, namespaces, sandbox profiles, virtualization, restricted processes, and permission models.

 - Build endpoint "harnesses" that allow TokenShift to intercept, control, observe, and modify agent execution flows.

 - Design infrastructure for deploying and running local LLMs across heterogeneous endpoint fleets, accounting for operating system, CPU architecture, GPU availability, memory constraints, and hardware acceleration.

 - Evaluate local inference runtimes and model formats such as llama.cpp, MLX, ONNX Runtime, Ollama, vLLM-compatible runtimes, and emerging alternatives.

 - Develop mechanisms for model discovery, installation, versioning, updates, health monitoring, and lifecycle management across large numbers of developer machines.

 - Research hardware-aware model selection and routing — deciding which models can run effectively on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA GPUs, Windows workstations, Linux machines, CPU-only environments, and other endpoint configurations.

 - Build benchmarks that measure model latency, throughput, memory consumption, startup time, resource contention, and developer experience on real endpoint hardware.

 - Investigate security boundaries between local models, cloud-hosted models, agents, MCP servers, shells, and enterprise resources.

 - Collaborate with the core CLI and platform teams to take endpoint research from prototype through production.

 - Track the rapidly evolving AI agent, sandboxing, and local inference ecosystems and proactively identify technologies PointFive should support.
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


MUST-HAVE

 - Deep understanding of operating system fundamentals: processes, permissions, filesystems, IPC, networking, signals, and process trees.

 - Strong understanding of sandboxing and workload isolation concepts.

 - Hands-on systems experience across multiple operating systems, ideally including Linux, macOS, and Windows.

 - Experience building or debugging software that runs directly on developer endpoints, workstations, or servers.

 - Comfort operating close to the metal — binary behavior, system calls, OS APIs, environment variables, config files, process injection/interception, and runtime behavior.

 - Investigative, reverse-engineering mindset — you enjoy taking apart systems you didn't build and figuring out how they actually work.

 - Ability to move comfortably between research prototypes and production-quality systems code.


NICE TO HAVE

ABOUT PROXIMA

Proximity-based therapeutics represent one of the most promising frontiers in modern drug discovery with the potential to treat previously intractable diseases and target ‘undruggable’ proteins. Our technology combines proteome-scale structural data with state-of-the-art generative AI foundation models, and coupled with our talented team of scientists and engineers we are uniquely well-positioned to discover and develop a new class of medicines. Small businesses represent 99.9% of all companies, yet they're still forced to choose between clunky, outdated enterprise phone systems or their personal phones. This multi-billion dollar market has been overlooked for decades, left to cobble together solutions that slow them down instead of helping them grow.

 

Quo is changing that. We bring calls, texts, and customer information together into one easy-to-use, AI-powered platform. We're not just building a phone system. We're setting a new standard for how businesses connect with their customers.

 

Driven by our values, we move fast, build with determination, and obsess over delivering value to the businesses that have been underserved for far too long.

 

Today, Quo is trusted by more than 120,000 companies and rated #1 in customer satisfaction on G2. We're backed by Y Combinator, Tiger Global, Craft Ventures, Slow Ventures, and other top-tier investors. It's safe to say we're onto something big.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're growing Quo's mobile engineering team as we invest seriously in mobile for the first time in years. You'll join an established, close-knit team of mobile engineers shipping our iOS and Android apps, reporting into our mobile Engineering Manager. Mobile is becoming a first-class surface at Quo: we're moving the team closer to our core phone workstream (the calling experience itself — low latency, high call quality, no dropped connections) and making sure mobile keeps pace as we ship new AI, revenue management, and task management features across the product.

This isn't a platform-architecture role — the big technical direction decisions for mobile are already staffed and largely mapped out for the next 6-12 months. This is a hands-on, feature-delivery role: shipping real product improvements, working across shared Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) modules and native iOS/Android code, and partnering closely with product, design, and backend teams.

Some of the things you'll do:

 - Feature Development: Shipping new features and improving existing functionality across iOS and Android to keep mobile at or near parity with our web and desktop experience.

 - Shared Module Work: Building and adapting shared Kotlin Multiplatform modules so they integrate smoothly and feel native on both iOS and Android.

 - Cross-Platform Collaboration: Partnering with the rest of the mobile team (iOS and Android engineers) and our Mobile Foundations platform team to extend and integrate shared functionality.

 - Reliability & Quality: Helping raise the bar on our core phone experience on mobile — call quality, reliability, and performance are a real differentiator for Quo.

 - Cross-functional Delivery: Working closely with PMs, designers, and backend teams to ship customer-facing work, often jumping into an existing workstream and building context quickly.

Technical stack and tools:

 - Android is built in Kotlin, adapted to support Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) following clean architecture principles

 - iOS development is primarily in Swift with SwiftUI for new features, UIKit where necessary

 - Shared KMP modules include Apollo GraphQL, Ktor networking, OpenTelemetry, and feature-specific modules (conversations, contacts, alerts, etc.)

 - Persistence layers today are Room (Android/KMP) and Realm (iOS) — how these reconcile long-term is an active discussion, not yet locked

 - Dependency injection via kotlin-inject; testing with JUnit, Mockk, Turbine, and Maestro for cross-platform E2E

 - Collaboration tools: Linear, Slack, Notion, Figma


ABOUT YOU

 - High agency and ownership. Our mobile team is small (currently 3 product-focused engineers, growing significantly) and fully distributed across time zones. You're comfortable operating with fewer frameworks and more ambiguity than you'd find at a larger organization, and you go solve problems rather than waiting to be told to.

 - Strong communicator. You collaborate well cross-functionally with PMs, designers, backend engineers, and other mobile engineers, and you're comfortable working async across time zones.

 - Solid mobile engineering fundamentals, whether that's native iOS (Swift/SwiftUI), native Android (Kotlin), or cross-platform via KMP.

 - Low ego, direct communicator, ready to jump into a problem space, build context fast, and coordinate with the team as you go.

 - Comfortable with, or genuinely curious about, using AI tools to work faster and better.

Nice to have:

 - Direct production experience with Kotlin Multiplatform

 - Experience with GraphQL (Apollo Client) and modern async/networking patterns (Ktor)

 - Familiarity with mobile observability/telemetry (e.g., OpenTelemetry)

 - Experience with E2E testing (Maestro) and modern build tooling (Gradle, KSP)

 - Experience with feature flags and gradual rollouts

 - Knowledge of mobile performance optimization and memory management


COMPENSATION

The annual base salary range for this position is as follow, plus equity and benefits:

 - SF Bay Area, Los Angeles, Seattle, Portland, Boston, New York, and Washington, DC Metro: $170,000 - $200,000 USD

 - All other US Locations: $153,000 - $180,000 USD

 - Canada: $156,100 - $183,600 CAD

The ranges displayed reflect the target for new hire salaries, and within each range, individual pay is determined by your skills and experience, as well as relevant education. Your recruiter can share more and answer questions about the specific salary range during the hiring process.

Salary is just one component of Quo's total compensation package. Your total rewards package will include equity, extensive medical coverage, a monthly lifestyle stipend, and a flexible PTO policy.

ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.

We are looking for a Senior Supply Reliability Engineer who has built supplier programs that prevent problems rather than react to them. You will own the development, qualification, and long-term reliability of Radiant’s supply base — establishing the processes, standards, and supplier capabilities that ensure the right part arrives to the right standard, every time. While you’ll have the technical depth to handle complex non-conformances and corrective actions when they arise, your primary focus is upstream: strengthening supplier processes, closing capability gaps, and building a supply base that performs without constant intervention.
This is a builder role: the old house is being brought down, and a new foundation is being poured, but we still need to build the structure, apply the finishes, and pass final inspection. You’ll own what exists, upgrade aging systems, and create something the industry hasn’t seen before. You’ll mentor the engineers around you and help set technical standards, without formal people-management responsibilities, and grow into the team’s technical lead as it scales. We’re not here to maintain the status quo in nuclear quality; we’re here to raise the bar. SENIOR AI RESEARCH ENGINEER


WHY WOULD YOU LOVE THIS JOB?

We're hiring a Senior AI Research Engineer in Vancouver to work on how agents learn from experience. You'll focus on two Iris products: Agent Memory and Agent Playbooks. Together they decide what an agent keeps from its past work and how that changes what it does next.

Most of the hard problems here are still open. When should an agent write something down? What happens when a user's preferences change, or two facts conflict? How does an agent turn a task it solved once into a skill it can reuse, and how does that skill improve each time it runs? Which questions in a support log deserve to become an FAQ? And how do you do any of this without blowing up latency or token cost?

This is a research role, and a highly applied one. You'll spend your time reading the literature, forming hypotheses, and running experiments that tell us what actually works. The research counts when it makes Memory and Playbooks better for our customers.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to rethink how a construction project gets managed from inception to build.

Construction runs on handoffs: a project moves from a customer conversation to a scope, to an estimate, to a set of purchase orders, to a production schedule, with someone at every one of those boundaries re-entering what the last person already wrote down. The industry has long treated that as the cost of doing business, even though it is where schedules slip, where margin quietly disappears, and why almost nobody in this field can tell you what a building will cost until it is nearly built.

As a vertically integrated company, we are building the opposite of that, which means one authoritative representation of a project that everything downstream reads from, so that sales, estimating, procurement, and the factory all work off the same source of truth and a change in one place propagates. You will work closely with the design automation platform, which turns a building design into a manufacturable model and production plan, and the factory software team, to integrate real manufacturing data into our upstream models. This is part of the flywheel that will truly make construction faster and more predictable: real production data, cycle times, quantities, and labor we actually see on the floor, feeding back into how the next project is scoped, estimated, and bought, so that every building we deliver makes the next one more accurate to plan.

This is a hands-on role to deliver a software experience end-to-end, from understanding the problem statement to designing and deploying a solution. Your customers are the estimators, buyers, and project teams working alongside you, and you would spend real time with them, becoming an expert in their workflows. If you like taking an ambiguous, high-stakes part of a business and turning it into software that people run on, there is a lot of ground here.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own how a project flows through our systems, from the first customer conversation through to what the factory builds, including every handoff in between.

 - Design the underlying data model and system of record, so that each function works from one authoritative representation of a project rather than maintaining its own copy.

 - Build full-stack applications that turn manual, document-driven processes into software that operations teams run their day on.

 - Define the data contracts and interfaces between business functions, and keep them clear enough that engineers and agents can both work against them.

 - Apply AI to the manual and unstructured parts of the process, and build it to drive value in production not just demo well.

 - Partner with other software teams to close the loop between what we plan and what we actually produce, so that real operating data improves the next project.

 - Set the technical direction for how these systems evolve, including where we build and where we buy.

 - Partner directly with the teams who will use what you build to find the highest-leverage problem to solve next, then cut scope until it ships.

 - Mentor and grow other team members; this is an opportunity to shape the software engineering culture in a small, agile team.

Prior knowledge or experience in construction or manufacturing is not required. We'll get you up to speed.




MUST HAVE

 - 7+ years building production software.

 - Strong full-stack engineering, ideally in Python and Typescript, including automated testing, CI/CD, monitoring and alerting, and root cause analysis. You've owned systems end to end, from data model through interface.

And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.
