Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




JOB SUMMARY

Saronic is seeking a Technical Operations I to support mission operations across vessel operation, systems support, and mechanical maintenance for our autonomous platforms, including the 12 ft UUV, the 24 ft Corsair, and the 52 ft Mirage. This role is for someone with 2–4 years of experience, working under direct supervision while building proficiency through training and qualification progression.

In this role you will stand operational watches, assist with mission planning, pre- and post-mission checks, launch and recovery, and monitor autonomous vessels during live operations, exercises, and customer demonstrations. You will also execute scheduled maintenance on diesel engines, propulsion, electrical, and hull systems using established procedures and checklists. The ideal candidate is hands-on, eager to learn, and disciplined about safety, documentation, and escalating issues to senior staff. This role works a rotational schedule of 60 days on and 60 days off, built around three 60-day deployments per year.

Responsibilities

How you support the mission:

 - Stand operational watches and support vessel operation during live operations, exercises, and customer demonstrations.

 - Assist with mission planning and execute pre- and post-mission checks.

 - Support launch and recovery of autonomous vessels and monitor them during live operations.

 - Execute scheduled maintenance on diesel engines, propulsion, electrical, and hull systems using established procedures and checklists.

 - Support troubleshooting of mechanical, electrical, and autonomy/software issues by gathering data and escalating to senior staff.

 - Document maintenance actions, faults, and parts usage clearly and completely.

 - Follow operational safety requirements and established procedures on the water and in the shop.

How you support the team:

 - Build proficiency in vessel systems, mission tooling, operational safety, and maintenance documentation through training and qualification progression.

 - Take ownership of your personal qualification progress and training requirements.

 - Keep tools, spares, equipment, and workspaces organized and mission-ready.

 - Seek out additional mission prep or maintenance work when idle rather than waiting to be assigned.

 - Escalate uncertain technical issues to a supervisor and seek guidance before acting on unfamiliar systems.

Role Requirements

 - Completes mission, operational, and maintenance tasks accurately with guidance from supervisors.

 - Responds promptly to direction and completes assigned tasks within expected timeframes.

 - Takes responsibility for personal qualification progress and training requirements.

 - Follows established procedures and escalates uncertain technical issues to a supervisor.

 - Documents maintenance actions, faults, and parts usage clearly and completely.

 - Keeps tools, spares, equipment, and workspaces organized and mission-ready.

 - Recognizes the limits of their own experience and seeks guidance before acting on unfamiliar systems.

 - Rotational work schedule of 60 days on, 60 days off, with travel for three 60-day deployments per year, including OCONUS deployments.

 - Able to certify as "fit for work" by demonstrating ability to swim and tread water, lift up to 75 lbs., and spend extended time periods on the water.

Qualifications

 - 2–4 years of experience in vessel operation, marine or mechanical maintenance, or a related field.

 - Hands-on aptitude with diesel engines, propulsion, electrical, or hull systems; formal training or certification is a plus.

 - Familiarity with unmanned or autonomous systems, or defense technology programs, is a plus.

 - Prior military service, maritime academy, or commercial/recreational boating experience is a plus.

 - Comfort reading procedures and checklists and keeping accurate maintenance records.

 - Willingness to learn quickly and progress through Saronic's training and qualification path.

 - Active U.S. security clearance is required in advance of hire. TOP SECRET clearance with SCI eligibility is preferred, but not required in advance of hire.

Physical Demands

 - Ability to certify as “fit for work” by demonstrating ability to swim and tread water

 - Frequently and repetitively, lift, push and carry up to 75 lbs.

 - Will be exposed to marine environments, including sun, wind, rain, cold, and saltwater spray, often for extended periods

 - Must be able to operate in daylight, low-light, and night conditions using marine navigation systems and visual cues

 - Ability to perform physically demanding work for extended periods of time, up to 12 hours/day

 - This role may require to wear company provided PPE ie. Plate Carrier and Helmet no more than 25 lbs




BENEFITS

 - Medical Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Dental and Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium under the basic plan for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Time Off: Generous PTO and Holidays

 - Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents

 - Competitive Salary: Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

 - Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan with company match

 - Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

 - Life and Disability Insurance: Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

 - Pet Insurance: Discounted pet insurance options including 24/7 Telehealth helpline

 - Additional Perks: Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office

Saronic is growing fast, and our footprint has to keep pace: new waterfront sites, new countries, and new kinds of facilities that don't fit a standard office or industrial lease. The Expansion team needs someone who can take on whatever the next expansion problem is, figure out what it actually takes, and get it done.

The Expansion Specialist is a generalist operator who will work on strategic, ambiguous, and often one-of-a-kind projects that sit between real estate, operations, finance, legal, and government relations. One month that might be scouting a test site with open-water access and room to operate; the next it might be building the business case for a new regional hub, or working with local and state government on incentive packages.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Job Description:

We’re looking for a Staff Supplier Development Engineer to help lead the technical development, industrialization, and performance improvement of suppliers supporting munitions commodities. This role will assess supplier capabilities, manufacturing readiness, capacity, quality systems, and production processes while resolving complex technical, quality, and delivery issues. The engineer will work closely with Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Program teams to support supplier selection, new product introduction, qualification, and production ramp-up. The ideal candidate has strong aerospace manufacturing experience, can lead onsite supplier development and recovery efforts, and is able to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.

What you’ll do:

 - Lead the technical development and performance improvement of suppliers supporting critical munitions commodities.

 - Assess supplier technical capabilities, manufacturing processes, capacity, quality systems, tooling, workforce, and production readiness for prototype, development, qualification, and production programs.

 - Conduct supplier capability assessments, manufacturing readiness reviews, process audits, capacity analyses, and onsite technical evaluations.

 - Partner with Strategic Sourcing and Engineering to evaluate and select suppliers capable of meeting technical, quality, cost, schedule, and production-rate requirements.

 - Serve as the primary technical interface between suppliers and internal Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Program teams.

 - Lead supplier industrialization activities, including manufacturing planning, tooling readiness, process validation, capacity planning, qualification, and production ramp-up.

 - Review engineering drawings, specifications, GD&T, bills of material, special-process requirements, and statements of work to ensure suppliers fully understand technical and manufacturing requirements.

 - Drive design-for-manufacturability and design-for-assembly discussions between internal Engineering teams and suppliers to improve producibility, reduce cost, and shorten lead times.

 - Develop and manage supplier technical development plans, production readiness plans, capacity recovery plans, and corrective action plans.

 - Lead technical problem-solving activities involving manufacturing defects, dimensional nonconformances, process variation, tooling issues, material shortages, and production constraints.

 - Apply structured root-cause and corrective-action methods, including 8D, 5-Why, fishbone analysis, fault-tree analysis, and other appropriate problem-solving tools.

 - Review and approve supplier manufacturing documentation, including process flow diagrams, manufacturing plans, inspection plans, control plans, PFMEAs, work instructions, and qualification documentation.

 - Coordinate First Article Inspection activities in accordance with AS9102 and support the resolution of FAI discrepancies and manufacturing nonconformances.

 - Evaluate supplier production capacity using cycle times, yield, equipment availability, staffing, tooling, and material flow to confirm the ability to meet current and future demand.

 - Support suppliers through engineering changes, new product introductions, prototype builds, qualification activities, and production-rate increases.

 - Develop measurable improvement plans for suppliers experiencing delivery, quality, capacity, or technical performance issues.

 - Lead onsite supplier recovery efforts and regularly communicate progress, risks, and corrective actions to program and executive leadership.

 - Monitor supplier performance trends and use data to identify recurring issues, systemic risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

 - Support the development of alternate sources and risk-mitigation strategies for sole-source, long-lead, and flight-critical components.

 - Work with suppliers to implement lean manufacturing, process controls, mistake-proofing, yield improvement, cycle-time reduction, and production-flow improvements.

 - Ensure suppliers comply with applicable AS9100, AS9102, engineering, configuration-control, special-process, and customer requirements.

 - Provide technical guidance and mentorship to less-experienced Supplier Development, Supplier Quality, and Supply Chain team members.

 - Travel regularly to supplier locations to conduct assessments, resolve technical issues, and support production readiness and recovery activities.

Required qualifications:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field.

 - Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.

 - 7+ years of experience in supplier development, manufacturing engineering, supplier quality engineering, quality engineering, or a related technical role within aerospace, defense, or another highly regulated manufacturing environment.

 - Demonstrated experience developing suppliers and resolving complex manufacturing, quality, capacity, or delivery issues.

 - Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes such as CNC machining, structural fabrication, composite manufacturing, casting, forging, welding, heat treatment, plating, coating, finishing, and mechanical assembly.

 - Ability to read and interpret complex engineering drawings, GD&T, bills of material, material specifications, and manufacturing requirements.

 - Experience conducting manufacturing process audits, supplier capability assessments, capacity analyses, and production readiness reviews.

 - Experience with First Article Inspection requirements and AS9102 documentation.

 - Working knowledge of AS9100 quality management systems and aerospace supplier qualification requirements.

 - Experience applying structured root-cause analysis and corrective-action methodologies, including 8D, 5-Why, and fishbone analysis.

 - Knowledge of PFMEA, control plans, process capability, statistical process control, measurement systems, and inspection methods.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional technical teams and supplier improvement initiatives with limited oversight.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to make data-driven technical decisions.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical risks and recovery plans to suppliers and senior leadership.

 - Ability to manage multiple supplier development projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment.

 - Ability to travel to domestic and international supplier facilities as required.

Preferred qualifications:

 - Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance, depending on program requirements.

 - Experience supporting munitions, unmanned aircraft systems, advanced aerospace platforms, or defense programs.

 - Experience supporting the industrialization and production ramp-up of newly designed munitions components and systems.

 - Experience leading supplier recovery efforts for critical delivery, capacity, or quality issues.

 - Experience with lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, value-stream mapping, process capability analysis, and production-flow optimization.

 - Familiarity with FAR, DFARS, ITAR, export compliance, and government contracting requirements.

 - Experience working in both prototype and production environments with aggressive schedule and production-rate requirements.

 - ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt, APICS/ASCM certification, or another relevant professional certification.

Job Description

Help shape the future of physical AI in defense by building perception models for unmanned autonomous systems across aerial, maritime, land, and space domains.

We’re looking for a deeply technical engineer who can turn emerging research into reliable autonomous capabilities and shares our conviction that AI can protect service members and civilians. As a Staff Engineer on the Model Development team within Applied AI, you’ll drive the design, training, adaptation, and evaluation of multimodal deep-learning and foundation models for unmanned platforms.

You’ll take hands-on ownership of models that help autonomous systems understand their surroundings, recognize unfamiliar objects, and interpret scenes over time. Your work will account for limited compute, real-time latency, noisy sensors, and changing environments, with rigorous evaluation of how perception performance affects downstream reasoning and autonomy.

You’ll partner closely with teams in reasoning, MLOps, large-scale simulation, autonomy, and inference to deliver capabilities as part of Hivemind Enterprise.

What you’ll do

 - Design, implement, train, adapt, and evaluate perception models, with an emphasis on vision and multimodal foundation models for autonomous platforms.

 - Make and validate tradeoffs among vision foundation models, vision-language models (VLMs), specialized deep-learning models, and traditional computer vision methods.

 - Develop capabilities for detection, segmentation, tracking, and spatial and temporal scene understanding, including representations that support downstream reasoning and autonomy.

 - Build reproducible training and adaptation workflows using self-supervised learning, supervised fine-tuning, transfer learning, and distillation as appropriate.

 - Define data requirements, curation and annotation strategies, training objectives, and evaluation datasets that support meaningful comparisons across models and operating conditions.

 - Establish rigorous evaluations with real and simulated sensor data, measuring missed detections, false alarms, localization accuracy, temporal consistency, uncertainty, and generalization.

 - Incorporate latency, memory, compute, and power constraints into model architecture and training decisions in partnership with hardware, autonomy, and inference teams.

 - Diagnose model failures across environments and sensor conditions; use data mining, targeted curation, and training experiments to close performance gaps.

 - Deliver trained models, reproducible experiments, and clear performance evidence to partner teams, including documented limitations and interfaces for downstream use.

 - Set technical direction for perception model development, mentor engineers, and communicate experimental findings and tradeoffs to research, engineering, product, and organizational leadership.

Required Qualifications

 - BS/MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, and/or similar degree, or equivalent practical experience. Typically requires a minimum of 7 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 6 years and a Master’s degree; or 4 years with a PhD; or equivalent work experience.

 - Demonstrated track record of developing and deploying perception models in production, with substantial hands-on contributions to model design, training, and evaluation. In particular, a demonstrated track record of designing model architectures, training objectives, and loss functions.

 - Deep expertise in computer vision, modern deep learning, and vision or multimodal foundation models.

 - Strong command of training and adaptation approaches such as self-supervised learning, supervised fine-tuning, transfer learning, and distillation.

 - Experience defining datasets, training objectives, benchmarks, and reproducible experiments, with attention to data leakage, label quality, and distribution shift.

 - Fluency in traditional computer vision, geometry, and probabilistic methods, and an ability to combine them thoughtfully with learned models.

 - Strong Python programming skills and experience with training frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow.

 - Demonstrated depth in one or more perception areas, such as object detection, segmentation, tracking, 3D understanding, or video representation learning.

 - Experience working with real sensor data and evaluating model robustness across changes in viewpoint, lighting, weather, or sensor characteristics.

 - Familiarity with NVIDIA Jetson or other edge compute platforms and the tradeoffs involved in deploying perception models under resource constraints.

Preferred Qualifications

 - MS or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or similar degree.

 - Experience optimizing models for edge deployment using quantization, pruning, distillation, or hardware-aware architecture choices.

 - Experience with open-vocabulary perception, vision-language alignment, or adaptation to new domains with limited labeled data.

 - Experience with robotic or unmanned autonomous systems, including multimodal sensing (e.g. EO/IR, IMU, lidar, radar, etc.), geometric scene representations, sensor fusion, etc.

 - Experience with large-scale datasets, distributed training, and reproducible experimentation across multiple GPUs.

 - Familiarity with synthetic data, sensor simulation, and methods for measuring and reducing simulation-to-real gaps.

Senior QA Automation Engineer, Data Visualization and Platform
Mexico | Brazil | India | Costa Rica | Honduras | Peru

ABOUT SIFT

Sift is the data infrastructure platform for hardware engineering teams. Sift turns high-frequency telemetry into engineering insights for mission-critical systems. Teams use Sift to build and operate rockets, satellites, autonomous vehicles, energy systems, defense platforms, and more.

Founded by former SpaceX engineers who built the tools behind Dragon and Starlink, Sift is building the data infrastructure to herald the AI era for physical systems.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Engineers use our data exploration product to plot and investigate live and historical telemetry at high channel counts.

You will own test automation for that product and our GPU-accelerated charting engine, including the move from legacy charts to the new engine. Your job is to catch functional, performance and cross-browser regressions before customers do, and to turn today's partly manual performance testing into repeatable checks in CI. Later, you will also cover our core application layer: access control, navigation, search and the design system. You will report to the Head of Quality Engineering and work embedded with the data visualization team.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU'LL:

 - Own the end-to-end suite. Extend and maintain our Playwright tests for panels, annotations, data sources, sharing and plotting. Keep them fast, stable and trusted.

 - Make E2E a merge gate. Get smoke and critical-path tests running on every pull request, cut flakiness and define what blocks a release.

 - Expand browser coverage. Add Microsoft Edge and Firefox alongside Chrome, with a focus on Windows, where many of our customers work.

 - Automate performance testing. Turn our browser and hardware performance study into repeatable tests with frame-time and lag thresholds, driven by our telemetry simulator at realistic channel counts and data rates.

 - Introduce visual regression checks for charts and panels where they add signal without flakiness.

 - Prove the chart migrations. Build a parity suite that compares each legacy chart view with its new-engine version, across time-series, scatter, histogram, FFT and 3D charts.

 - Cover the core application layer. Map coverage gaps and build regression tests for access control (RBAC and ABAC), service accounts, folders, navigation, the home page, search and the design system.

 - Train and guide a QE in another time zone. Onboard a QE who runs regression overnight, and review their results.

 - Shape quality before code merges. Review test plans with engineers, push for unit test coverage in the web app, and test features before release.

 - Report on quality. Track pass rates, flaky tests and performance trends, and surface regressions quickly to the team.
   


REQUIRED SKILLS:

 - 5+ years in QA automation or SDET roles, with at least 2 years building UI test suites for complex web applications.

 - Strong Playwright and TypeScript skills. You have designed suites, not only written tests: fixtures, test data setup, tagging, parallelization and flake control.

 - Experience running E2E tests in CI, ideally GitHub Actions, as a blocking gate on pull requests.

 - Cross-browser testing experience across Chrome, Microsoft Edge and Firefox on Windows and macOS.

 - Hands-on frontend performance testing: browser DevTools, performance traces, frame rate and rendering analysis.

 - Comfort reading React code and writing unit tests with Vitest or Jest.

 - Experience testing authorization (RBAC and ABAC) and backend APIs, ideally Go services over gRPC.

 - Professional working proficiency in written and spoken English (CEFR B2 or above), used daily for design reviews, test plans, risk reports, working with and training teammates.

 - At least 4 hours a day of overlap with US Pacific time.
   


BONUS POINTS:

 - Testing data visualization, charting or WebGL and canvas-heavy applications.

 - Experience with real-time or streaming data products.

 - Visual regression testing with Playwright screenshots or a similar tool.

 - Python scripting for test data and load generation.

 - Familiarity with telemetry, time-series data or hardware test workflows.

 - Using AI agents to write and maintain tests.

 - Testing software that customers run in their own cloud or on-prem.
   


ENGINEERING AT SIFT:

 - E2E and browser: Playwright, TypeScript

 - Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vitest, Testing Library

 - Backend and API: Go, gRPC, PostgreSQL

 - Integrations and edge: Rust, Python, Protobuf

 - Test data and scripting: Python

 - Streaming: Kafka-compatible event streaming

 - CI: GitHub Actions
   


LOCATION:

This is a remote, full-time-equivalent independent contractor engagement for candidates based in Latin America or the Caribbean. You will work at least 4 hours a day overlapping with US Pacific time and collaborate closely with engineering teams in California.

Compensation range: $4,000 - $4,500 USD per month (Latin America and the Caribbean)

ABOUT THE ROLE



QRmaint is scaling internationally and right now, its international implementations are being run by the sales team. That pulls them away from selling and isn't an efficient way to do it. This role fixes that.

You'll take ownership of QRmaint's international implementations end to end: from kickoff, through system configuration, to go-live, and train each customer's team so they're self-sufficient once you're done. By taking these projects off the sales team's plate, you free them to focus on what they do best: selling.

This grows the implementation function to two people, split by market and language: you own the international customers, while implementations on the Polish market continue to be handled in parallel. It's a role for a hands-on operator from the maintenance or industrial world who's comfortable running a project independently and confident teaching customers how to get the most out of a new system.

Reporting: initially directly to QRmaint's board; in time, into the person responsible for post-sales (likely the Customer Success Manager, once that function expands to cover post-sales).




ABOUT THE PRODUCT



QRmaint is a mobile-first CMMS (Computerised Maintenance Management System) that helps maintenance teams keep machines, equipment, and facilities running at peak performance. Built around QR codes, it gives technicians instant access to asset history, work orders, and maintenance schedules from their phone — scan a code and report a failure, log work, or pull a machine's full history in seconds. The platform combines work order management, preventive maintenance, asset and spare-parts management, inspections, and downtime reporting on one central system, trusted across manufacturing, facility and real estate management, retail chains, schools, and field-service providers.

QRmaint recently joined SINGU – a leading provider of CAFM and facility-management software – as a new acquisition within the group. It continues as a distinct product in the SINGU portfolio, and this role is dedicated to it.




LOCATION

Hybrid – 2-3 times from office per week in Kraków or Warsaw.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING



 - Run implementations end to end for international customers – own the full journey from kickoff, through configuration, to go-live.

 - Handle the technical setup – configure QRmaint for each new customer, set up integrations, and migrate and clean up their data.

 - Train the customer's users – onboard the customer's team on the product so they can run it themselves once the implementation is done.

 - Manage the implementation as a project – own the schedule, milestones, and customer communication, and coordinate with the wider QRmaint team (sales, support, product).

 - Take international implementations off the sales team's plate – pick up the projects that sales runs today, and give them their selling time back.

 - Help out on support – part of your time goes to customer support requests. Implementations won't fill the role from day one, and support questions frequently turn into implementation work anyway, so the two go hand in hand.

 - Feed customer insight back to product – consult with the product team on the scope of new features and fixes, based on what you hear in your conversations with customers.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE TEAM

 - Maintenance, facilities, or industrial experience – this is the key requirement. You need to speak the same language as the people you'll work with on the customer side. That matters more than prior implementation experience: you understand how maintenance teams actually operate.

 - The product and the implementation process – learned on the job. Deep familiarity with QRmaint itself is not an entry requirement; we'll teach you the application and the process here.

 - The ability to run a project independently – manage a schedule, communicate with the customer, and work through obstacles without waiting for instructions.

 - Comfort in a training role – you'll be teaching the customer's users how to use the system, so you're at ease explaining and coaching.

 - English, Polish and German languages – all mandatory, at a level that lets you run implementations and training with international customers entirely on your own.




WHAT DOES SUCCESS LOOK LIKE

International implementations that used to sit with sales now run cleanly and independently through you – kickoff to go-live, on schedule, with customer teams that are confident and self-sufficient on the product afterwards. Sales freed to sell. And an implementation function that scales, split clearly by market and language, with international rollouts firmly in your hands.




TOOLS YOU'LL USE DAY TO DAY

HubSpot, Jira, and Fin.




WHY JOIN SINGU?

 - Competitive salary depending on your experience: between 11 000 - 15 000 PLN net on B2B or between 9000 – 12500 PLN gross CoE.

 - Real ownership of international implementations – you're not picking up a slice of someone else's process; you own these projects end to end, from kickoff to a customer running on their own.

 - A collaborative, no-micromanagement culture with honest, open feedback – we work as equals, share what didn't go well, and improve together.

 - Part of a fast-scaling international group – redefining how real estate and maintenance are managed across Europe, with QRmaint as a distinct, growing product within the portfolio.

Front-End Engineer II - Data Marketplace Experiences

ABOUT THINKING MACHINES

The mission of Thinking Machines is to build AI that extends human will and judgment. We are training frontier models with Inkling, developing Tinker to let people make models their own, and crafting interfaces that broaden human-AI communication. We believe the future worth building is human, and we're hiring people who want to build it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

In this role, you’ll work on discovering, understanding, and shaping model behaviors, both to improve Thinking Machines’ models and to contribute to the open scientific community. The ways AI systems behave – their character, their actions, and the ways they interact with people – will impact all of us. We believe a safe AI ecosystem requires the work of measuring and shaping that behavior to be decentralized, resilient to correlated failures, and open to public scrutiny.

Improving model behavior and alignment is a cross-cutting effort, involving both direct interventions across our training stack that are integrated into the model training loop as well as longer-horizon bets toward developing a systematic understanding of model behavior. As a model behavior researcher, you’ll help us build a scientific foundation for understanding and shaping model behaviors, apply it across our training stack, and publish our findings and tools in the open so that others can build on our work and customize the models we release.

Note: This is an "evergreen role" that we keep open on an on-going basis to express interest in this research area. We receive many applications, and there may not always be an immediate role that aligns perfectly with your experience and skills. Still, we encourage you to apply. We continuously review applications and reach out to applicants as new opportunities open. You are welcome to reapply if you get more experience, but please avoid applying more than once every 6 months. You may also find that we put up postings for singular roles for separate, project or team specific needs. In those cases, you're welcome to apply directly in addition to an evergreen role.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

We’re hiring for several roles that will work on projects ranging from discovery and measurement of unexpected model behaviors to model psychology and best practices for shaping model character. Example areas where you may contribute include but are not limited to:

 - Designing methods for surfacing unexpected model behaviors, categorizing them, and tracking them over time.

 - Developing and releasing open-source tools for simulating environments in a controlled setting and exploring how model behavior depends on input conditions.

 - Running controlled experiments to measure how much model character traits from early training are preserved through RLVR, and designing new interventions to make instilled traits more robust.

 - Studying the functional psychological behavior and emotional states of models, and exploring how these states relate to observed behaviors like reward hacking.

 - Measuring and shaping how models think of themselves and their situation, and exploring how this affects downstream generalization of model behaviors.

 - Developing best practices for writing model specs, instilling their values into models, and measuring whether we succeeded.

 - Building and publishing open evaluations of model behaviors and character traits to improve public knowledge and transparency about our evaluation processes.




SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum qualifications:

 - Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Physics, Mathematics, or a related discipline with strong theoretical and empirical grounding.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts in writing and collaborate effectively across research and engineering teams.

 - Relevant experience in designing evaluations, explaining model behavior, character training, model psychology, or a related area.

 - Strong interest in open science or in developing open tools for public understanding of AI systems.

Preferred qualifications — we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all preferred qualifications, but at least some:

 - Hands-on experience with large language models, including writing and iterating on prompts, evaluating outputs, and building an intuition for why a model behaves the way it does.

 - A portfolio of scientific publications, open-source libraries and tools, or other public-facing research or writing, especially in areas related to model behavior.

 - Familiarity with published literature on behavior generalization and on techniques for shaping model character (e.g. emergent misalignment, synthetic document finetuning, the persona selection hypothesis).

 - Experience generating synthetic data at scale for training or evaluation.

 - Experience with automated behavior classifiers and LLM judges.

 - A strong grasp of probability, statistics, and ML fundamentals, and strong research judgement, including the ability to design meaningful experiments and interpret the results.

 - PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Physics, Mathematics, or a related discipline with strong theoretical and empirical grounding; or, equivalent industry research experience.


LOGISTICS

 - Location: This role is based in San Francisco, California. 

 - Compensation: Depending on background, skills and experience, the expected annual salary range for this position is $400,000 - $500,000.

 - Visa sponsorship: We sponsor visas. While we can't guarantee success for every candidate or role, if you're the right fit, we're committed to working through the visa process together.

At least five years in hands-on application development and a recent record of shipping production software. You can contribute meaningfully to implementation while developing other engineers and managing the team.

 - Practical AI development experience: At least two years of substantial work applying AI to software development. You have implemented or improved agentic workflows, harnesses and evaluation or feedback loops, and can explain their effect on team effectiveness and software quality.

Video experience – ads or otherwise – is a plus.

 - Distributed-team leadership and communication: Experience leading engineers across countries and time zones. Strong written and spoken English, clear technical writing and effective collaboration with Product, Design, Data Science and commercial colleagues are essential.

About the Role:

We are looking for Engineers to drive webAI Public Sector initiatives focused on secure, resilient, and distributed data systems operating at the tactical edge.



In our world, network connectivity isn't guaranteed. Systems must thrive in Denied, Degraded, Intermittent, and Limited (DDIL) bandwidth environments. We are less concerned with formal peer-to-peer or blockchain dogmas and far more focused on practical, robust edge synchronization: building systems that can discover local nodes, store-and-forward critical data across ad-hoc transports (such as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth), and reconcile state once connectivity is restored.



Ultimately we’re looking for a Network Software Engineer that knows Rust and is comfortable with the complexities of working in DDIL environments, or a Network-adjacent Software Engineer that understands Peer-to-Peer systems very well. Along with Rust, this role will also interact with our other languages to integrate our distributed AI technology into complex, security sensitive networks used by government and enterprise customers. Those include Go, Swift, Python and C++, but you are not expected to have experience in these if applying for this role.



This is real world edge work built for dynamic field settings, rather than sterile cloud data centers or closed SCIF environments. You will design and implement advanced synchronization and networking systems that enable reliable AI operations across heterogeneous environments, from edge devices to cloud isolated government systems, while upholding the highest standards of performance, reliability, and data privacy.



The ideal candidate will be based in Austin, Texas or in the Washington, D.C./Northern Virginia area. On a case-by-case basis, we will consider fully remote candidates. Qualified candidates who are not based in Austin, Texas may be asked to travel to our Austin, Texas headquarters. This role will require up to 25% travel, including occasional on-site work at customer locations to support deployment, troubleshooting, and integration of our platform within enterprise environments.



Responsibilities:

 - Architect Resilient Transport & Sync Layers: Design and implement store-and-forward transport and data synchronization protocols tailored for low-bandwidth, high-latency, and DDIL field conditions.

 - Ad-Hoc Networking & Discovery: Implement local peer discovery and async I/O transports operating over heterogeneous physical links, including Wi-Fi, Bluetooth/BLE, LoRa and ad-hoc mesh networks.

 - Field Ready Systems Engineering: Apply delay tolerant networking (DTN) principles and local conflict-free data synchronization (e.g., CRDTs and content-addressable storage) to ensure mission critical applications function offline indefinitely.

 - Integration with Core Components: Integrate applied software components deployed at the edge with core infrastructure.

 - Performance & Resource Optimization: Employ memory management and debugging techniques against resource-constrained systems to improve our network.

 - Security & Cryptographic Primitives: Understand and implement various authorization and authentication security patterns, suitable for DDIL and contested environments.

 - Cross Functional Collaboration: Partner with hardware, mobile, and forward-deployed teams to validate end-to-end functionality under simulated and live field constraints.



Qualifications:

 - U.S. citizenship and an active U.S. Secret security clearance, or the ability to obtain one within six months of the start date.

 - 5-7+ years of software engineering experience building robust systems software or distributed networking services.

 - Core Languages: Strong proficiency in Rust or other systems level languages (Go, C, or C++).

 - Resilient Networking Expertise: Demonstrated experience with store-and-forward architectures, delay-tolerant networks (DTN), async I/O, or local device-to-device transport layers (e.g., BLE, TCP/IP, socket-level async networking).

 - Edge & Offline First Mindset: Practical experience solving synchronization challenges under intermittent, contested, or low-throughput network constraints (DDIL).



Preferred Skills:

 - Familiarity with hybrid mobile/cloud application architecture and state reconciliation.

 - Hands-on experience testing and evaluating wireless networking hardware and software in physical field or operational testing environments (outside of traditional lab/SCIF environments).

 - Background in content-addressable data structures, Merkle DAGs, or CRDTs.

The Opportunity: Senior Manager, Payroll Operations (Remote - USA / Canada) 

Payroll Operations is where production payroll gets made right: remittances, check issuing, one-off payments, reversals, and the cases that arrive when something needs fixing, across union and non-union productions. The Senior Manager owns how that work runs. You will lead a Team Lead and a group of specialists covering both union and non-union payroll, and own the team's partnership surface with Finance, Tax Operations, Union Payroll, and Product.

This is a genuine leadership role with direct accountability for operational outcomes and KPI performance. You will set clear owners, priorities, and standards, and inspect against them so issues surface early. You will also build a team that raises problems early, learns from errors without blame, and always weighs the impact on productions and the workers they employ.



What You'll Do: 

Run payroll operations

 - Own the case queue, routing, and prioritization across union and non-union work: set and hold the team's service levels, rebalance load across people, and know ticket volume and aging at any point

 - Keep remittances, check issuing, one-off payments, and reversals accurate and on time

 - Own payment controls, including approvals for one-off payments and corrections

 - Run a clear escalation model with defined owners and response standards, and set clear guardrails for what the team can decide versus bring up, so decisions happen at the right level without constant escalation

 - Own the escalation path for complex or novel operational problems, and coach the team through the hard calls rather than taking them over

 - Own how the team responds to internal requests, with clear ownership and response standards

Raise quality and report results

 - Build and run a quality program for the team's payroll work, and hold the team accountable for improving its own processes

 - Turn recurring errors into training, SOP, or process fixes, described by cause rather than by person

 - Hold the team to keep SOPs owned and current, turn recurring problems into reusable frameworks, and track the impact of errors and share themes with Finance and leadership

 - Set the team's targets and own its KPIs, including remittance accuracy and case service levels; read team-level metrics to coach and reprioritize, and escalate trends rather than incidents, with drivers and actions, to senior leaders

 - Track pending customer credits and report trends and drivers to leadership

Lead and develop the team

 - Manage a team lead and specialists: set targets, run regular 1:1s, coach against each person's metrics, hold career conversations, and build development plans

 - Build cross-training and coverage plans, define advancement paths, and onboard new hires effectively

 - Lead the team through change: explain the why, set expectations, and manage the productivity dip that follows new tools, processes, or structure

 - Build a candid, blameless culture where people raise problems early, and model it by naming your own misses

 - Set the tone that the team wins together: default to collaboration over territory, and break silos across the department

 - Make customer trade-offs explicit, weighing impact on productions and workers against cost and effort, and coach the team to make those trade-offs well on their own

Partner and plan

 - Build a quarterly plan for the team with Client Operations leadership, and surface capacity and staffing needs as volume grows

 - Partner with Finance, Tax Ops, Union Payroll, Success, Support, RevOps, and Enablement, with clear response expectations

 - Be a strong voice for operations in product priorities, so what ships reflects how the work really runs

AI is a requirement of this role

In this role, we expect you to lead on AI by example, not delegate it.

 - Build with AI yourself, including agents, workflows, and automations, so you can model good practice, judge what is worth building, and coach your team to build their own

 - Take an AI-first approach to how your team's work gets done, and use AI where your team can see it

 - Align with the team's AI champions on what gets built, so effort goes where it pays off

 - Protect your team's time to learn, including AI certification

 - Complete Wrapbook's AI certification for people leaders



What You'll Have: 

 - 5 to 8+ years in payroll operations, ideally including union payroll or an EOR or PEO environment

 - 3+ years of people management, ideally in a high-volume, fast-growing environment, with a record of developing people and growing them into stronger roles

 - Strong knowledge of payroll remittances, reversals, adjustments, and related compliance requirements

 - Experience managing a case queue and service-level metrics, and improving them through process changes

 - Experience setting team targets and SLAs and managing capacity across a team

 - Skill at using data to explain performance, diagnose root causes, and communicate clearly to senior leaders

 - A manager's mindset: set owners and standards, inspect against them, and escalate with substance

 - Experience leading a team through change, including explaining the why and managing the productivity dip

 - Hands-on AI experience, which is required for this role: you use it daily, have built agents or workflows yourself, and can coach a team to do the same

 - Candor: you raise problems early and treat errors as process gaps rather than personal failures

 - Sound judgment on customer trade-offs

 - Excellent written and verbal communication across Finance, Product, and operations teams

 - Nice to have: entertainment, media, or production payroll experience; union payroll rules and remittances; Salesforce case management and SLA configuration

AI Forward Deployed Engineer - Applied AI

ABOUT ZIP

Zip is the AI platform for enterprise procurement — built for humans and agents working together. By orchestrating procurement across teams, tools, and suppliers with the help of AI agents, companies can secure the resources they need to innovate faster than ever before.

The world’s most influential enterprises trust Zip, including T-Mobile, OpenAI, AMD, Mars, Dollar Tree, and more. Together they’ve saved over $8 billion and processed over $500 billion in spend. Zip’s team includes product leaders from Apple, Airbnb, and Meta, as well as former procurement leaders from United Health, Sanofi, MGM Resorts, Discover, and NASA.

Backed by Adams Street, Alkeon, BOND, CRV, DST, Tiger Global, and Y Combinator, Zip has raised $371 million, most recently at a $2.2 billion valuation and has been recognized by Forbes Fintech 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, Inc. Best in Business, and LinkedIn Top Startups.




YOUR ROLE

Be at the forefront of bringing agentic AI to procurement: automating intake, accelerating approvals, and transforming how enterprises manage spend and vendor decisions at scale.

As an AI FDE, you will partner closely with a small group of enterprise customers to design, build, and deliver high-quality AI agents and AI based products that automate complex procurement workflows. You'll make those first customers successful, turn what works into a repeatable playbook, and train our Solutions Consultants to scale the deployment to the rest of our customers.

This is a high-impact role ideal for someone who thrives at the intersection of customer engagement, solution design, and AI-driven product development.

This track is for procurement leaders who have led sourcing, contracting, intake and approvals, the work our agents automate, and want to shape how AI does it. You don't need to code. You'll work alongside our engineers to turn your procurement judgment into agents customers trust.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design & Build AI Agents & AI Based Products: Work hand-in-hand with customers to understand procurement workflows and develop AI agents & AI based products that solve their most critical pain points.

 - Plan and Scope Deployments: Set the scope, success criteria and project plan with the initial launch customers before kickoff, then own time to value through go-live.

 - Own the Quality Bar: Write the requirements, test cases and evals, and hold the line on accuracy and reliability before an agent goes live.

 - Feedback Loop into Product: Turn what you learn in the field into requirements and priorities for engineering and product, and guide the roadmap for our AI agent platform.

 - Build the Playbook: Turn what works into a repeatable playbook and train our Solutions Consultants to scale the deployment to more customers.

 - Bring the Procurement Lens: Turn sourcing, contracting and approval best practice into agent skills, policies and test cases, and judge agent output the way a procurement leader would.




YOU MAY BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE

 - Thrive in high intensity environments where change and iteration are key to success

 - 4+ years of in-house procurement experience, including implementing procurement tools (ie. Coupa, Ariba etc.)

 - Ownership of a spend portfolio, with software and services deals you negotiated end to end

 - A procurement workflow you designed in a P2P tool, such as intake or PR-to-PO

 - Daily use of AI tools in your own sourcing or contracting work

 - A track record of taking projects from plan to production: setting scope, success criteria and timelines, and delivering against them

 - Experience writing requirements and partnering with engineering and design to ship products

 - A track record of influencing cross-functional partners and leadership without direct authority

 - Ability to prioritize ruthlessly, even if it may disappoint customers or stakeholders

 - Strong written and verbal communication with internal and external stakeholders, including executives

 - Extreme attention to detail, with the ability to quickly grasp complex business processes and industry knowledge

 - Deep technical curiosity with ability to understand and influence how AI agents & AI based products are built, tested, and improved

 - Bonus: Experience with agent-building tools (e.g., n8n, Glean) or familiarity with MCP (Model Context Protocol)

 - Bonus: Contracting and risk reviews for AI vendors, or SOX and audit controls work

 - Bonus: Org-wide training you built and delivered

 - Bonus: Product management experience, or past roles where you worked with end customers to influence software development

 - Bonus: Python or SQL scripting experience

About the Role  Zeta is seeking a Senior Manager, Legal to join its legal team and serve as the day-to-day legal owner serving the in the global domain name and internet-infrastructure ecosystem with daily focus on the commercial, regulatory, corporate, and transactional needs of a business that runs critical internet infrastructure under a framework of global contracts and policies, chiefly those set by ICANN.This is not a narrow contracts role. It combines commercial contracting with registrars, resellers, and infrastructure providers; ICANN and registry regulatory work; product terms and privacy; sanctions and compliance; corporate and intercompany matters; and the occasional high-intensity strategic transaction. We are looking for a hands-on lawyer who can draft independently, structure unfamiliar business arrangements rather than relying only on templates, and become the trusted legal partner to senior business stakeholders. You will report into Zeta’s India legal leadership and work across time zones with business, technical, and operations teams and with external counsel in several jurisdictions. Expect the majority of your time to go to commercial, product, and regulatory contracting, with the ability to switch into complex transaction, corporate, or specialised ICANN work when projects arise.

Commercial, channel, and vendor contracting

  • Draft and negotiate reseller and partner agreements, commercial addenda, SLAs, and revenue-share arrangements, build templates for different partner models (low-touch, hybrid, API-led), and manage renewals, amendments, and novations.

  • Review the financial mechanics within these arrangements, including pricing, rebates, netting, and payment-agent structures.

  • Negotiate agreements with registry back-end operators, DNS and escrow providers, and region-specific registry service arrangements, including licences and filings in jurisdictions such as China.

  • Interpret and apply registry agreements, registry-registrar agreements, and registrar accreditation requirements, and handle ICANN compliance notices, approvals, and consent processes.

  • Support new gTLD applications and registry bids, and manage URS, UDRP, registrar transition, and DNS abuse matters when they become legal or compliance issues.

  • Run the legal workstream for the sale, acquisition, or transfer of a TLD or registry business, including the asset purchase agreement, transition arrangements, ICANN notices and consents, and the full closing set.

  • Manage closing conditions, transferred versus retained liabilities, and post-closing deliverables, coordinating buyer counsel, specialist external counsel, ICANN, and internal teams.

    • Product, privacy, compliance, and corporate

  • Draft and maintain terms of use and privacy policies, review signup and clickwrap flows, and advise on GDPR, DPDP Act, and e-evidence questions as applied to registration data.

  • Analyse sanctions exposure, including EU asset-freeze risk, advise on restructuring or exiting high-risk relationships, and build SOPs for law-enforcement and court-order requests.

  • Support entity restructurings, mergers, and overseas-investment structuring across the group, and draft intercompany service, cross-charge, financing, and netting arrangements.

  • Handle IP and brand licensing issues, select and manage external counsel, and maintain playbooks, templates, and compliance calendars.

    • You will also be part of Zeta’s wider legal team and will support other group matters as they arise, including commercial, technology and SaaS, privacy, corporate, and employment work, for which on the job support will be provided.

  • Cross-border transaction exposure across India, the Middle East, China, the US, the EU, and offshore holding jurisdictions.
